decisions.title: Bare command entry precedence
decisions.gist: Choose how bare Jet commands find a package entry.
decisions.lesson: An entry is what a command starts. A command function is a top-level `fn <cmd>`. A role home is a package-root file such as `@run.jet`. A typed `Output` names an executable and its entry function. A package default chooses one output. Bare commands need one order for these choices, while an explicit file names its source. This ballot compares shallow inference, canonical files, and written facts. `jet test` keeps the package `#Test` runner when no `fn test` exists, including a visible zero-test result.
decisions.explainer:
Inside a package, an explicit file wins. Otherwise a non-empty `@<cmd>.jet` wins, then one matching root file, then one matching `src/` file. If no command override exists, stock resolution checks manifest `defaults`, a sole compatible `Output`, `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, and `<package>.jet`. A second candidate produces a diagnostic instead of a filename guess. `--show-default` skips overrides and keeps today's `jet <cmd>: using stock default` line. At a workspace root, use `-p <member>` first; outside a package, bare commands keep the usage error.

These rules extend S12, D-CLI-BARE1, D-ROLEFILE1, D-CMDOVERRIDE1, D-VERDICT-678-1, and D-ILE1 in `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`. Current resolver evidence is `Source/main.rs:3891-3920`, `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs:935-1028,1085-1140`, and `tests/cli_parts/runtime.rs:598-670`.
decisions.story: Guido van Rossum opens a payments package after a teammate moves the API entry to `App.jet` and adds a smoke wrapper at `@run.jet`. He needs bare commands to keep the wrapper, while `--show-default`, explicit files, and a candidate error make each choice visible.

options.name: Shallow role and function order
options.detail: The resolver checks a non-empty package-root role home, then exactly one root file with the command function, then exactly one `src/` file. Root-level means directly inside the package; top-level means not nested inside another declaration. It never searches deeper, so a second candidate stops the command.
options.technical:
Inside a package, A covers bare `run`, `dev`, `debug`, `check`, `build`, `test`, and `doc`. An explicit file wins. A non-empty `@<cmd>.jet` with a matching top-level function is the command override; an empty home is inert.

Then scan direct root `.jet` files for exactly one top-level `fn <cmd>`, then direct `src/` files. If no override exists, keep today's stock sequence: `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, typed `Output` selection with `defaults`, then `<package>.jet`. Never scan deeper or generated files outside the source set.

`--show-default` ignores overrides and prints `jet <cmd>: using stock default`. At a workspace root, `-p <member>` selects the package; outside a package, bare use keeps the usage error. `jet test` stays on the package `#Test` sweep when no `fn test` exists, including zero found tests. A proposed `E_DUPMAIN` row names duplicate files; A adds no `jet fix` pin.

options.name: Canonical filenames and Outputs
options.detail: The resolver keeps today's named files and typed Outputs. It checks command overrides before stock resolution, then keeps `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, typed `Output` values, `defaults`, and `<package>.jet`. A lone arbitrary `App.jet` function is not a stock candidate, so explicit naming remains necessary. The manifest maps `defaults.run` to `outputs.app`, whose entry is `app_run`.
options.technical:
Inside a package, B covers bare `run`, `dev`, `debug`, `check`, `build`, `test`, and `doc`. Explicit files and the existing command-override scope stay ahead of stock resolution; an empty role home is inert. B adds no new any-name root or `src/` function scan.

Without an override, stock resolution keeps today's order: `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, typed `Output` selection with `defaults`, then `<package>.jet`. A generated file must stay outside the candidate source set or under a nested directory. No candidate-listing pin action is added.

`--show-default` ignores overrides and prints `jet <cmd>: using stock default`. At a workspace root, `-p <member>` selects the package; outside a package, bare use keeps the usage error. `jet test` keeps the package `#Test` sweep when no `fn test` exists, including zero found tests.

options.name: Override-safe facts, then shallow inference
options.detail: C keeps the shipped override order, adds one shallow inference path, and makes duplicate choices visible. It checks a non-empty role home, one matching root file, then one matching `src/` file; no deeper directory counts. If no override exists, written stock facts and canonical files choose the entry. A proposed `jet fix` writes one candidate into `package.jet`.
options.technical:
C preserves ratified D-CMDOVERRIDE1. For bare `run`, `dev`, `debug`, `check`, `build`, `test`, and `doc` inside a selected package, an explicit file wins. Next, a non-empty `@<cmd>.jet` home wins. Then exactly one direct root `.jet` file with top-level `fn <cmd>` wins. If root has no match, exactly one direct `src/` file with that function wins. An empty home is inert.

If no command override is selected, stock resolution checks `defaults.<cmd>`, a sole compatible `Output`, `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, then the retained `<package>.jet` fallback. An explicit `defaults.<cmd>` wins before a sole compatible `Output`. A generated file stays outside the candidate source set or under a nested directory. `--show-default` ignores overrides and prints exactly `jet <cmd>: using stock default`, as asserted in `tests/cli_parts/runtime.rs:598-670`.

At a workspace root, `-p <member>` selects the package; outside a package, bare use keeps the usage error. `jet test` uses the package `#Test` runner when no `fn test` exists, including a visible zero-test result. A proposed registered `E_DUPMAIN` lists candidate paths and offers proposed `jet fix --pin-entry <path>`, which writes the selected path to `package.jet`.

The proposed `entry_resolution: explicit` switch refuses root and `src/` function inference. It still permits explicit files, role homes, and stock manifest entries.

comparisons.note: Cargo uses an explicit `--bin` target, then `[package] default-run` for its stock binary choice. This resembles C's written stock facts without changing command overrides. The recorded limitation is that multiple binaries need an explicit target without `default-run`. Source: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-run.html#target-selection.
comparisons.code:
[package]
name = "ledger"
default-run = "cli"

[[bin]]
name = "cli"
path = "src/bin/cli.rs"

$ cargo run -- --port 8080

comparisons.note: Go's package entry is the current module or package, so `go run .` needs no source filename. The systems census records module-aware direct execution and no manifest-level entry inference. C keeps Go's short package command but adds checked shallow choices. Source: https://go.dev/cmd/go/#hdr-Run_specified_go_tool.
comparisons.code:
$ go mod init example.com/ledger
$ go run . --port 8080

comparisons.note: Zig puts the choice in a named build-graph step, so `zig build run` selects the declared run node. The systems report praises graph, cache, and generated help, but records package-level task parity as unmeasured. C keeps a direct command while making its source choice visible. Source: https://ziglang.org/learn/build-system/#run-step.

Deno keeps direct file execution explicit and uses `deno task` for named project commands. The census praises generated run, watch, and test commands, but task declarations add another project fact. C keeps written facts and adds checked shallow source inference. Source: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/init/.
comparisons.code:
$ deno init
$ deno run main.ts
$ deno task dev
$ deno test

comparisons.note: Bun runs a file directly with `bun run index.ts` or the naked `bun index.ts`; `bun run` prefers package scripts over source files. The census praises the no-config path, while the recorded caveat is that script names and files need explicit resolution rules. C writes those rules and lists conflicts. Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime.
comparisons.code:
$ bun run index.ts
$ bun index.ts
$ bun run dev

comparisons.note: Just runs the recipe marked `[default]`, or the first recipe when no mark exists, when called without a recipe. The systems census praises listing and static unknown or cycle checks, but records Just as a command runner rather than a full build graph. C uses a written stock choice without hiding source conflicts. Source: https://just.systems/man/en/.
comparisons.code:
[default]
check:
  cargo test

$ just
cargo test

recommendation.why: C keeps D-CMDOVERRIDE1 intact: explicit files and command overrides remain ahead of stock resolution. It adds one shallow root or `src/` inference path and makes ambiguity visible with candidate paths and a proposed pin action.

whyNot.reason: A keeps the shallow source rule, but it has no written manifest tier or proposed pin action. It is close to the split option, which C absorbs while retaining the ratified override order.
B preserves named files and Outputs, but a lone root `App.jet` function stays invisible to bare commands. It also offers no candidate list or proposed `jet fix` pin.

recommendation.tradeoff: C adds a root and `src/` scan, a registered ambiguity row, and a proposed package pin. The accepted cost is one more source rule, bounded at two shallow levels; no shipped override changes. Experts can refuse inference with proposed `entry_resolution: explicit`.

hybrid.synthesis: Keep D-CMDOVERRIDE1's order. After no command override, use manifest defaults or a sole compatible Output. Then check `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, and `<package>.jet`. Add shallow root and `src/` function checks, candidate listing, and a proposed pin. Keep `--show-default` exact, explicit files, `#Test`, and proposed `entry_resolution: explicit` as expert exits. The split precedence-and-diagnostic option is absorbed by C.

harvest.aspect: A supplies the shallow boundary and clear duplicate stop.
harvest.use: Keep root, `src/`, and the no-deeper boundary.

harvest.aspect: B supplies compatibility with named files and Outputs.
harvest.use: Keep stock `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, and the package fallback.

harvest.aspect: C keeps override order and adds inference plus repair.
harvest.use: Select C; it absorbs the split option's diagnostic-only design.

reviewPasses.base: The base draft defines three distinct entry mechanisms, gives each one a realistic package tree, and records the recommendation with its accepted tradeoff.
reviewPasses.boilOcean: The breadth pass tested Cargo `default-run`, Zig's named `run` step, Deno's `deno task`, Bun's file and script resolution, and Just's `[default]` recipe. These mechanisms strengthen the comparisons, but none replaces one checked Jet resolver.
reviewPasses.hybrid: The hybrid pass keeps A's shallow boundary and B's compatibility paths, then adds C's override-safe stock facts, candidate listing, pin action, and expert exits.
reviewPasses.cooperative: The cooperative pass gives A a deterministic role-home path, B a stable compatibility path, and C an explicit repair path without changing shipped override order. The recommendation still favors C because it joins written stock facts with safe inference and actionable ambiguity.
reviewPasses.beginner: Fresh agent: Rli5Entry. Skill: rli5. The beginner pass found unclear terms, an empty role home, a mismatched story, and incomplete pin and command examples. The ballot now defines each term, aligns the package story, shows stock versus selected output, and explains the pin path.
reviewPasses.adversarial: Author model family: OpenAI. Adversarial model family: Anthropic. The attack found a possible override-order regression, omitted `<package>.jet` and workspace boundaries, and an unlisted split option. The ballot now preserves the ratified order, names every stock and verb path, and absorbs the split option in C.

decisions.title: How Jet finds and runs named jobs
decisions.gist: Choose how a developer names and runs a Jet job.
decisions.lesson: A job is a Jet function marked with `#Job`. Its scope says: `.Dev` in development, `.Ship` in release, and `.Internal` from code or schedules only. Typed arguments check inputs such as `limit: Int`; a schedule tells `jet dev` when to start it, such as `every 5min`. Files are source, while a job causes effects. Every option has `jet jobs` text and `--json` listings. Tab suggests commands and files, and labels jobs for that entry. Every option has a Jobs panel. Only how a person selects and runs a job changes.
decisions.explainer: `#Job` registers a top-level function in one checked job list. `jet jobs` reads that list; words after `jet` form the project command space, where built-in names such as `run` and `test` already live. A collision is an error, not a choice.
decisions.story: Priya maintains a service project with `run.jet`, a `seed_data` job, and a `seed_data.jet` file used by a data tool. She runs `jet jobs`, chooses `seed_data`, and checks the job panel after `jet dev` starts it. She expects the listing to show its scope and schedule, and the panel to change `last run: never` to a time after the run. The choice matters when a file and job share a name, when a job is internal, and when two workspace members have `seed_data`.

options.name: Explicit entry and separator
options.detail: Keep the current explicit path. Priya names the entry, `--`, and the job every time. This makes file and job intent clear, but scripts repeat the entry path. The common listing and panel still inspect the scope, schedule, and last run.
options.technical: `jet run <entry> -- <name> [args]` remains the runner form. Words after `--` go to the selected job. The bare-entry form `jet run -- <name>` uses D-CLI-BARE1 before the existing job selection.

options.name: Project job as a top-level word
options.detail: Make each visible job a top-level `jet <job>` command. This is shortest for repeated calls, but job names compete with built-in and future commands. A file with the same name needs another form.
options.technical: A project job enters the same top-level command list as Jet's built-in verbs. Reserved or future collisions use E0928. `jet run <file>` stays the file escape.

options.name: Explicit job verb with a naming menu
options.detail: Put one chosen verb before every job name. The extra word shows intent and keeps files separate. The owner chooses exactly one of `job`, `do`, `x`, `call`, or `invoke`, then rejects the other four without aliases.
options.technical: After selection, only `jet <chosen> <name> [-- <args>]` invokes a job. The existing `jet run <entry> -- <name>` path remains. Choosing a word reopens D-JOB-NAME1, which currently reserves `job` as the one vocabulary word.

options.name: Bare job fallback after file lookup
options.detail: Try a file or directory first, then run a matching job from the resolved entry. This keeps `jet run` short, but a typo can run a different job, and a new `seed_data.jet` file can shadow an old job call. `.Internal` jobs need exclusion, and several workspace members need `-p`.
options.technical: The proposed order is file or directory, then a matching non-internal job, then a registered no-job diagnostic. A bare `seed_data` checks `seed_data` and `seed_data.jet` before the job. A file and job with one name report a collision before running. A workspace with several runnable members requires `-p <member>`. Bare job arguments have no required `--` boundary, so flag-shaped values can be consumed by Jet; the explicit form remains safe. Proposed `jobs: { resolve_names: false }` disables job lookup only; `jet run seed_data.jet` still runs the file.
options.code:
// proposed: bare fallback after file lookup.
#[Job(.Dev), Doc("Seed local data")] fn seed_data(limit: Int) {
    print(limit)
    print("seeded")
}

// proposed short call.
$ jet run seed_data 20
20
seeded

// proposed file and job collision.
$ jet run seed_data
Error: `seed_data` names both a file and a job.
Fix: jet run run.jet -- seed_data

// proposed scope guard: `.Internal` is not eligible for argv.
$ jet run inspect_job
Error [E1294]: No job named `inspect_job`
 Why: The first program subcommand must name a function marked `#Job`.
 Fix: Mark a function `#Job`, or check the subcommand spelling.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1294
declared jobs: greet, seed_data

// proposed workspace selection.
$ jet run -p api seed_data 20
20
seeded

// proposed refusal switch; file lookup remains enabled.
jobs: { resolve_names: false }
$ jet run seed_data
Error: bare job lookup is disabled.
Fix: jet run run.jet -- seed_data
$ jet run seed_data.jet
file

// A typo can still select a different visible job.
$ jet run deploy
# runs `deploy` if that job exists, with no warning

options.name: Explicit `jet jobs` runner
options.detail: Use `jet jobs` for both listing and running. Without a name it lists jobs; with a name it runs that job from the resolved entry, and `--` forwards job arguments. `jet run -- <name>` stays canonical, while `-p <member>` selects a workspace member.
options.technical: The proposed `<name>` positional on `jet jobs` resolves the entry with D-CLI-BARE1, then selects a non-internal job. `jet jobs -p <member> <name> -- <args>` selects a workspace member. A missing name uses registered E1294 and lists the entry's jobs. `.Internal` jobs remain callable from code and schedules, never from argv. Expert exits are `jet run --show-default` to see the entry, `jet run run.jet -- seed_data` to spell it, and proposed `jobs: { resolve_names: false }` to refuse bare lookup.
options.code:
// Real fixture listing.
$ scripts/agent/jet-env jet jobs
greet        [ship] Say hello from a shipped project job
seed_data    [dev] Seed local data (every 5min)
inspect_job  [internal]

// proposed: `<name>` is the new positional on `jet jobs`.
$ jet jobs seed_data
hello from job
seeded

// proposed: a wrong name uses registered E1294 and lists this entry's jobs.
$ jet jobs missing
Error [E1294]: No job named `missing`
 Why: The first program subcommand must name a function marked `#Job`.
 Fix: Mark a function `#Job`, or check the subcommand spelling.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1294
declared jobs: greet, seed_data

// proposed: `.Internal` remains unavailable from argv.
$ jet jobs inspect_job
Error [E1294]: No job named `inspect_job`
 Why: The first program subcommand must name a function marked `#Job`.
 Fix: Mark a function `#Job`, or check the subcommand spelling.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1294
declared jobs: greet, seed_data

comparisons.note: Npm uses `npm run <command> [-- <args>]` and lists scripts with bare `npm run`. This supports A and E's explicit separator, while string scripts lack Jet's typed job metadata. Source: `https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-run-script`.
comparisons.code:
"scripts": {"test": "tap test/*.js"}
$ npm run test -- --grep="pattern"

comparisons.note: Deno uses `deno task <name>` and supports task dependencies. This supports E's explicit name boundary, but string commands do not give Jet's checked function arguments. Source: `https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/task/`.
Just uses `just <recipe>` and offers shell completion. This supports B's short command and E's discovery boundary, but recipe bodies remain shell text. Source: `https://just.systems/man/en/`.
comparisons.code:
test-all:
    cc *.c -o main
    ./test --all
$ just test-all

comparisons.note: Cargo keeps options before `--` and forwards later words to the binary. This supports A and E's explicit forwarding boundary, while aliases do not describe typed jobs. Sources: `https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-run.html` and `https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#alias`.
comparisons.code:
[alias]
rr = "run --release"
$ cargo run --example exname -- --exoption exarg1

comparisons.note: Clap derives typed arguments, help, subcommands, and completion from one declaration. This supports E's one checked job list, but clap does not choose a project entry file. Source: `https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/`.

Typer runs `typer file.py run hello` and installs completion. This supports A's explicit file path and E's discoverability, but adds a wrapper word. Source: `https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/typer-command/`.

Mise warns that bare `mise <task>` can be shadowed by future commands. This is a cost of D's bare fallback, not support; E keeps job intent explicit. Source: `https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/running-tasks.html`.
comparisons.code:
[tasks."test:unit"]
run = "cargo test --lib"
$ mise run test:unit

recommendation.why: E gives Priya one explicit job command: `jet jobs seed_data`; `jet jobs` still lists the resolved entry's jobs. `jet run -- seed_data` and `jet run <entry> -- seed_data` keep the ratified paths, while a file name never becomes a job by accident. `-p <member>` resolves workspace choice, `.Internal` stays out of argv, and a wrong name gets a diagnostic with the list. The common panel also shows each job's scope, schedule, and last run.

whyNot.reason: A keeps intent explicit but repeats the entry path for every script. Its listings and panel can still help, so its loss is only the longer invocation.
B has the fewest keystrokes, but every project job enters the top-level command list. A job named `build`, `test`, or a future command must be rejected or renamed, and file paths need another form.

C makes intent explicit, but adds a command word before every job. Choosing `job` reopens D-JOB-NAME1, while `do`, `x`, `call`, and `invoke` create retired vocabulary; E uses the existing `jobs` word.

D is shorter than A, but a typo can run a different job, a new file can shadow an old call, and flag-shaped arguments lack a clear `--` boundary. Even with `.Internal` exclusion and `-p` checks, job intent stays implicit. A sigil-prefixed fallback is only a spelling variant of D, not a separate design, and still leaves a second lookup rule.

recommendation.tradeoff: E adds the word `jobs` to every shorthand run and gives `jet jobs` a new positional. It accepts two visible forms, `jet jobs <name>` and `jet run -- <name>`, to keep job intent explicit. A named job still needs a resolved entry, and the panel must show whether a job is runnable from argv.

hybrid.synthesis: E keeps A's explicit separator and escape path, B's short repeated call, C's visible job word, and D's bare-entry convenience without merging file and job namespaces. The common listing, completion, JSON, and panel surfaces stay independent of the invocation choice. `jet jobs <name>` becomes the safe shorthand; `jet run -- <name>` remains the canonical ratified form.

harvest.use: Keep `jet run <entry> -- <name>` for scripts and debugging.
Keep a short command, but put it under `jet jobs`, not at top level.
Use the existing `jobs` word instead of reopening verb names.
Keep `jet run -- <name>` for D-CLI-BARE1 plus the ratified separator.
Adopt `jet jobs <name> [-- <args>]` with `.Internal` and workspace guards.

reviewPasses.base: The base draft compared explicit entry paths, top-level jobs, an explicit verb, and a bare fallback.
reviewPasses.boilOcean: The breadth pass tested `mise` shadowing and `Typer` file execution, then kept their boundary and completion lessons without adding a wrapper or task graph.
reviewPasses.hybrid: The hybrid pass formed E from A's separator, B's short call, C's visible word, and D's bare-entry resolver.
reviewPasses.cooperative: The cooperative pass gave A-D complete invocation examples, reserved-name errors, workspace selection, and scope limits.
reviewPasses.beginner: Fresh agent: Rli5Jobs. Skill: rli5. The beginner pass defined job terms, aligned the `seed_data` and `seed_data.jet` story, and showed commands, outputs, errors, and panel state. It also added scope, argument, completion, and last-run explanations.
reviewPasses.adversarial: Author model family: OpenAI. Adversarial model family: Anthropic. The attack moved orthogonal surfaces into the lesson, exposed D's typo, shadowing, `.Internal`, workspace, and flag-boundary risks, and changed the recommendation to E. It verified the fixture's `jet run -- greet` result and kept the ratified `--` path explicit.

decisions.title: Devtools UX archetype
decisions.gist: Choose how Jet's developer tools show one running program in five places.
decisions.lesson: Jet can show a build error, old query data, a failing test, and reload time. The choice decides whether a person starts beside the app, on a selected item, or in a full workbench. A host means one place where the tools appear: browser overlay, workbench page, terminal, editor panel, or native app overlay. Each host must show the same selected item and point in history.
decisions.explainer: Every option shows the same Build, Routes, Queries, Tests, and Traces panels. A person can keep the last good page after a failed edit and open source-linked What, Why, and Fix text. One typed event stream is the shared record that carries panel facts between places. A panel is a focused view such as Build or Tests.
decisions.story: Maya edits examples/features/web/web_app.jet while a checkout page runs. She changes route "/" from home to save; save returns no page, so Jet reports E0421 and keeps the last good page. Then checkout data becomes old, and the save test fails. She first opens Build, then Queries, then Tests, and follows each result from the small status line to its details.

options.name: Dock
options.detail: A dock is a panel fixed beside the running app. Maya opens Build, selects E0421, and reads What, Why, and Fix in three steps. It is quick to scan, but it can cover app content and needs another action for history.
options.technical: The browser and native app use a resizable dock. The terminal renders two columns at 80×24, and the editor and workbench use the same panels. Selection means the current item; the time cursor means a chosen history point. Proposed native overlay toggle: F12 by default, with proposed project override `package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }`.
options.code:
docs/proposals/prototypes/devtools-ux/A-dock.html
// Open the prototype and choose Build.
$ jet dev examples/features/web/web_app.jet
[Dock beside app] Build  Routes  Queries  Mutations  Forms  Table  Store  Traces  Cost  Gates  Tests  Jobs
[Action] click Build -> click E0421 -> What / Why / Fix
[History] click History -> move the time cursor to 120ms.
[Terminal] jet dev; type Build, press Enter; type E0421, press Enter; type History, press Enter.
[Native overlay] proposed F12 toggles it; proposed override: package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }.
// The dock can cover checkout content while it stays open.

options.name: Lens
options.detail: A lens is a small inspector that opens from a visible item. Maya uses Alt+J, selects `/widget`, keeps its facts open, and moves the time cursor. It gives strong context, but Build or Tests needs the Ctrl+K palette or program map.
options.technical: The browser opens Lens with Alt+J and shows the selected route, query, table, or form beside its source line. Ctrl+K opens the keyboard palette for any panel. The terminal lists named items and opens facts with Enter. Proposed native overlay toggle: F12 by default, with proposed project override `package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }`.
options.code:
docs/proposals/prototypes/devtools-ux/B-lens.html
// Open the prototype and choose Inspect.
$ jet dev examples/features/web/web_app.jet
[Inspect Alt+J] select /widget -> route /widget -> source web_app.jet
[Lens] render mode: browser page; checkout query: stale; last change: 120ms
[Ctrl+K] type Build -> press Enter
[Build] E0421 What / Why / Fix; last-good page remains
[Runtime] Ctrl+K -> type Traces -> press Enter -> Jet frames only
[Terminal] jet dev; Ctrl+K; type Queries; press Enter; [ ] moves time; origin: terminal.
[Native overlay] proposed F12 toggles it; proposed override: package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }.

options.name: Workbench
options.detail: A workbench is a full window with a program tree, timeline, and inspector. The tree lists program items, the timeline orders changes, and the inspector shows selected details. It gives dense diagnosis, but every quick status check starts with a context switch.
options.technical: The browser offers three panes: tree, timeline, and inspector. The terminal shows the same data as a text waterfall, which is a time-ordered list. Compare selects current or previous history. The editor and native app open the same workbench. Proposed native overlay toggle: F12 by default, with proposed project override `package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }`.
options.code:
docs/proposals/prototypes/devtools-ux/C-workbench.html
// Open the prototype and choose Build failed.
$ jet dev examples/features/web/web_app.jet
[Action 1] open Workbench -> tree Build -> E0421
[Timeline] 120ms reload after failed save; stale checkout query; save test failed
[Inspector] What / Why / Fix -> source web_app.jet
[Compare] choose previous, then current; selected item remains
[Terminal] jet dev; Tab cycles panes; Ctrl+Shift+W focuses Workbench; type Build; press Enter.
[Native overlay] proposed F12 toggles it; proposed override: package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }.

options.name: Pill → Lens → Workbench
options.detail: A pill is a small status line, a lens is a contextual inspector, and a workbench is a full tree, timeline, and detail view. Maya reads the pill, selects a visible item in Lens, then opens Workbench when the problem needs room. If no item renders, the pill opens Build; if Lens cannot open, Ctrl+K opens the palette. Three controls need teaching, but each reaches the same selected item and history point.
options.technical:
One `jet.devtools.v1` stream is the shared record. One typed `core.ui` panel definition renders it. The pill is a compact status line, the lens is a contextual inspector, and the workbench is a full tree, timeline, and detail view.

Browser, terminal, editor webview, and native overlay render these views. Last input wins across hosts. Each host labels the current selection with its origin host. A host that joins later receives the current snapshot, selected item, history point, and origin.

The prototype terminal section labels `Terminal · jet dev` and `same panel definition, 80×24 minimum`. It shows a two-line status, `palette Ctrl+K`, named panels, `selection` plus `cursor`, and three columns: `PROGRAM TREE`, `TIMELINE + COMPARE`, and `INSPECTOR`. Its footer shows `[ ]`, `Alt+J`, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, and `?`.

Keyboard-only path: Alt+J opens Lens. Ctrl+K opens the palette; type Build or Tests, then press Enter. Ctrl+Shift+W opens Workbench. [ ] moves the history point, and Esc closes the view. Proposed native overlay toggle: F12 by default, with proposed project override `package.jet devtools: { overlay_key: "F10" }`.

The pill, Lens, Workbench, and stream are proposed ballot behavior, not runnable today. The current equivalent is `jet dev examples/features/web/web_app.jet`; `NO_COLOR=1` gives the current monochrome terminal.

Below 768px, the pill collapses to a dot with a count. Lens opens as a bottom sheet. The native overlay takes at most 1 ms of each frame. If it exceeds that budget, it degrades to the pill.

A plugin panel that throws or exceeds its render budget becomes an error card. The shared selection and history point stay unchanged. Release stripping is tracked by D-DX-PROD1; this ballot does not assert its release behavior.

recommendation.why: For a build error, Maya reads the pill, opens Build, and sees E0421 with What, Why, and Fix while the last-good page stays. For old query data, she opens Lens or Queries and sees the selected item and its source. For a failing test, she opens Tests from the pill or Ctrl+K and sees the failed test. D gives a status check, a contextual view, and a full history view without changing panel definitions.

whyNot.reason: A reaches E0421 in three actions, but its dock stays beside the app and can cover checkout content. D keeps the same panel list after the pill or Lens identifies the problem, and no panel stays open for a quick check.

B reaches visible `/widget` in two actions, but Build or Tests needs at least two more actions through Ctrl+K or the map. D keeps that same Lens path and adds pill status first. D does not remove B's extra navigation for items that are not visible.

C reaches E0421 after opening Workbench, selecting Build, and selecting E0421, at least three actions before details. D lets Maya read pill status in one glance, then use Lens or Workbench. D does not remove C's context switch for deep diagnosis.

recommendation.tradeoff: Selection means the item currently inspected. The time cursor means the chosen point in event history. Last input wins across hosts, and every host shows the origin host beside the current selection. D must teach three entry points and enforce these labels. That cost is accepted because a quick status check does not require the full view.

hybrid.synthesis: D deliberately composes A's compact status and panel list, B's rendered-item inspection, and C's tree, timeline, comparison, and source views. It is progressive disclosure, not a new panel mechanism: one stream and one selection model connect the three entry points.

harvest.use: Keep all first-party panels reachable after the pill or Lens identifies a problem.
Start from a visible route, query, form, table, or store, then keep its facts open.
Use the tree, timeline, two-history comparison, and source-linked inspector in Workbench.
Connect pill, Lens, Workbench, terminal, editor, and native views with one selection and history point.

decisions.title: Panel registration and typed devtools events
decisions.gist: Choose how a package makes a devtools screen available.
decisions.lesson: A function is code that receives inputs and returns output. A panel is a function that returns a typed screen tree (`core.ui`) for a devtools host. A marker is a special annotation that gives a declaration a defined compiler meaning. Registration tells Jet where the panel is. A host is a browser overlay, workbench, or terminal that renders the panel. A typed event is a named record with declared field types. This choice decides how packages register panels, pass render-time state, publish values, and remove code from release builds.
decisions.explainer:
Jet already reports live observations: a running program can say that an event happened without sending its fields. The panel API adds a typed function that each host can render.

`#Job` is a useful marker precedent for discovery and dispatch, not release erasure. `function_is_root` keeps job functions rooted so dispatch can call them. `JobScope::Dev` controls job visibility, not function deletion. `MaturityTag` has `Experimental`, `Tested`, and `Hardened`; it has no `.Dev` tag.

D proposes a new panel-specific release rule. The rule removes panel functions and their `devtools.publish` sites from release builds, including development-only event construction tied to those sites. This rule belongs to card #2424 and is not inherited from jobs.

Before each render, the host reduces authorized typed events into the panel's state parameter. State is package-scoped, so a third-party panel cannot read another package's values without an explicit policy grant.
decisions.story: Sarah Drasner reviews a payments package that must show invoice `inv-904`, 3499 cents, and card suffix `4242` in the browser, workbench, and terminal without exposing the full card number.
decisions.detail: Owner tradeoff pass, 2026-09-02: option D now makes each publish site name the state field it feeds and checks the state struct against those sites. It types secrets `#Credential` with a scrubbed path and makes third-party denial the default, so nothing recurring is left for authors or projects.

options.name: Function marker
options.detail: A puts one marker on the exported panel function. The compiler lists it before startup, and each host calls it with typed `PaymentsState` before every render. A needs its own panel release rule, but it has no written value gate, so an unlabelled card number reaches every attached host. The naming menu offers `#Devtools`, `#Panel`, `#Inspect`, `#DevPanel`, and `#Tool`; `#DevPanel` says both purpose and scope.
options.technical:
`#DevPanel` is proposed as a function marker. The host builds `PaymentsState` from authorized events and passes it to `payments_panel(state)` before each render. A's publish call forwards an unlabelled value, so the full card number appears in the event stream.

A panel-specific release rule removes the panel function and its publish sites from release builds. This is new work for the card, not behavior inherited from `#Job`. The existing `#Job` path keeps jobs rooted for dispatch. `#DebugOnly` is the existing statement-scoped release precedent, so it does not supply this function-level panel rule. Keep the marker's formatter output and editor grammar stable.

options.name: Startup registration call
options.detail: B calls a registration function from `fn run` or an initializer. The running process adds the function to a registry, and the host passes typed `PaymentsState` before each render. `jet inspect devtools` is empty before startup, and duplicate names produce the chosen E1410 startup error. The call path has no written value gate, so a full card number can be sent.
options.technical:
`devtools.panel("Payments", payments.payments_panel)` is proposed. The registry rejects a second `Payments` name with E1410; this is an explicit B rule, not an inherent property of runtime registration. The host reduces package-authorized events into `PaymentsState` and calls the typed function before each render.

Release mode removes the registration, panel function, and publish sites through a proposed devtools release condition. Development with no attached host uses a no-allocation publish fast path. No source-level value gate exists.

options.name: Manifest panel list
options.detail: C lists fully qualified exported panel paths in `package.jet`. The build validates each path before startup, and every host passes typed `PaymentsState` before each render. A moved function produces E1411, but the manifest adds a second source of truth and has no written value gate, so its publish call forwards the full card number.
options.technical:
`devtools.panels: [payments::payments_panel]` is proposed package metadata. The manifest is authoritative for names and exports, while the host reduces package-authorized events into `PaymentsState` and calls the typed function before each render.

A stale path fails with E1411 before startup. Release compilation omits listed panel functions and their publish sites. The manifest does not place a value decision beside the publish expression, so the full card number is sent.

options.name: Marker plus typed observation
options.detail:
D marks the exported panel function and sends typed events through `jet.devtools.v1`. The host reduces authorized events into `PaymentsState` before each render. The `value:` label is the written gate for sending a selected field. A new panel release rule removes panel functions from release builds; card #2424 adds it, not `#Job`. State is package-scoped, so third-party panels cannot read other package values by default. Beginners write one marker; experts inspect panels, spell the gate, or deny third-party loading.

The panel's state struct is the only list an author writes. Each publish site names the state field it feeds, as `field: .settled_cents`. The compiler checks the struct against those sites: a field no site feeds is a warning naming the field, whose fix text shows the site to write. State fields carry defaults or `?T`, so a panel renders before its first publication. Secret input is typed `#Credential`, so an unscrubbed value is refused at the publish sink; `.suffix(4)` behind `#Scrub(Credential)` is the shown path.

Third-party panels are denied by default, so no policy exists to maintain until a project allows one. Publish sites in release follow D-DX-PROD1's build fact; panel functions and their only-callers compile out.
options.technical:
`#DevPanel`, `core.devtools`, `jet.devtools.v1`, `devtools.publish`, and `value:` are proposed syntax. The host calls `payments_panel(state: PaymentsState)` after reducing only the panel package's authorized event families. A panel receives no ambient global event store.

`#Job` is not a release-stripping precedent. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Job.rs:162-292` handles dispatch visibility, while `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs:1413-1463` emits job wrappers. `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Liveness.rs:392-412` roots jobs, so job functions are force-kept alive for dispatch. `JobScope::Dev` controls visibility, not function deletion. `crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/items.rs:928-943` lists `Experimental`, `Tested`, and `Hardened`; it has no `.Dev` maturity tag. `#DebugOnly` is statement-scoped and cannot replace this function rule.

Release rule: `#DevPanel` functions, every function whose only callers are panels, and argument construction used only there compile out of release. A release caller of a panel is a compile error naming the caller. `devtools.publish` sites keep or lose their value slot per D-DX-PROD1's `inspect` fact. Development with no attached host uses a no-allocation no-op path. Add the gate to the single fact registry with existing `tighten` or `loosen` words; do not invent a third law word.

Publication contract: `devtools.publish(family, event, value: expr, field: .name)`, where the field belongs to a panel state struct in the same package. The missing-field warning and E1404 are registered by card #2424 with What, Why, Fix, and snapshots. Any edit that creates a publication carries the `needs-review` class and is emitted only when one site and one in-scope scrubbed expression are unambiguous. The publish sink joins the taint lattice: `#Credential` and `#PII` values are E0722 there.

`jet inspect devtools` is a proposed inspect action listing panels and published fields per package. `policy: .{ devtools: .{ third_party: .Deny } }` is a proposed extension of D-TEAMPOLICY1's field set with default `.Deny`. An allow-list of package identities is the only written form, and a denied load is a registered diagnostic. Expert exits: see the catalog, spell the gate, refuse with project policy.

Telescope uses a `Watcher` with `register($app)` and option filtering; this supports B's registration hook, while local-only defaults and pruning limit stored data. Source: `~/.cache/jet-luna/dx/backend/report.md`.

Actuator endpoints require deliberate exposure, and sensitive values sanitize to `******`; this supports C's declared catalog, but an endpoint is not a shared panel tree. Source: `~/.cache/jet-luna/dx/backend/report.md`.

recommendation.why: D combines static discovery, typed observation, package-scoped render state, and a written value gate in one path. Its release rule removes panel functions, while every host renders the same `core.ui` tree. Beginners use one marker and a typed state parameter; experts can inspect the catalog, spell selected publication, or deny third-party loading. Each publish site names the state field it feeds, so the compiler can check the author's list and the taint law can refuse a secret.

whyNot.reason: A discovers panels before startup, but its publish call forwards a full card number without a written gate. It leaves the event contract and sensitive-value decision outside the registration mechanism. A trait or protocol contract would only type-check this same marker path, so it is a refinement of A rather than a distinct registration choice.

B selects panels per run and rejects duplicate names with E1410, but `jet inspect devtools` cannot list a panel before startup. Its runtime call also leaves release handling and sensitive-value decisions to runtime policy.

C validates a qualified manifest path and reports E1411 when it becomes stale, but the manifest adds a second source of truth. It cannot place the sensitive-value decision beside the publishing expression.

recommendation.tradeoff: Authors mark one function and, at each publish site, name the value and the state field it feeds; the compiler checks that list against the struct. No recurring policy work remains, because third-party loading is denied until a project allows it.

hybrid.synthesis: The final design uses marker discovery, typed observation, package-scoped state, field-labelled selected-value publication checked against the state struct, a taint-checked publish sink, and a panel-specific release rule. Hosts render one `core.ui` tree, while project policy denies third-party loading by default without creating another registration path.

harvest.use: Keep marker-based listing and add the panel-specific release rule.
Show the same panel after startup without using a runtime registry.
Keep project policy at the package boundary and validate panel ownership.
Make typed events, package-scoped state, and explicit selected publication canonical.

The second found a warning naming a fed field, no mapping from `cents` to `settled_cents`, and a credential only commented; D now labels sites, defaults the state, and tags the credential.
