decisions.detail:
This revision answers the owner's four identical questions. It replaces unsafe blanket regeneration in A and B with real preservation-respecting alternatives. D remains the recommendation and retains its existing letter.

The existing package version names the package release. D-CONF-NAME1 ratifies that bare field. A second root version would be ambiguous, so the proposed file format uses format: { version: 1 }. This adds format.version; it does not add a second root-level version or rename the package release.

Current source inventory is below. These are code observations, not newly executed workloads.

package.jet: Package/Convert.rs:115-147 writes bare name, version, and jet. Manifest.rs:324-359 distinguishes channel dispatch from range constraints. Package/mod.rs:2566-2570 parses version, jet, and edition. There is no file-format version.

Lock.rs:2301-2329 rejects non-current versions; load at 3076 suppresses failures while load_strict at 3084 preserves them. Every consumer must use the same disposition and must not reinterpret unsupported data as a missing lock.

jet-store/src/lib.rs:387-452 defines and checks jet.build-record/v1. The store retains content-addressed blobs and classifies build-record failures at 747-764. Source/ReceiptStore.rs:41-55 defines current receipt and link formats. ReceiptStore.rs:445-447 currently turns a decoding failure into no reusable receipt.

Source/ReceiptSections.rs:1-51 already provides bounded canonical JSON, type and schema digests, parent binding, and append-only section records. D-RECORD1=B already owns the one record index and requires ratified artifact bytes to remain unchanged. Reuse both instead of adding another envelope or history index.

Consumers include PackageFacts and Manifest, package templates and public projections, Lock readers, JetPin, BrowserLock, NixIdentity, provider admission, driver Loader, build-record publication and inspection, ReceiptStore, ReceiptSections, RecordIndex, and CmdStatus. All must agree on missing, unsupported, and corrupt.

Existing marker-only fixtures under tests/fixtures/build-metadata-compat do not prove safe conversion. Keep originals and add complete fact-bearing fixtures for each admitted format. Never invent a historical layout from its version number alone.

options.name: Use the exact writer toolchain
options.detail: Read each file with its trusted original Jet toolchain, rather than converting it. Original readers preserve original meanings. Historical toolchains must remain available.
options.technical: A amends the current minor-channel dispatch contract to require exact tool identity for metadata reads. Retain every original file. Never infer authority by re-solving dependencies. Tools must already be trusted and installed; an unavailable reader is an explicit unsupported result, not permission to download or execute a binary. Status remains non-producing. This option avoids historical conversion but ties access to the availability and security of old toolchains.
gains: Original readers preserve original meanings.

losses.loss: Historical toolchains must remain available.

options.name: Explicit version with manual conversion
options.detail: Separate file and package versions; stop whenever the file needs conversion. File version stays independent of compiler release. Supported upgrades still interrupt a build.
options.technical: B uses the same format.version spelling and preservation checks as D. It performs no automatic conversion, even when a supported, complete, identity-preserving conversion is available. Existing update tooling may invoke that conversion explicitly. It may not resolve new dependencies as a format repair. Newer files are read-only or refused. Evidence conversions produce linked projections, never replacement observations.
gains: File version stays independent of compiler release.

losses.loss: Supported upgrades still interrupt a build.

options.name: Defer compatibility policy
options.detail: Keep the greenfield contract and require matching files until a later owner decision. No historical-format promise is made. Cross-version usability remains unspecified.
options.technical: C makes no new historical-reading promise and adds no format field. The existing safety and evidence laws still apply. A mismatch must not permit an old writer to replace newer authority, silently rebuild a trust graph, or erase old evidence. Those protections are not optional compatibility features. A later ballot remains necessary before declaring a compatibility guarantee.
gains: No historical-format promise is made.

losses.loss: Cross-version usability remains unspecified.

options.name: One preservation rule with automatic safe reads
options.detail: Use version in a clear scope, preserve originals, and automatically read supported older data without changing its meaning. Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable. Shared readable views preserve their linked original evidence. Newer files remain untouched. Unknown required meanings still need a newer reader.
options.technical:
One rule governs every read: preserve recorded facts and interpret only supported meaning. Never write to an input whose declared format version is newer than this reader supports. One shared typed result distinguishes missing, supported, unsupported-version, unsupported-required-meaning, and corrupt. Unsupported-version retains the found marker and admitted support set, including whether the input is older or newer. 

An unsupported version lies outside the admitted support set, whether older or newer. Report unsupported-version and write nothing to that input. Required source or lock input stops the build. Immutable evidence stays visible but cannot justify success or reuse. A disposable cache entry becomes a miss; rebuild under the current reader's cache identity, not over the unsupported input.

Unsupported-required-meaning means an admitted format contains an unknown required field or section. The same role outcomes apply. Only explicitly optional data may remain opaque. Corruption remains a distinct error, not missing data or unsupported-version.

Missing required source stops the operation. An absent optional package file remains valid for a supported standalone invocation. A missing required lock stops locked, frozen, or offline operation. In ordinary online mode, only the existing authorized lock-producing workflow may create it. 

Missing evidence is unavailable without rerunning its producer. Missing cache data is a miss. Callers supply requiredness; a decode failure never becomes missing. Existing file owners supply their format and role. Keep the current wire decoders; do not build a plugin framework or require every artifact to share one serialization.

The old phrase four rules referred to source files, locks, caches, and evidence. These are different permissions under one preservation rule, not four user workflows. Source files are never rewritten merely because a reader is newer. Locks may change encoding only when exact facts are preserved. Only cache entries may be discarded and rebuilt. Evidence is append-only.

Use format: { version: 1 } only in package.jet and its existing inline package carrier. Locks, caches, receipts, and build records retain their existing format markers. The field is version, not manifest. Its scope distinguishes it from the existing top-level version: "1.4.2" package release. D-BUILDCOMPAT1 narrowly amends D-CONF-NAME1's Package block vocabulary to add format. Bare name and package-release version remain unchanged. 

New templates write the format line. The leading format declaration is a literal positive integer, checked by the common package parser before interpreting the rest of the document. No second general parser is introduced. Unsupported file versions and duplicate declarations fail before dependency resolution.

Unknown package keys remain errors. Only explicitly designated non-semantic metadata may be retained without interpretation. A new key that affects builds, security, or claims requires a recognized file version; it is never ignored under an older version. Existing jet constraints and edition meanings do not become format identifiers.

For an admitted older lock, decode and validate all exact revisions, hashes, signatures, provenance, toolchain identities, browser identities, and Nix closure facts. A read-only in-memory view must preserve their meaning. Under locked, frozen, or offline operation, preserve original bytes and do not fetch, re-resolve, or write a converted lock. 

The initial support set contains no older lock encoding. Version-1 locks from older Jet releases already use the current encoding and remain readable without replacement. Format-only replacement is dormant until an owner amendment admits an evidenced older encoding.

If such an encoding is admitted, a normal unlocked, online build atomically replaces it with the current encoding. It first verifies that every exact fact is preserved, the original digest is unchanged, and the original content-addressed copy is retained. Missing authority stops conversion; only a separately requested dependency update may resolve new choices.

Reuse D-RECORD1's existing index and identity. Reuse ReceiptSections' bounded canonical typed-section decoder for new cross-version evidence views, including build-node sections. Keep existing ratified parent bytes and current wire readers unchanged. A supported old record may gain a separate view bound to the original digest, schema identity, tool identity, and claim inputs. It never becomes a new observation. 

Unknown sections remain available as opaque bytes with their original identity. An unknown section name, type, or schema is required by default and excludes the record from current success or reuse claims. Optionality must be part of an authenticated contract the reader already recognizes, never an unchecked claim inside unknown bytes.

The current ReceiptSections envelope has no optionality flag. This proposal does not add one or reinterpret existing bytes. Until an owner registers a recognized non-semantic optional section contract, no unknown section qualifies as optional. Unsupported and corrupt records remain visible with distinct reasons. Status never reruns a producer or launches an old toolchain.

This removes a new versioned decoder for each evidence class. Existing receipt and build-record decoders still own their current wire formats; a shared read policy is not a claim that their bytes are identical. The shared typed-section path handles added evidence fields without multiplying historical codecs. Use current canonical JSON and hashes; add no external serialization dependency.

Initial package support is today's unmarked form plus the new scoped format version 1. Lock support is version 1. Cache and build-record support remain jet.store.v1 and jet.build-record/v1. Receipts retain jet-receipt-v2, jet-receipt-links-v1, and the current ReceiptSections format. Lock version 0 is unsupported: the marker-only fixture does not establish a historical layout. 

This support set is a proposed compatibility exception for owner approval. Keep any historical importer separate from the current reader. Remove each importer after all retained first-party authority has migrated and each retained evidence object has a verified linked view or an explicit unsupported record. Original evidence remains immutable. Adding another historical importer or changing the support set requires an owner amendment. This is not an indefinite promise to read arbitrary future formats.

Design-away work: replace manifest with scoped version; replace blanket regeneration with one preservation check; reuse the existing index and typed sections; keep locked reads byte-preserving. Automatic compatibility cannot invent an unknown required meaning. Declared optional data may remain opaque; anything that affects authority or a success claim must be understood.
gains: Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable.
Shared readable views preserve their linked original evidence.
Newer files remain untouched.

losses.loss: Unknown required meanings still need a newer reader.

comparisons.note: Protocol Buffers separates compatible additions from meaning-changing edits and forbids reusing field numbers. This informs extension policy; Jet would not add Protobuf.

recommendation.why: D removes repeated compatibility policy and reuses the existing index linking views to original evidence. Safe older files work automatically without changing dependencies or rewriting observations.
gains: No silent downgrade or dependency change.
One rule for all readers.

losses.loss: Unknown required meanings need a newer reader.
losses.mitigation: Guessing an unknown meaning could change dependencies, security, or a recorded result.

whyNot.reason: A depends on old toolchains remaining available and safe.
B interrupts builds even when a lossless conversion is already known.
C leaves ordinary cross-version use unresolved.

recommendation.tradeoff: Original bytes stay preserved. Locked or offline reads leave the lock path unchanged; an admitted old encoding may be replaced only under the defined normal-build rule.

The revision defines all three scopes, the exact conversion trigger, each role outcome, and release matching; the preservation rule and locked/offline behavior remain explicit.
reviewPasses.adversarial: Author model family: OpenAI GPT. Adversarial model family: OpenAI GPT. Fresh agent: CompatAdversarial. decisions.checkInstructions:
After ratification, build a fresh compiler and exercise complete old, current, newer, and corrupt fixtures for package.jet source, locks, disposable caches, receipts, and build records. Check exact lock facts and unchanged bytes under locked and offline reads. Check that an input newer than the reader supports cannot be overwritten. Verify cache-only rebuild, visible unsupported evidence, preserved original digests, and no producer execution by status. 

Cover concurrent conversion and interrupted atomic publication. Register and snapshot each new diagnostic. Verify package templates, inline carriers, public projections, and grammar output use the same format.version meaning. Do not treat marker-only fixtures as conversion proof.

Locks preserve exact dependency choices. Receipts record past runs. Only caches may be recreated without losing authoritative facts. One preservation rule governs them all.

decisions.title: One place to inspect compiler decisions
decisions.gist: Where should Jet explain decisions that change generated code or execution?
decisions.lesson: A compiler can approve a speedup, refuse it, or move running code to a slower engine. This view shows the decision and its recorded evidence: a static safety check, a projected speed estimate, or an observed execution. It does not run another analysis. Expired or stale evidence is unavailable, not guessed.
decisions.story: Nora sees a loop run slowly. She needs to know whether it was vectorized, copied its input, or took a slower execution path, without reading generated backend code.
decisions.inWild:
clang -O2 -Rpass=loop-vectorize -Rpass-missed=loop-vectorize \
  -Rpass-analysis=loop-vectorize auto_loop.c
# https://releases.llvm.org/17.0.1/docs/Remarks.html
decisions.detail:
This ballot explicitly amends D-CLI-ONE1 with the selected route: inspect decisions, inspect why, or emit --explain. D-ACCEL1, D-RECORD1, and D-EXPLANATION-RECORD1 remain binding. #2945 supplies one checked record; CLI, editor, and lints render its projections.

All options also propose the same output policy: one concise tool-diagnostic notice per affected function and run for an actual slower-engine transition. Existing quiet suppresses notices, not evidence. Program output and exit status do not change. No new verbosity flag is proposed.

Every row identifies its producer and evidence method. Source, configuration/profile, target, compiler build, generated artifact, and run identity determine validity. D-RECORD1 retention is bounded; eviction makes an old explanation unavailable. No stored row is a new proof or speed claim.

options.name: jet inspect decisions
options.detail: Put all checked compiler decisions in one source-facing inspection view.
options.technical:
Add decisions to the existing inspect-plane registry and reuse its file, package, live, and replay scopes. Show source span, decision kind, disposition, checked reason, target/profile identity, and build/run identity. Concise text is the default; existing JSON controls expose details.

Use #2945's ratified explanation record and the existing record index. Optimizer, copy-insertion, vector-proof, and tier producers write the authoritative rows. Rendering never repeats the proof, executes a producer, or invents a missing premise. Existing accel remains its specialized projection of the same rows.

Distinguish accepted, rejected, not attempted, unsupported, stale, redacted, unavailable, and exhausted-budget records. Legality proof and measured profitability remain separate. Record source-edit fixes once; #2884 and #2896 lints consume them rather than rerunning analysis.

Ordinary jet run writes one deterministic concise notice per deopted function to the existing compiler-diagnostic channel, never program stdout. Program-produced stdout/stderr bytes and return values are unchanged. Repeated transitions retain full records but do not flood the default terminal. Existing quiet behavior suppresses tool notices without discarding their records.

All UI and CLI projections share record identities, redaction, retention bounds, and source links. Changes to source, configuration/profile, target, compiler implementation/build, generated artifact, or run identity invalidate the view. Every row records its producing component and evidence method: static legality, projected/measured profitability, or observed execution. No new inspect dev plane or generic second explanation database is added.
options.code:
# Proposed A
jet inspect decisions examples/features/lowlevel/simd_auto_loop.jet --json
jet run examples/features/operators/spaceship.jet
# One concise notice per function taking a slower path.
# --json exposes the structured records; no new verbosity flag.
gains: One discoverable command.
CLI, editor, and lint views share records.
Slower execution paths are visible by default.

losses.loss: Retained decision records use bounded storage.

options.name: jet inspect why
options.detail: Use a general explanation query for the same decision records.
options.technical: Use the same checked records, redaction, scopes, and default notices as A. The only mechanism difference is the public query name and its broader discovery contract. It must not invent a second proof or merge unrelated explanations without typed categories. The ambiguity is a real naming tradeoff, not an excuse to duplicate implementation.
options.code:
# Proposed B
jet inspect why examples/features/lowlevel/simd_auto_loop.jet --json
# Same records and default slower-path notices as A.
gains: One broad question-style command.

losses.loss: The name does not distinguish compiler decisions from other explanations.

options.name: Annotate generated output
options.detail: Attach decision records to emitted artifacts and keep inspection artifact-led.
options.technical: Annotate emitted artifacts using the same checked record IDs. Retain source/build/target identity and default deopt notices; a new renderer cannot silently drop the existing card's visibility requirement. This is viable for artifact-oriented users, but live and editor views must resolve through the matching artifact. It does not replace source-level explanations with generated Rust errors.
options.code:
# Proposed C
jet emit --explain examples/features/lowlevel/simd_auto_loop.jet
# Source links and checked reasons annotate the emitted artifact.
gains: Decisions appear beside their generated instructions.

losses.loss: Source and live explanations require finding the matching artifact.

comparisons.note: Optimization remarks separate accepted, missed, and analysis records and can be serialized. They do not define Jet authority, privacy, or execution semantics.
comparisons.code: https://releases.llvm.org/17.0.1/docs/Remarks.html

recommendation.why: A gives beginners one obvious view while experts retain structured records and precise scope. Every consumer reads the same checked reason.
gains: No duplicated decision or lint analysis.

losses.loss: One new route; stored evidence uses space and older explanations expire.
losses.mitigation: Past explanations require retained evidence. The existing bounded record budget makes the cost and expiry explicit.

whyNot.reason: Why is broader than the concrete compiler-decision question.
An artifact-first workflow makes ordinary source and live questions harder to answer.

recommendation.tradeoff: Keep explanations bounded and source-linked; never fabricate an answer after evidence expires.

decisions.title: Which C++ adoption boundary should Jet complete?
decisions.gist: Which C++ adoption boundary should Jet complete?
decisions.lesson: Jet already has a ratified C++ binder; the original omission report is stale. A keeps that boundary and completes its adoption evidence. B and C explicitly amend the binding mechanism. None grants arbitrary C++ compatibility, a second runtime, or weaker safety.

story.current: Today D-FFI-CPP1=A generates cpp.counter. The reduced program constructs a Counter at 10, adds 5, prints 15, and closes its owner. This preparation did not rerun it. A keeps the binder and completes adoption proof; B replaces lowering; C replaces automatic discovery with explicit selection.
story.problem: Jet already has a ratified C++ binder; the original omission report is stale. A keeps that boundary and completes its adoption evidence. B and C explicitly amend the binding mechanism. None grants arbitrary C++ compatibility, a second runtime, or weaker safety.

inWild.note: C++ runs the same constructor, add, print, and destructor lifetime. The research comparison also uses the primary Swift, Carbon, CXX, and Zig documentation.

decisions.detail:
A retains the existing generated-C-shim architecture. B explicitly replaces it with direct C++ lowering. C retains its lowerer but replaces header discovery with explicit selection.

All options complete D-FFI-CPP1’s fallible-call contract. Cleanup consumes the owner on success or failure and returns success or CppError. It never panics internally or retries destruction. The public CppError enum also gains Callback for a stopped callback. These changes are explicit owner choices in this ballot.

The richer workload is shared by A/B/C. Integer overload prints 15; floating overload prints 17; the named operator prints 20. Callback prints 42; rejected callback yields Jet fallback -1; template prints 42. An intentional C++ throw returns CppError and yields fallback -1. Then consuming close runs once. The reduced snippet is not the full acceptance workload.

The handle is an opaque #SingleUse owner. ^counter moves ownership into close_counter and prevents later use. C++ exceptions never unwind into Jet. Cleanup remains consumed if destruction reports an exception; no dangling owner is returned.

For this admitted callback shape, require synchronous, non-retaining, same-thread, noncapturing, effect-free calls. Prove those facts through the existing checked foreign contract or vetted provider; a pointer signature alone is insufficient. The trampoline contains every Jet stop/unwind. It records Callback and returns through C++ normally; the enclosing call returns CppError.Callback. Unknown retention, threads, context, or asynchronous behavior refuses. Other ratified callback protocols are not silently revoked or bypassed.

Pinned headers and native tools are shared binding-production requirements. Consumers may reuse admitted, hash-verified package/cache outputs through existing authority. A cache hit needs no local Clang regeneration. A miss needs the declared inputs/tools; it cannot download undeclared artifacts. No new bundle format or trust mechanism is added.

Require actual AOT, Cranelift/default-run, interpreter, and web execution. Missing tools or providers fail proof rather than skip. Materialize tests/fixtures/cpp_counter/main.jet from the original workload. The current native fixture and a JIT foreign-boundary refusal are not parity evidence.

Research Swift, Carbon, CXX, and Zig from their primary documentation. Compare ownership, exception fences, imported shapes, ABI/tool ownership, and refusals. #2933 and #2958 keep broader adoption ownership. No new runtime, dependency, or tier exception is granted.

options.name: Keep the generated C shim
options.detail: Complete adoption through the existing header-driven binder and ordinary Jet calls.
options.technical:
Retain D-FFI-CPP1=A. Clang JSON AST feeds the existing checked descriptor; the binder emits cached C-linkage shims and the cpp.<library> projection. Classes remain opaque #SingleUse handles with explicit consuming cleanup. Catch exceptions and return typed CppError. Preserve overload labels, named operators, checked callbacks, and supported on-demand template instantiations.

Pin header, namespace, implementation archive, Clang/archiver, target, descriptor, shim, and generated-source identities. Unsupported ownership, inheritance, layout, callback lifetime, or ABI shapes reject before exposure. No dependency enters compiler seam crates. Every applicable tier consumes this same descriptor and library; target absence is a blocker, not a successful stub.

Reuse admitted binding outputs under the existing package/cache authority: descriptor, generated source, shim archive, and target/tool/input hashes must agree. Only a cache miss requires local regeneration. Apply the shared fallible-cleanup and contained-callback contract; no old panic-on-close or unwinding trampoline remains.
options.code:
# A: current consumer shape; complete the existing boundary.
use cpp.counter as cpp

fn run() {
    counter := cpp.new_counter(10) ?? panic("constructor")
    print(counter.add_amount(5) ?? panic("method"))
    cpp.close_counter(^counter) ?? panic("close")
}
gains: Reuses the ratified binder and callers.
Hides C++ ABI and exception machinery behind one checked boundary.

options.name: Adopt a direct Clang importer
options.detail: Import C++ semantics directly while retaining checked Jet ownership and errors.
options.technical:
Replace D-FFI-CPP1’s C-shim lowering with one dedicated C++-call TIR operation. Carry the Clang-selected mangled symbol, calling convention, this adjustment, lifetime facts, and typed exception edge. Invoke the existing admitted external Clang tool for target-specific AST/ABI facts. Add no Clang library dependency to compiler seams.

AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web must consume this operation directly. Remove c.jet_cpp_* projections, libjet_cpp_* archive lookup, and generated shim callers together. If a backend needs generated C thunks, it does not implement B; do not relabel a shim as direct import.

Keep the shown cpp.counter projection, checked ownership, fallible cleanup, callback containment, and error meanings. Jet owns target ABI/layout and exception lowering. Unsupported shapes refuse. This option does not authorize additional public value types, import spellings, or an I9 exception.
options.code:
# B proposed importer; same Counter consumer and output 15.
use cpp.counter as cpp

fn run() {
    counter := cpp.new_counter(10) ?? panic("constructor")
    print(counter.add_amount(5) ?? panic("method"))
    cpp.close_counter(^counter) ?? panic("close")
}
gains: Direct semantic import can reduce shim mediation for admitted calls.
losses: Jet takes responsibility for target C++ ABI and layout semantics.
Replacing the existing binder requires a complete cutover.

options.name: Use an explicit binding declaration
options.detail: Make the supported foreign surface explicit before generating the same Jet projection.
options.technical:
C makes .cppbind.json the sole input to the existing inspect bind cpp action. Header-only automatic discovery for that library retires. Top-level fields are header, library, and bindings. Each binding has cpp and jet. header resolves through package-root path authority; library is a logical link name resolved only through declared library roots.

A cpp selector is a fully qualified C++ declaration name followed by parameter type-ids. Resolve type-ids semantically in the selected translation unit, including aliases. Include the method’s cv/ref qualifiers and explicit template arguments where present. Exception specification is checked from the resolved declaration, not used to invent overloads. Exactly one accessible AST declaration must match. Accessible Clang-synthesized destructors may be selected.

The binder prints canonical selectors for inspection and copying. Unknown fields, duplicate selections or exports, invalid names, missing or ambiguous matches, and header drift reject. A selected constructor requires a selected consuming destructor. Types and lifetime/error policy come from the checked descriptor, never a text ABI parser.

Hash the selection file and every resolved artifact into the existing binding identity. Keep one descriptor/shim lowerer. No new command, parallel discovery mode, or separate trust mechanism is added. The same cleanup and callback contract applies.
gains: The admitted foreign surface is explicit and reviewable.
losses: An explicit binding selection must track header changes.
A new selection file is required beside ordinary package facts.

decisions.gist: Must a performance claim beat its plain spelling?
decisions.lesson: A performance spelling is not faster merely because its output is correct. This choice adds a benefit gate to the existing peer and regression gates. Measure the same work and scope each claim to the cells it actually wins.

story.current: The repository already has a paired map/para_map crossover example; it records cheap cases that did not win. No timing is rerun during preparation.
story.problem: A performance spelling is not faster merely because its output is correct. This choice adds a benefit gate to the existing peer and regression gates. Measure the same work and scope each claim to the cells it actually wins.

decisions.detail:
A adds a standing process requirement; it does not authorize syntax or a benchmark-only implementation. The owner may authorize a bounded prototype to obtain pre-acceptance evidence. Keep all current safety, diagnostics, determinism, and I9 requirements.

Census layout, parallel operations, indexed mutation, inline controls, freeze/views, static constants, pools/IDs, channels/shared state, collections, and text views. Distinguish benefit claims from control/safety claims. Reuse tools/perf/dx-benchmark-matrix.mjs and existing evaluator/baseline gates.

Empty/tiny input, setup, allocation/cache behavior, numeric overflow/equivalence, target differences, noisy trials, and absent original fixtures remain explicit cells or blockers. Only an owner decision may change the required scope. No result was measured in this preparation.

options.name: Require a paired, scoped win
options.detail: Require same-workload evidence before accepting a performance benefit; keep the plain path and explicit expert control.
options.technical:
Register each performance claim as an executable plain/candidate pair in the existing matrix. Match input bytes, exact numeric bounds, effects, output oracle, target/toolchain/artifact, host, warmup/trials, and setup. Each declared required metric must pass independently. A candidate/plain ratio below 1.00 with sufficient evidence is a win; equality is not.

Preserve the separate standing peer gate: Rust permits only the <=1.05 same-run noise band; every non-Rust peer requires <1.00. Never average cells or metrics. Wrong, stale, absent, unavailable, unsupported, contaminated, or inconclusive results remain non-passing. Keep setup/cold costs and resource use visible.

A workload-family win is not a universal claim. Control-only or safety-motivated surfaces need not pretend to be speed improvements. Reuse the current matrix, evaluator, and artifact laws; add no timer, runtime selector, or scoring mechanism. A losing ratified feature stays carded; only the owner may retire or rescope it.
options.code:
# Proposed A: existing source, new publication gate
// Existing same-workload pair; work consumes every element.
serial :: values.map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
parallel :: values.para_map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
assert_eq(serial, parallel)
# Candidate beats plain on every claimed required cell/metric.
# Missing or inconclusive evidence blocks the benefit claim.

decisions.title: Which JIT optimization default and runtime bound should apply?
decisions.gist: Which JIT optimization default and runtime bound should apply?
decisions.lesson: Jet has two consumers of the same Cranelift backend. Choose one coordinated setting and a measurable internal JIT/AOT bound. Internal parity never waives the standing peer gate. The original LCG source is missing, so no new timing or substitute reproduction is claimed.

story.current: Both consumers currently use none. The recorded 200-million-step LCG run was cancelled; its original source must be recovered before timing.
story.problem: Jet has two consumers of the same Cranelift backend. Choose one coordinated setting and a measurable internal JIT/AOT bound. Internal parity never waives the standing peer gate. The original LCG source is missing, so no new timing or substitute reproduction is claimed.

inWild.note: Cranelift exposes optimization levels; speed is a setting, not evidence that this Jet workload is faster.

decisions.detail:
No new syntax, command, dependency, or I9 exception is proposed. A/B change both crates/jet-jit/src/jit/api_debug.rs and runtime_host.rs together. #2888/#2892 supply shared-MIR work and #2919 supplies the corpus/evaluator.

Recover the exact original LCG bytes and hash them. A lookalike recurrence is not the reproduction. Use scalar, indexed, columnar, and explicit-parallel cells, with exact outputs and identities. Separately record cold and warm costs. Deoptimization, cancellation, absent providers, mismatch, and inconclusive trials cannot pass.

Existing AOT, default run/dev, interpreter, and applicable web semantics remain identical. Publish the selected setting and legality through the same explanation record. This ballot chooses a target contract, not a claim that speed already achieves it.

options.name: Speed in both JIT consumers; tight gate
options.detail: Use coordinated speed optimization and require warm JIT/release-AOT <=1.05 in each named cell, without relaxing cold or peer gates.
options.technical:
Set Cranelift opt_level to speed in both api_debug.rs and runtime_host.rs. Keep the existing legal MIR and optimization records. Add no flag, pipeline, or dependency. Each warm JIT/release-AOT ratio must be <=1.05. That is a parity ceiling, not a win.

Measure cold process, preparation, and first-output costs separately. Every existing peer and resource gate remains binding. If speed mode loses a required cell, repair lowering or backend work and keep the card open. Never relax the bound, hide compilation costs, or count an AOT/deoptimized run as JIT.
options.code:
# Proposed A: compiler configuration, not a new CLI flag
opt_level = "speed"
# Both Cranelift consumers.
# Warm JIT/release-AOT <=1.05 per required internal cell.
# Cold/startup and standing peer gates remain separate.
gains: One configuration for both consumers.
A tight, per-cell runtime acceptance bound.
losses: Additional optimization can increase compilation work; cold evidence must expose it.

options.name: Speed with a wider internal ceiling
options.detail: Use the same coordinated speed setting but allow warm JIT/release-AOT <=2.00.
options.technical: Apply precisely the same semantic, configuration, cold, identity, and peer gates as A. Only the internal Jet JIT/AOT ceiling changes to 2.00. It cannot excuse a required peer loss or be called parity.
options.code:
# Proposed B: same compiler setting
opt_level = "speed"
# Both consumers; internal warm ratio <=2.00.
# No waiver of cold, resource, or standing peer gates.
gains: More implementation latitude against Jet’s own AOT baseline.
losses: Allows JIT to take twice the AOT execution time on an internal cell.

options.name: Keep none; improve shared lowering
options.detail: Retain the current opt_level and seek improvements in the existing shared MIR path.
options.technical: Keep none in both consumers while improving the existing shared legal MIR. Preserve every current criterion and hard peer gate. This option does not accept a new JIT/AOT ratio or promise that MIR work alone closes the recorded slowdown. The reported cancellation remains unresolved until the original workload passes.
options.code:
# Proposed C: retain the existing configuration
opt_level = "none"
# Improve shared MIR; prove the original workload.
# The recorded cancelled run is not a passing result.
gains: Avoids the extra optimization work of speed mode.
losses: Leaves the reported JIT deficit without A’s tight acceptance target.

recommendation.why: Use coordinated speed optimization and require warm JIT/release-AOT <=1.05 in each named cell, without relaxing cold or peer gates.
gains: One configuration for both consumers.
A tight, per-cell runtime acceptance bound.

losses.loss: Optimization performs additional compilation work.
losses.mitigation: The selected backend setting may improve generated code by doing more compiler work. Required cold and resource gates must catch any unacceptable cost.

whyNot.reason: Allows JIT to take twice the AOT execution time on an internal cell.
Leaves the reported JIT deficit without A’s tight acceptance target.

recommendation.tradeoff: Preserve the current safety, diagnostics, and cross-tier contract. Unavailable or inconclusive evidence cannot pass.

decisions.title: Should para reuse the existing measured selection gate?
decisions.gist: Should para reuse the existing measured selection gate?
decisions.lesson: Parallel syntax defines safe transfer and deterministic result rules, not guaranteed speed. A avoids needless workers without changing those rules. It uses the existing acceleration policy rather than inventing another scheduler or timing rule.

story.current: The checked-in crossover example compares map and para_map across sizes and costs. Original S7 bytes are missing and must be recovered for closure.
story.problem: Parallel syntax defines safe transfer and deterministic result rules, not guaranteed speed. A avoids needless workers without changing those rules. It uses the existing acceleration policy rather than inventing another scheduler or timing rule.

inWild.note: The same ordered map comparison; a parallel iterator does not promise that a cheap callback wins.

decisions.detail:
Preserve D-PARCAPTURE1 and D-ADAPTRT1. A adopts D-ACCEL1’s current selection law unchanged; B explicitly changes only this surface’s dynamic selection; C keeps current explicit scheduling. No new syntax, force switch, scheduler, dependency, or tier exception is authorized.

Recover exact S7 sources and outputs 3999999 and 4000000000000. Keep original time/RSS scope. The existing cheap-case <=1.05 overhead ceiling is not a claimed win and cannot relax a stricter paired gate or any standing peer metric. Explain selected engine, measured/static inputs, and identity through #2945/#2899.

Exercise tiny/empty inputs, retained first result, seeds/chunks, deterministic merge, ordered errors, rejected captures, failure cleanup, controlled time, and unavailable workers on every applicable tier. Probe and caller execution must preserve the same operation; no input-specific or benchmark-only fallback is allowed.

options.name: Reuse the measured acceleration gate
options.detail: Keep para semantics and let the existing gate avoid unprofitable worker scheduling.
options.technical:
Reuse D-ACCEL1’s 1024-item floor and projected 2x gain rule. A static rejection reads no clock. For an eligible probe, bracket one retained first chunk with at most two monotonic timestamps. This explicitly replaces #2922’s old one-clock-read criterion; a duration needs both endpoints. Count probe, storage, allocation, and workers in end-to-end results.

Retain the first result exactly once. Caller execution preserves the same logical chunks, seed-factory calls, adjacent deterministic merge, ordered outputs, and lowest-source-index failure. Never substitute an ordinary left fold or replay effects. No partial result escapes; existing effects are not rolled back.

Validate captures, shareability, transfers, and callback facts before selection. A serial choice cannot legalize an invalid program. Missing clock/workers selects the canonical caller engine with an explanation. Controlled worlds never read an uncontrolled host clock. All adapters consume the one Prelude/Foundation policy and explanation record.
options.code:
# Proposed A: unchanged public operation
// Existing same-workload pair; work consumes every element.
serial :: values.map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
parallel :: values.para_map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
assert_eq(serial, parallel)
# Static refusal: no timing reads.
# Eligible first chunk: <=2 timestamps; retain result once.
# Select workers only when the existing gate predicts 2x gain.
gains: Avoids unprofitable scheduling without another selector.
Preserves explicit para ownership and reduction semantics.
losses: An eligible runtime probe has a bounded measurement cost.

options.name: Use static selection only
options.detail: Use known size and cost facts without a runtime timing probe.
options.technical: Reuse the existing legality facts and canonical caller/worker engines. Select workers only when static facts justify them; otherwise keep the same caller-engine para semantics and explanation. No clock reads or guessed callback cost. This requires a static selection policy amendment to D-ACCEL1 for this surface; all other acceleration uses retain their law.
options.code:
# Proposed B: unchanged public operation
// Existing same-workload pair; work consumes every element.
serial :: values.map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
parallel :: values.para_map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
assert_eq(serial, parallel)
# No clock reads.
# Missing static cost proof selects the caller engine.
gains: No runtime timing overhead.
losses: Cannot exploit profitable cases whose callback cost is only known at runtime.

options.name: Keep explicit worker scheduling
options.detail: Keep the current explicit parallel request and report its actual overhead.
options.technical: Preserve the current explicit scheduling behavior and all legality/order/failure rules. Measure the existing workers and allocation path; reduce overhead within that path. Do not introduce a force flag, another scheduler, or a silent serial legality exception. A losing cheap case remains a failed criterion.
options.code:
# Proposed C: unchanged operation and scheduling policy
// Existing same-workload pair; work consumes every element.
serial :: values.map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
parallel :: values.para_map((item: Int) -> work(item, cost))
assert_eq(serial, parallel)
# Keep explicit workers and measure complete costs.
# A losing cheap case stays open.
gains: No new selection policy.
losses: Cheap or small callbacks still pay explicit scheduling overhead.

recommendation.why: Keep para semantics and let the existing gate avoid unprofitable worker scheduling.
gains: Avoids unprofitable scheduling without another selector.
Preserves explicit para ownership and reduction semantics.

losses.loss: An eligible probe consumes time and bounded state.
losses.mitigation: A runtime duration requires observation. Static rejection avoids the probe; retaining its result prevents duplicate user work.

whyNot.reason: Cannot exploit profitable cases whose callback cost is only known at runtime.
Cheap or small callbacks still pay explicit scheduling overhead.

recommendation.tradeoff: Preserve the current safety, diagnostics, and cross-tier contract. Unavailable or inconclusive evidence cannot pass.

decisions.title: What compiler proof must Jet require before 1.0?
decisions.gist: What compiler proof must Jet require before 1.0?
decisions.lesson: A compiler turns source code into executable operations. Proof can show those operations keep the allowed behavior under precise rules. Tests inspect examples. The rules themselves can be wrong. Every choice retains tests and explicit foreign-tool assumptions. Permitted resource failures depend on stated premises, not an unlimited promise.
decisions.story: Maya releases a calculation library. She needs the same allowed answers and failures across Jet modes. Her reviewer asks which translation steps have checked arguments and which still rely on tests or external tools.
decisions.inWild:
# https://compcert.org/man/manual001.html
# Compile the corresponding C calculation library.
ccomp -c calculation.c
# The covered proof ends before external assembly/linking.
# Honor source, numeric, tool, and environment assumptions.
decisions.detail:
A compiler reads source, checks its rules, and translates it into executable operations. Semantic preservation means the translation introduces no behavior outside the published language's allowed behavior. A model is the precise rule set. A theorem is a proved statement. A proof artifact stores an argument for replay by a checker.

The model itself is trusted and can misstate Jet. Validate its executable form against ratified specifications, I5 examples, and the canonical conformance corpus. A disagreement blocks the affected claim. Repair an incorrect model; if the language rule itself must change, obtain an owner decision. A theorem claims agreement with published Jet semantics, never unstated application intent.

Acceptance relation: when compilation succeeds, target behavior must refine source behavior under the stated configuration, resource, foreign-contract, and scheduling premises. Every completed target result, failure, and externally visible event trace must be allowed by the source model. Preserve specified event order and failure behavior. Target scheduling may select an allowed source schedule; it may not introduce a deadlock or violate a promised progress condition.

Finite resources are explicit. State stack, allocation, fuel, and scheduling premises, and list modeled resource-exhaustion outcomes. A target-only exhaustion result is admissible only where existing ratified semantics permits it and the stated resource premise fails. Otherwise it needs a separate owner-approved semantic change. This ballot grants no new I9 exception, generic timeout exemption, or freedom to turn defined errors into undefined behavior.

Preservation alone permits a compiler that rejects everything. Acceptance and coverage therefore remain independently required through conformance, examples, and real workflows. An invalid user's program still needs the correct Jet diagnostic. A compiler-internal failure on valid supported source is not a new user restriction.

Fixed denominator: all I9 modes and ratified applicable capabilities at the candidate revision. Dropping a tier or capability cannot satisfy this gate without a separate explicit owner decision and any required I9 carve-out. The research ledger is not the denominator authority. Use the existing construct, Core, route, and example censuses.

Stage map. Parsing reads structure; checking establishes rules; compile-time evaluation executes code while deciding meaning; initial lowering creates shared operations. Optimization changes those operations. Adapters marshal or translate them for each mode. Jet-owned runtime and Prelude implementations provide Core behavior. A covers all these stages, including Prelude implementation correctness against its contracts, not merely correct symbol calls.

B covers parsing, checking, compile-time evaluation and its reachable operations, and initial lowering. D covers shared-operation optimization, adapters, and Jet-owned runtime/Prelude implementations, starting from valid shared operations. E covers the shared-operation reference interpreter and its Jet-owned runtime/Prelude operations; source processing and other modes remain tested. F requires executable mechanized source and shared-operation semantics, but no production compiler theorem. C adds no formal gate.

Artifact binding is mandatory for every claimed proof. Accepted shape 1: extracted or in-logic generated implementation, with proof/model/source/build identities and every extraction/compiler/runtime assumption named. Shape 2: direct verification of the implementation source against a specified language model, with the source-to-binary toolchain explicitly trusted or separately checked. Shape 3: each covered translation has a certificate accepted by a sound checker whose executable identity and build assumptions are bound.

A theorem about an abstract algorithm plus an unrelated unverified Rust implementation does not qualify. A hash alone establishes identity, not correspondence. Each release receipt must name the proved object, checked relation, binding shape, exact implementation/checker/certificate identity, and trusted build chain. Certificate instances are checked on the relevant compile, not replaced by an old passing batch.

No binding architecture is selected here. The bounded experiment must compare these shapes on the same slice and expose their trust chains. A later concrete major architecture or dependency choice requires its own owner ballot before production adoption. This ballot does not authorize rewriting the compiler inside a prover. No direct Rust or Cranelift semantic verification model was captured in this corpus; A's Rust Prelude and compile-time coverage remain explicit missing prerequisites.

Per-mode boundary. Release: Jet's theorem reaches emitted Rust under a stated Rust model; rustc, LLVM, assembler, and linker remain trusted foreign tools unless separately checked. Development: it reaches emitted Cranelift IR under a stated model; Cranelift and its toolchain remain trusted. Web: it reaches emitted output under a stated model; the browser engine remains trusted. Interpreter: Jet-owned interpretation is covered, but the Rust build chain producing that interpreter is still trusted unless separately bound by stronger evidence.

Thus A is not an end-to-end physical-machine theorem for every release binary. It removes unproved Jet-controlled transformations, not all foreign-tool exposure. Foreign optimization remains outside that theorem and under existing differential and performance gates. Retaining rustc/LLVM is not a proved optimization guarantee. Proving or checking a larger foreign suffix later would require new evidence, not an assumption that the literature makes it impossible.

Two methods can cooperate: prove a transformation algorithm, or prove a result checker sound and require an accepted certificate for each covered result. Sound means no incorrect translation is accepted under the checker rules. A tested checker, bounded validator, timeout, unknown, unsupported construct, missing certificate, or failed replay is not proof.

Checker rejection or unknown must use a deterministic already-proved fallback path, or stop compilation as an internal failure when no such path exists. Never accept unchecked output or blame valid source. The fallback decision and reason are inspectable. Required performance cells still gate release: a slower valid fallback is not permission to average away a loss. Same inputs, tool identities, and configured proof limits must yield the same decision.

Every required stage needs a checked argument: a bound proved implementation, or a sound bound checker with an accepted result certificate. Tests cannot fill an A proof cell. Foreign implementations, operating systems, hardware, and explicit unsafe contracts remain named premises or separate obligations. Foreign call marshalling and Jet-controlled boundary behavior remain in the relevant Jet proof scope.

Every option retains conformance, diagnostics, examples, independent differential/property/mutation evidence, platform/domain qualification, performance, and the ratified professional-handoff window. Tests remain valuable for model validity, acceptance/coverage, unproved components, integration, and external assumptions. Proof removes uncertainty about all covered inputs within its model; tests do not duplicate that universal argument.

Historical evidence illustrates the distinction. Csmith reported no CompCert middle-end bug in six CPU-years while finding problems in unproved components. That result belongs to its historical compiler versions and campaign, not current CompCert or Jet. Current CompCert documentation includes a proved parser and Clight-to-assembly phase; preprocessing, assembly, linking, system library, and floating-point assumptions remain important boundaries.

Feasibility context, not option ranking: the historical CompCert work reported roughly 42,000 Coq lines; the CakeML compiler paper reported roughly 100,000 HOL4 proof-script lines. These are different subsets, architectures, dates, and counting methods. They do not estimate Jet effort. Cost can be increased and work decomposed; neither establishes that the required model and binding exist today.

A research slice must cover values, mutation, compile-time behavior, rejection, failure, and observations with deliberate false claims rejected. It is a research result, not release qualification. New #2925 consumes existing census/proof/hardening owners. Full-Jet feasibility remains unestablished. The existing build-failure receipt is context on the card, not the reason for choosing a proof policy.

recommendation.why: Require a checked relation for every Jet-controlled step, including compile-time and Core behavior. Bind arguments to the real implementation while exposing the foreign compiler suffix.
gains: No Jet-controlled stage can qualify solely through example tests.

losses.loss: 1.0 waits on a proof obligation whose size and feasibility are unmeasured.
losses.mitigation: More resources and modular checking can build the missing model and binding. They cannot replace the obligation to establish them before release.

losses.loss: Covered semantic changes require renewed proof correspondence before release.
losses.mitigation: Checkers and dependency reuse avoid needless reproof. A changed relation or binding still needs a new argument; old evidence establishes the old object.

whyNot.reason: It proves the single initial lowering, but leaves later Jet optimization and runtime behavior generally unproved. A covers those Jet steps; both still assume foreign compiler tools.
It proves the back half, but source checking, compile-time evaluation, and initial lowering can still supply the wrong valid operations.
A proved reference makes differential tests stronger, but agreement on tested cases does not prove the other production modes or source translation.
A precise executable model is valuable, but does not establish production compiler correspondence.
Even the strong ratified test window cannot establish preservation for all covered inputs. Tests and proofs answer different questions.

recommendation.tradeoff: Require a stronger release obligation and ongoing correspondence discipline, without claiming an end-to-end machine theorem or guaranteed date.

decisions.title: Keep audit methods distinct while removing repeated report mechanics
decisions.gist: How should Jet organize audits without erasing their different questions?
decisions.lesson: An audit method asks a particular question and demands particular evidence. Jet has distinct methods with overlapping report mechanics. Every option preserves the methods and their proof requirements.
decisions.story: User asks for a loop-syntax consistency audit. The agent must not substitute a philosophy review simply because both inspect language features.
decisions.inWild:
# https://agentskills.io/specification
skill-name/
  SKILL.md       # metadata and instructions
  references/   # read when required
  scripts/      # optional executable helpers

options.name: Distinct methods, existing shared rules
options.detail: Keep named methods. Consolidate repeated reporting into the existing shared reference. Audit names continue to identify distinct questions. Repeated report steps have one maintained source. Shared report guidance remains a required dependency.
options.technical:
Retain separately routed surface, spec-compliance, mission, persona, first-principles, ontology, type-unification, and pragmatism methods. Retain frequency research and competitive measurement as distinct workflows. Each keeps its own question, required evidence, investigative method, artifacts, and stopping conditions.

Reuse .agents/skills/_shared/audit-dispositions.md for shared report mechanics. Keep _shared/standing-lens.md for its distinct evidence role. Do not create a competing common protocol file. Keep global authority, model policy, and ownership rules in AGENTS.md. Required reference loading stays explicit.

Shared mechanics respect each method’s output and write boundaries. Report-only methods are not forced to create Tower cards. Keep empirical sampling, independent-reader protocols, and method-specific stopping rules inside their own methods.

Update project-owned triggers and consumers together. Keep host-specific invocation claims qualified until the active host is tested. Shared/global skill installations are inspection-only. This choice authorizes neither a generic audit checklist nor automatic follow-on audits.
options.code:
# Request: audit loop syntax for consistency
surface-audit/SKILL.md
  # Own question, evidence, method, completion.
  # Read ../_shared/audit-dispositions.md.
spec-compliance-audit/SKILL.md
  # Keep its distinct comparison against ratified law.
_shared/audit-dispositions.md
  # Canonical shared report disposition rules.
# Keep standing-lens.md for its separate evidence role.
# Run surface-audit only; return consistency findings.

options.name: Self-contained methods

decisions.title: Which proof checker should anchor Jet’s compiler assurance work?
decisions.gist: Which proof checker should anchor Jet’s compiler assurance work?
decisions.lesson: A proof checker verifies mathematical arguments. It does not establish that a model describes the real compiler. Jet already requires proof across its own stages. This choice selects the development tool, not a weaker proof boundary or a compiler rewrite.
decisions.story: Maya reviews a changed compiler pass. She needs one reproducible argument tied to its real implementation, not an unrelated theorem or a green test run.
decisions.inWild:
# https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas
# Inside the Rust calculation crate:
charon cargo --preset=aeneas
./bin/aeneas -backend lean calculation.llbc
# Translation output still needs proofs and checked binding.
decisions.detail:
D-COMPILER-PROOF1=A is already ratified. This ballot selects only one canonical proof-construction and replay toolchain. It does not reduce required stages, permit new resource failures, rewrite the compiler, or add a public Jet command. Ordinary Jet installation requires no proof assistant. Root compiler and seam dependencies remain path-only.

Compare the three permitted implementation bindings on the same nontrivial slice under #2925: verified construction, direct verification of real implementation source, and a sound translation checker with accepted certificates. The selected tool must reject detached algorithm theorems and digest-only correspondence claims. Unknown, timeout, unsupported, admitted, missing, and substituted evidence cannot satisfy a proof cell.

Canonical proof artifacts identify proposition, source/model/implementation, checker, binding method, assumptions, construction chain, and candidate. Prefer universal pass arguments checked during compiler construction. A per-compilation certificate must be checked for the actual translation. Preserve deterministic proved fallback and all performance gates.

Primary evidence: https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas ; https://compcert.org/man/manual001.html ; https://cakeml.org/ . Aeneas documents safe-subset limits and ongoing unsafe/concurrency work. No complete Jet/Rust/Cranelift proof model or comparative checker benchmark was captured. These are explicit implementation prerequisites, not inferred capabilities.

options.name: Lean 4
options.detail: Use Lean 4 as the canonical proof checker. Rust-oriented proof tooling has a documented Lean route. One checker anchors replay and claim composition. The model and checker remain named trust assumptions.
options.technical: Use Lean 4 for canonical source, shared-operation, target-model, checker-soundness, and composition arguments. Pin it in the development environment, not the compiler dependency graph. Aeneas may generate proof input where its supported subset applies. Its Rust-to-model translation is not automatically a checked implementation binding. Unsafe, concurrency, external definitions, nested control, and generic-reference gaps remain explicit obligations, not exclusions.
options.code:
# Proposed: prove the calculation compiler slice with Lean 4.
# Pin Lean and every model or generator input.
node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs --replay
# Reject missing implementation correspondence.

options.name: Rocq
options.detail: Use Rocq as the canonical proof checker. CompCert provides concrete compiler-preservation proof practice. One checker anchors replay and claim composition. CompCert’s theorem does not verify Jet’s Rust implementation.
options.technical: Use Rocq for the same complete Jet obligation relation. CompCert supplies methods and formalization examples, not transferable correctness of Jet. Aeneas has a Coq backend, but its documentation identifies Lean and HOL4 as its most mature backends. Do not infer comparative proof speed or total Rust coverage from this evidence.
options.code:
# Proposed: prove the same calculation slice with Rocq.
# Pin Rocq and every model or generator input.
node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs --replay
# Reject missing implementation correspondence.

options.name: HOL4
options.detail: Use HOL4 as the canonical proof checker. CakeML demonstrates checked compiler construction and composition. Aeneas documents a mature HOL4 backend. CakeML’s verified binary is not a verified Jet binary.
options.technical: Use HOL4 for the same source-to-output models and implementation-bound arguments. CakeML demonstrates verified construction, including a bootstrapped compiler, but adopting HOL4 does not authorize a Jet-to-CakeML port or a self-hosting gate. Existing Rust, Cranelift, and browser suffixes retain their explicit boundaries.
options.code:
# Proposed: prove the same calculation slice with HOL4.
# Pin HOL4 and every model or generator input.
node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs --replay
# Reject missing implementation correspondence.

comparisons.note: Aeneas translates a safe Rust subset toward proof tools. Unsupported code and translation trust remain separate obligations.
comparisons.code:

# Inside the Rust calculation crate:

./bin/aeneas -backend lean calculation.llbc
# Translation output still needs proofs and checked binding.

gains: Rust-oriented proof tooling has a documented Lean route.
One checker anchors replay and claim composition.

losses.loss: The model and checker remain named trust assumptions.
losses.mitigation: A checked argument still depends on its stated rules and the mechanism checking those rules.

whyNot.reason: Rocq’s compiler precedent is strong, but the examined Rust toolchain documents stronger Lean and HOL4 support.
HOL4 remains credible; Lean offers the selected dependent-type proof workflow without requiring CakeML adoption.

recommendation.tradeoff: No checker choice removes the model or implementation-binding obligations.

decisions.title: When should Jet retain the reasons behind a checked claim?
decisions.gist: When should Jet retain the reasons behind a checked claim?
decisions.lesson: A useful explanation shows the rule, its inputs, and whether they still apply. Jet already records facts, proofs, and source changes. This choice decides how those reasons survive for editors, review, and learning without creating another meaning for the program.
decisions.story: Maya changes a bound after reviewing an optimization. She wants the old explanation to remain inspectable and the current claim to become stale immediately.
decisions.inWild:
# https://www.why3.org/doc/starting.html
why3 ide hello_proof.why
# Select a goal, inspect its task, change the source.
why3 replay hello_proof
# Changed goals remain visibly obsolete until replayed.
decisions.detail:
This extends D-FACTMODEL1, D-FACT-LAW1, D-FACT-OWN1, D-PROVE-SEM1, D-JPROOF1, D-RECORD1, and source-bound semantic operations. It does not reopen their meaning, privacy policy, or artifact format ownership. Migrate producers and consumers together; no legacy reader or parallel explanation engine.

Static derivation, mathematical proof, recorded execution, sampled agreement, and external assumption are distinct evidence methods. A renderer cannot promote one into another. Changed premises invalidate dependents. Stale, expired, redacted, unavailable, unsupported, and budget-exhausted states remain explicit. Hover must not execute user effects.

The same bounds, ownership, failure, mutation, and optimization witnesses must expose the same claim and premises through CLI, editor, review, and learner. Negative controls substitute a source revision, remove a premise, attach a false reason, and mislabel sampled agreement. Every consumer must reject the false current claim.

options.name: Shared reason records
options.detail: Retain compact reason links with existing evidence. Every consumer uses the same checked reason. Old claims retain inspectable source-bound premises. Retained reason links occupy storage.
options.technical: Extend existing typed evidence with derivation references: subject, claim, producer/method, rule, premise identities, source origin, source/run/target identity, assumptions, disposition, and optional observation/counterexample reference. Facts remain enums and keep one authoritative producer. Intern links; retain only the configured evidence slice. Existing privacy and retention rules govern payloads. No new artifact container or second fact plane.
options.code:
# Proposed evidence projection; existing record container.
claim: bounds-safe
rule: index-within-length
premises: [index-range, length]
source: calculation.jet@revision
validity: stale-after-bound-change
# Expand through existing inspect, editor, or review views.

options.name: Recompute on request
options.detail: Rebuild the reasons from exact inputs when requested. No dedicated retained derivation graph. Current reasons use current authoritative analysis. Old explanations need the old inputs and analysis tools.
options.technical: Use the same record schema as a query result, but do not retain reason links with evidence. Reanalysis is static and must not execute user effects. Historical queries require exact source, configuration, implementation, and target inputs. Missing inputs or exhausted analysis limits yield unavailable or unknown, not reconstructed certainty.
options.code:
# Proposed query against retained exact inputs.
claim: bounds-safe
request: recompute-reasons
source: calculation.jet@old-revision
# Missing old input or tool: unavailable, not guessed.

options.name: Complete derivation snapshots
options.detail: Retain the full derivation for each requested evidence capture. A capture contains all permitted derivation details. Historical inspection needs less reconstruction. Unneeded derivation detail consumes capture capacity.
options.technical: Serialize the complete allowed static derivation for each explicitly requested evidence capture, using the existing record container. Never capture arbitrary runtime values or secrets by default. Respect size and retention limits. A truncated or redacted capture names its missing parts and cannot pretend to be complete.
options.code:
# Proposed complete capture in existing records.
claim: bounds-safe
capture: full-derivation
source: calculation.jet@revision
# Privacy and retention limits still apply.
# Omitted or expired detail stays explicit.

comparisons.note: Why3 keeps proof attempts and transformations, marks changed goals obsolete, and can replay them.
comparisons.code:
# https://www.why3.org/doc/starting.html
why3 ide hello_proof.why
# Select a goal, inspect its task, change the source.
why3 replay hello_proof
# Changed goals remain visibly obsolete until replayed.

recommendation.why: Compact shared links preserve one reason across tools without copying full trees. Exact identities make stale claims visible.
gains: Every consumer uses the same checked reason.
Old claims retain inspectable source-bound premises.

losses.loss: Retained reason links occupy storage.
losses.mitigation: Keeping a historical reason without recomputation requires retaining some information about that reason.

whyNot.reason: Historical explanations disappear when their exact inputs or tools are unavailable.
Complete snapshots retain detail that compact links can share or load only when needed.

recommendation.tradeoff: Deduplication and bounded capture reduce storage, but cannot make retained information occupy no space.

surface.lesson: A useful explanation shows the rule, its inputs, and whether they still apply. Jet already records facts, proofs, and source changes. This choice decides how those reasons survive for editors, review, and learning without creating another meaning for the program.

decisions.title: How should ordinary editors reveal deeper reasoning about code?
decisions.gist: How should ordinary editors reveal deeper reasoning about code?
decisions.lesson: Short source hints help readers without hiding the program. Relationships and proof limits need more room. All choices use the same source-bound facts, complete text access, and keyboard paths. Canvas keeps its separately approved proof rail. No AI or Studio requirement is added.
decisions.story: Maya checks which value changed, who owns it, and why a result is stale. She needs a clear first view and the full evidence when investigating.
decisions.detail:
This chooses presentation defaults only for ordinary editors. D-CANVAS-PROOFLENS1 and other Canvas laws remain unchanged. D-CLI-ONE1, D-REF3, D-REPORT-EDITOR1, source debugging, and shared record identity remain authoritative. No new language syntax or independent evaluation model.

Required states: current, stale, redacted, unavailable, running, failed, empty, and large data. Required access: keyboard-only, stable focus, labels independent of color, reduced motion, narrow/wide layouts, and complete text alternatives. Values always name the observed run and frame. Unobserved values are unavailable.

Owner visual acceptance receives exact prerequisites, launch command, fixture paths, ordered interactions, expected states, and Pass/Bounce cues. A selected screenshot is insufficient. Machine checks remain agent-owned; visual acceptance judges readability and interaction, not compiler correctness.

options.name: Short hints, expandable evidence
options.detail: Show a concise source hint and open details on demand. Source stays readable by default. Experts can pin the complete relationship view. Text and keyboard routes preserve the same evidence.
options.technical: Use concise hover/inlay facts and an expandable, pinnable relationship view. Support ownership/lifetime strips, state transitions, event timelines, dependency/change impact, optimization reasons, and counterexample pairs. Each view is a projection of shared explanation records. Include source/run identity and explicit stale/redacted/unavailable states. No forced panel or quiz during ordinary editing.

options.name: Always-open reasoning panel
options.detail: Keep the complete relationship panel open by default. Detailed relationships are immediately visible. Evidence remains beside the source. The default panel takes space from the source.
options.technical: Open the complete source-linked reasoning panel by default in the ordinary editor. Users can close it, but every new supported workspace begins with the panel. Preserve the same keyboard, text, evidence, and privacy contracts. This does not change Canvas defaults.

options.name: Command-only evidence view
options.detail: Keep source undecorated and open evidence through a command. No persistent source decoration or panel. One explicit command opens complete evidence. The source gives no nearby cue that reasons are available.
options.technical: Expose the full view through an existing inspect/debug/editor action, but do not add default hover/inlay cues or nearby explanation affordances. Keep all evidence and keyboard/text functionality identical. Discoverability relies on command discovery and documentation.

# Opens the same complete source-linked evidence view.

Experts can pin the complete relationship view.

It hides the nearby cue that an explanation exists, without improving the evidence.

decisions.title: What should Jet Learn reveal before a learner makes a prediction?
decisions.gist: What should Jet Learn reveal before a learner makes a prediction?
decisions.lesson: A prediction exposes the rule a learner currently believes. A worked example can teach a rule before testing it. Jet already has an offline exercise runner. Every choice keeps explanations, controlled changes, unfamiliar transfer tasks, and an honest “I do not know” path.
decisions.story: Maya learns why a loop changes a value. She should learn the rule, not merely copy the answer that passes one exercise.
decisions.inWild:
# https://pythontutor.com/
value = 1
value += 2
print(value)
# Predict the next value, then step the visualizer.
# This comparison uses visualization, not AI tutoring.
decisions.detail:
D-LEARN1 already owns the runner, dependency-aware watch session, curriculum, and hints. This ballot chooses feedback order within that mechanism. No new command, language syntax, AI mode, or Studio requirement. #2926 still owns the complete capability/task census, not the interaction implementation.

Every task has an exact source/input identity, deterministic oracle, plausible wrong model, prerequisite, prompt, reveal policy, controlled edit, and different transfer task. Evidence-backed feedback may explain or show a valid counterexample. It cannot invent a reason because it sounds persuasive. Unknown execution or proof never completes a task.

Preserve user edits and progress across interruption. Bind completion to curriculum and oracle identities. Distinguish explain, predict, modify, and derive evidence from solution copying. A simulated reader is not a human learning study. Real transfer claims need actual participant evidence.

Acceptance includes ordinary CLI/editor operation, keyboard/text alternatives, watch and one-shot behavior, stale/unavailable/cancelled states, and the owner learning runbook. The choice is a design judgment; the campaign has not measured comparative learning outcomes for A, B, or C.

options.name: Predict, then reveal
options.detail: Ask for a prediction before showing the worked result. The first answer exposes the learner’s current model. A valid counterexample targets the mistaken rule. An explicit unknown answer reveals help immediately. The first prediction cannot use the unrevealed worked answer.
options.technical: Default each task to minimal prerequisite definitions, prediction or explicit unknown, actual evidence, focused explanation/counterexample, controlled change, and unfamiliar transfer. No forced delay or penalty for unknown. Expert skip leaves the prediction unmeasured, not completed. Ordinary editing never starts quizzes automatically.
options.code:
jet learn --watch=off
# Prompt: value starts at 1, then adds 2. Predict it.
# Answer: 2 / 3 / I do not know
# Reveal: source-bound trace and the distinguishing rule.
# Change: replace addition with multiplication.
# Transfer: derive the result in a different program.

options.name: Worked example first
options.detail: Show a worked example before the first prediction. A learner sees a concrete model before answering. The same later change and transfer tasks remain. The first prediction cannot measure an unrevealed initial model.
options.technical: Show the task’s worked result and valid explanation before asking for an answer. Record the first prediction as post-instruction evidence. Keep the same controlled change and structurally different transfer tasks. Do not claim this measures the learner’s initial understanding.
options.code:

# Show: 1 + 2 gives 3, with the source-bound trace.
# Explain the rule, then ask a related prediction.
# Change: replace addition with multiplication.
# Transfer: derive the result in a different program.

options.name: Learner-directed exploration
options.detail: Let the learner choose when to reveal and predict. The learner controls the order and pace. Every explanation and transfer task remains available. The record may lack an unrevealed prediction.
options.technical: Expose all actions from the start and record the actual order. Prediction after reveal is post-instruction, never baseline evidence. No adaptive AI or generated pedagogy. The deterministic task oracle and transfer requirements remain identical.
options.code:
jet learn --watch=off
# Choose: Predict / Step / Explain / Change / Transfer
# Revealing first marks the initial prediction unmeasured.
# Completion still requires the declared transfer evidence.

comparisons.note: Its visualizer steps through values and frames; teachers can ask students to predict a step. Jet does not copy its AI features.

gains: The first answer exposes the learner’s current model.
A valid counterexample targets the mistaken rule.
An explicit unknown answer reveals help immediately.

losses.loss: The first prediction cannot use the unrevealed worked answer.
losses.mitigation: Revealing that answer first removes the independent initial prediction this option is meant to capture.

whyNot.reason: It loses the unrevealed baseline even when the learner could already reason correctly.

recommendation.tradeoff: A learner may answer unknown immediately; the record must not invent an independent prediction afterward.
