decisions.title: Add borrowed keys and comparators to the rank prototype
decisions.gist: Add two ways to order records in the approved private rank experiment?
decisions.lesson: Rank 2 is the third item. Both choices place Cora:3 there and retain every record once; earlier/later names fall on the correct side. Each side need not be sorted. A view borrows text; get copies the selected record. Both choices are private prototypes.
decisions.explainer:
Rank 2 is the third item. Both choices put Cora:3 there, keep every original record once, and place earlier/later names on the correct side; neither side must be fully sorted. A borrowed view is read-only text tied to its record, not an independent copy. Both examples still copy the selected record through get. These are private experiments, not public methods. The shared name:number records are Eve:1, Ada:2, Cora:3, Bea:4 and Dina:5.

The numeric [9, 1, 5, 3, 7] fixture remains an inherited rank-law check.
decisions.story: Nora has name:number records. She needs the third name alphabetically, not a fully sorted list. The experiment may rearrange this working list. She wants to read each name without copying it, or supply a direct comparison.
decisions.detail:
D-RANK-SELECT2 is a callable amendment to the already ratified D-RANK-SELECT1=A prototype. It does not revisit the earlier partition-versus-index choice.

The same concrete job anchors both choices: Nora has Eve:1, Ada:2, Cora:3, Bea:4 and Dina:5, and wants the third name alphabetically: Cora:3. The approved integer case [9, 1, 5, 3, 7] at rank 2 remains a separate inherited fixture, not a different meaning. A full sort also orders values she will not inspect. A rank operation only promises the rank value and the two partition inequalities.

Existing `sort_by` already shows two useful callable shapes: a unary key and a two-argument callback that returns `Ordering`.

Option A adds those missing shapes to the isolated prototype. A unary key may return a checked `View<V>` rooted in its item, so a field such as a name can be compared without copying its text. A binary callback returns `Ordering` directly when the caller already knows how to compare two samples. Both shapes also have fallible forms. The receiver remains exclusive and mutable only during the authorized movement phase.

Option B keeps the original three forms. It is a real choice for a smaller prototype, but callers with borrowed text keys or an existing comparator remain outside its callable coverage.

D-RANK-SELECT1=A remains immutable authority. Its rank meaning, invalid boundary, partition inequalities, identity preservation, plain storage bound, owned-key callback order, Float relation, error behavior, canonical `get` pairs, and same-build cross-tier result law apply to both options. New callback forms do not create a public name or production API. Later adoption and performance gates remain separate.

A borrowed key is not a raw reference. Provenance ties it to the callback item and receiver. The prototype must release every such view before moving payloads. A fallible comparator may stage indexes before movement so its first error cannot leave a partial rearrangement. These are safety contracts, not user-visible choices about result ownership.

The required evidence still compares partition plus owned `get(k)` with the matching full sort plus `get(k)`. Borrowed bracket reads may supplement that pair only when both sides perform the same checked read.

options.name: Add borrowed keys and direct comparisons
options.detail: Implement two additions, each with and without returned errors: a comparable borrowed key from a record, or a two-record comparison. The name example avoids copying every name; other orderable borrowed views are allowed. Keep the existing record list rather than return a new one. Borrowed keys store one view/index per record; those views cannot escape selection. Comparisons may repeat; returning inconsistent comparators guarantee only termination, safety and record preservation. An error-returning comparison stores one temporary index per record before records move.
options.technical:
Status: proposed amendment only. It is not shipped, and it reserves no public method name.

The inherited forms stay exact:

- `[T].partition_at(k: Int) Bool`.
- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, key: fn(item: T) K) Bool`.
- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, key: fn(item: T) K !E) Bool !E`.

The receiver has exclusive mutable access, as the existing sort receiver. A valid zero-based rank returns `true`, places a rank-`k` value at index `k`, leaves both sides unsorted, and preserves every original element exactly once. Empty input, negative `k`, and `k >= len` return `false` before callbacks, workspace, or mutation.

The plain form keeps no heap allocation, constant auxiliary storage, no payload clone, and worst-case-linear comparisons. The owned-key form evaluates one owned, orderable `K` per original element in source order before movement. It keeps O(n) `(K, index)` descriptors, worst-case O(n) key comparisons, and the inherited fallible law. The first exact error preserves prior callback effects, invokes no later key, releases descriptors, leaves the receiver unchanged, and publishes no partial result.

A adds these overloads to the same `partition_at_by` family:

- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, key: fn(T) View<V> from _0) Bool`.
- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, key: fn(T) View<V> !E from _0) Bool !E`.
- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, compare: fn(left: T, right: T) Ordering) Bool`.
- `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, compare: fn(left: T, right: T) Ordering !E) Bool !E`.

`View<V> from _0` is the existing checked provenance spelling. The view is read-only, rooted in that item and therefore in the receiver. The checker rejects a view that escapes through a result, field, retained closure or later callback. Key evaluation occurs exactly once per original item in source order while the receiver is immobile. Retain O(n) (view, index) descriptors and use worst-case O(n) key comparisons. This is descriptor storage, not cloned name bytes or constant auxiliary storage.

Each borrowed view is released before any payload move. A key error releases all descriptors, runs no later key, preserves prior effects and leaves payload storage unchanged.

The infallible comparator is read-only, may repeat calls, and follows the plain kernel's constant-auxiliary, worst-case-linear target. A successful comparator must define a consistent total preorder. Reversed arguments reverse `Less` and `Greater`; equal values form a transitive tie class. If the callback violates that law but returns, execution remains memory-safe and permutation-preserving, yet no rank-order guarantee applies. Callback state must not make its result depend on call count.

The fallible comparator stages only an index permutation before moving payloads. It may repeat comparisons, stops at the first exact error, invokes no later comparison, preserves prior effects, drops staging, publishes no partial payload and leaves the receiver unchanged. Its conditional O(n) index storage is distinct from a hidden payload copy. The implementation applies the retained permutation only after comparisons succeed, then releases staging.

Use `baseline_sort_view_key` for borrowed-key evidence and `baseline_sort_fallible_compare` for fallible-comparator evidence. They are private full-sort adapters, not public `sort_by` forms. Existing `sort_by` unary-key and two-argument `Ordering` comparisons remain the source convention. Every baseline ends with the same `get(k)` observation as the candidate.

All successful calls retain the ratified partition inequalities, Float total order, identity-preserving multiset, and same-build outcome across AOT, default run, interpreter and applicable web. Equal-key pivot identity is unspecified across versions. Mandatory pairs remain partition-plus-`get` versus sort-plus-`get`, with `~values` on both preserving-input sides. A checked bracket read is supplementary and cannot replace an owned `get` pair. No public API, name or production cutover is authorized.

An inconsistent comparator may lose rank correctness, but the operation still terminates whenever each callback returns, preserves memory safety and retains every receiver value exactly once. The fallible comparator retains the same worst-case-linear comparison bound, including the no-error path; O(n) staging does not permit replacing selection with a full sort.

options.name: Keep the already-approved forms
options.detail: Keep plain ordering plus owned-key functions with or without errors. A String key copies one name per record; no new call forms are added. The same name-based job already works, without a full sort. Example text keys are owned copies; borrowed-key and direct-comparison forms are absent.
options.technical:
Status: proposed amendment choice only. D-RANK-SELECT1=A remains exactly as ratified and is not a public API.

Keep `[T].partition_at(k: Int) Bool`, `[T].partition_at_by(k: Int, key: fn(item: T) K) Bool`, and its fallible `K !E` form. The receiver is exclusive and mutable. A valid rank returns `true`, puts a rank-`k` value at index `k`, leaves both sides unsorted and preserves the multiset. Empty input, negative `k`, and `k >= len` return `false` before callback evaluation, workspace or mutation.

Plain selection keeps no heap allocation, constant auxiliary storage, no payload clone and worst-case-linear comparisons. The unary owned-key form evaluates one owned key per original element in source order before movement, retains O(n) key/index descriptors and has worst-case O(n) key comparisons. Its first fallible error preserves prior callback effects, propagates the exact error, evaluates no later key, releases temporary keys, leaves the receiver unchanged and publishes no partial result.

No receiver-borrowed key view or binary comparator is admitted. That is a callable coverage choice, not a claim that such forms could never be added. A later amendment would need its own provenance, comparator, failure and evidence law.

Successful results preserve the Float relation, partition inequalities, identity-preserving multiset and same-build result across AOT, default run, interpreter and applicable web. Equal-key pivot identity remains unspecified across versions. Mandatory evidence remains partition-plus-`get` versus sort-plus-`get`, with preserving-input `~values` on both sides. No bracket-only observation replaces the owned result pair, and no public adoption or performance claim follows.

comparisons.note: Rust compares two records and selects a position without fully sorting. The colon separates each name from its number.

recommendation.why: A adds borrowed keys and direct comparisons to the same private experiment.
gains: Avoid copying each name during key extraction.
Allow an existing two-record comparison instead of an owned key.

losses.loss: Borrowed keys store one view/index per record; those views cannot escape selection.
losses.mitigation: Exact-once key evaluation needs retained ordering information. Views must be released before the source is rearranged.

losses.loss: Comparisons may repeat; returning inconsistent comparators guarantee only termination, safety and record preservation.

decisions.title: How should an unsigned release source earn reusable trust?
decisions.gist: Choose whether approval covers an unchanged source scope or one exact release.
decisions.lesson: A direct release feed may have no authenticated-provider evidence. Jetpack must hash downloaded bytes, but a same-channel checksum cannot authenticate a publisher. Under A, an unchanged source scope needs no new source-grant prompt. A new request or follow origin needs approval first.
decisions.story: Maya configured an HTTPS release feed with no authenticated publisher evidence. She wants unattended matching updates after approving the source, target and allowed origins.
decisions.inWild: Homebrew's cask sha256 is a cask-authored download assertion. GitHub's asset digest is optional and comes from the same release metadata channel. Neither is independent publisher authentication, so Jet needs an explicit release trust policy.
decisions.detail:
D-RELEASE-TRUST1 is a source decision, not a hash shortcut. It applies to direct GitHub and arbitrary HTTPS release adapters when no existing authenticated provider has verified the publisher.

Before the first artifact request, jetpack shows the logical source target, metadata authority, resolver, selector, asset policy, target/platform, candidate origin, allowed origins and authentication state. An interactive yes is the only first-use authorization. Metadata text, recipe text, channel checksums and observed hashes cannot authorize a source.

A stores `release-trust-v1` under the existing `AUTH_PACKAGE` grant. It binds source target, metadata authority, repository when present, resolver, selector, asset name template, kind, format, root, entry, mode, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins. It excludes version, tag, observed digest and transient URL queries.

A matching grant applies to a later candidate when all bound facts are unchanged. The version, tag and observed hash may change. No new source-grant prompt is shown merely because the candidate changed. A metadata redirect, artifact origin or artifact redirect outside the approved origin scope stops before request or follow. Approval is required before that new action, and the expanded subject records the new scope.

B adds exact version, tag, selected asset and redacted candidate-origin facts. B therefore prompts for a new candidate. The recommendation is A because unattended matching updates require reusable source trust.

A channel checksum is parsed and compared with acquired bytes. It remains same-channel integrity evidence. Jetpack computes a new observed SHA-256 for every acquisition. A same identity with different bytes is a hard mutation error. It never replaces the working pin, cache or generation.

Direct feeds have no public signature, key or proof protocol. Existing authenticated providers retain their own protocol. A recognized provider failure is hard and never downgrades to source trust. The blanket `--trust` flag is rejected for release acquisition. `-y` cannot create or bypass a grant. Noninteractive mode returns E1255 when the required grant or origin approval is absent.

First-install and update trace

A project package uses `jetpack update --deps` to resolve the project channel lock. That command does not realize packages. The existing project realization path owns acquisition, staging and activation.

A user tool uses `jetpack use <ref> --prep` to realize a user profile. This path is independent of project cwd and project lock. The existing user-tool update path, including `jetpack update --tools`, keeps its own profile and generation. Both paths share this trust contract.

Origin scenario

### metadata authority

- **issuer:** `Release.https` declaration.
- **object:** `https://downloads.acme.test/desktool/releases.json`.
- **check before action:** The initial HTTPS origin must be in `origins`. Each metadata redirect is checked before its next request.
- **prompt and authority:** No artifact source grant is needed for the declared metadata request. A new redirect origin needs interactive approval before follow. The declaration and existing origin grant are the authority.

### artifact origin

- **issuer:** selected `ReleaseAsset.url`.
- **object:** `https://cdn.acme.test/desktool-1.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.
- **check before action:** The candidate origin must be in the declared or granted ordered origin scope before the first artifact GET.
- **prompt and authority:** A missing source grant needs approval before this GET. A later candidate under unchanged scope needs no new source-grant prompt. The source grant is the authority.

### redirect origin

- **issuer:** HTTPS `Location` response.
- **object:** `https://unexpected.acme.test/desktool-1.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.
- **check before action:** The redirect origin is checked before follow. The provider never follows first and trusts later.
- **prompt and authority:** A new redirect origin needs interactive approval before follow. The expanded ordered origin grant is the authority.


Authority boundaries

### source grant

- **issuer:** user, through an interactive approval.
- **object:** `release-trust-v1` with source, authority, resolver, selector, asset policy, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins.
- **check:** Exact scope match before an unsigned artifact GET and before any new request or redirect follow.
- **prompt:** First direct artifact use or a new origin requires approval. Same scope and a later candidate do not.
- **authority:** Existing `AUTH_PACKAGE` scoped grant and trust ledger.
- **exclusion:** It excludes mutable version, tag, observed hash, transient URL queries, Build steps and application launch.

### channel checksum

- **issuer:** configured feed issuer.
- **object:** candidate `channel_sha256` text from GitHub `digest` or custom `sha256`.
- **check:** Parse bare 64-hex or exact `sha256:` prefix to lowercase `Sha256`; compare with acquired bytes.
- **prompt:** None. A match never creates trust.
- **authority:** Same metadata channel only.
- **exclusion:** It is not publisher authentication, a source grant, build authorization or launch permission.

### observed hash

- **issuer:** Jet provider.
- **object:** SHA-256 of the exact acquired bytes and the concrete release pin.
- **check:** Compute after GET and compare with channel assertion and any known pin.
- **prompt:** None. A mismatch is a hard error.
- **authority:** Jet's lock, receipt and Store facts.
- **exclusion:** It proves byte identity only. It does not authenticate a publisher or authorize code.

### authenticated-provider evidence

- **issuer:** an existing provider protocol.
- **object:** provider-owned authenticated status.
- **check:** Verify the existing protocol before acquisition. A recognized failure stops.
- **prompt:** No downgrade prompt. Failure never becomes source trust.
- **authority:** Existing ratified provider authority and key policy.
- **exclusion:** Direct feed fields cannot manufacture it. It does not grant builds or launches.

### build authorization

- **issuer:** existing recipe and build approval policy.
- **object:** executable Build steps and locked `.fetch(url, sha256)` inputs.
- **check:** Preserve required hashes, sandbox, permits and confined outputs.
- **prompt:** Existing build approval prompt, when that policy requires one.
- **authority:** D-JPK-BUILDRECIPE1, D-JPK-SANDBOX2 and current build trust.
- **exclusion:** Release source trust, checksums and observed hashes do not authorize builds.

### application-launch permission

- **issuer:** user/runtime policy.
- **object:** launch of the activated app entry.
- **check:** Apply the existing launch policy after activation and on next launch.
- **prompt:** Only the existing launch-policy prompt, if any. Release acquisition never supplies it.
- **authority:** Existing RuntimePolicy and active generation.
- **exclusion:** Source grants, hashes and build approval do not launch an app.


Activation remains atomic. Trust authorizes only this source decision. It never authorizes another source, Build steps, arbitrary execution, host writes, elevation or application launch.

The design rejects hash-only trust, blanket `-y` or `--trust` authorization, catalog fallback, arbitrary origin use and retroactive redirects. It keeps scoped grants, pre-request gates, observed-byte pins, existing authenticated-provider authority and closed noninteractive behavior.

decisions.title: Choose the public owner for one shared core.tui session
decisions.gist: Should a managed call or a retained handle own one complete TUI session?
decisions.lesson: Jet already has the typed program, widgets, bindings, layout, commands, and terminal guard in source. The new boundary must publish one owner without a second tree, editor, focus, task, or renderer. A publishes only managed tui.run; B publishes only the retained session API. Both run the same task-list program.
decisions.story: Maya needs a task list with editable text, focus, a scrolling table, Save, and keyboard shortcuts. The same Model, Msg, update, view, and adapt code must run in a TTY and produce one deterministic non-TTY frame. The choice is only who owns the session lifecycle.
decisions.inWild: Bubble Tea v2 shows the useful run-owned shape: one model, update, view, event handling, command work, and Run result. That prior art does not settle Jet state, effect, cleanup, NO_COLOR, or mouse laws. The Jet fixture below covers those requirements.

options.name: Managed tui.run only
options.detail: A publishes one managed `tui.run` entry. The implementation may use a private session, but Jet code cannot name or retain it. The call owns first paint, normalized input, update, FIFO commands, redraw, non-TTY output, and cleanup. It returns `TuiResult<M>` and moves the final model directly.
options.technical: A uses the common callbacks `fn(M, Msg) (M, TuiCommand<Msg>) !TuiError`, `fn(M) UiNode`, and `fn(TuiEvent) ?Msg !TuiError`. Direct callback effects use D-EFF2 flow-through. `TuiCommand.Task(fn() Msg)` remains under the existing structured task scope. No public `TuiSession`, `tui.session`, driver, transport, configuration, or effect-row syntax is added.

options.name: Retained tui.session only
options.detail: B publishes `tui.session` and `TuiSession` lifecycle methods. `session.run()` borrows the handle, runs the real loop and returns only `TuiExit`. `frame()` inspects the last semantic frame. Idempotent `close()` restores the terminal. `finish(^self)` closes if needed and moves the model exactly once. No top-level `tui.run` exists.
options.technical: B uses the same callbacks, event, action, widget, task, cleanup, NO_COLOR, and non-TTY contracts as A. Stored callbacks and stored `Task` values use D-EFF2 maximal effects unless an existing `fn(…) -[E]>` bound applies. No public transport, raw-byte driver, second renderer, or generic model copy exists.

comparisons.note: Ratatui's Terminal::draw renders one semantic frame while the application handles typed terminal events and restoration.
comparisons.code:
terminal.draw(|frame| render(frame, &app))?;
app.update(event);

comparisons.note: Bubble Tea's NewProgram(model).Run() owns the application loop around model updates, views, commands, and cleanup.
comparisons.code:
p := tea.NewProgram(model)
finalModel, err := p.Run()

comparisons.note: crossterm's MouseEvent carries kind, column, row, and modifiers before application mapping.

recommendation.why: A gives the common interactive app one complete owner while keeping the implementation session private.
gains: One public call owns first paint, events, commands, redraw, and cleanup.
The direct callback path preserves normal effect flow-through.

losses.loss: A has no public handle for stepping or retained frame inspection.
losses.mitigation: A publishes only tui.run; B is the retained-session choice.

whyNot.reason: B is viable for inspection, but its retained lifecycle adds ceremony to the common one-run path.

recommendation.tradeoff: A chooses the shortest complete entry and gives up public retained-session control.

Future focused proof, not run here: run the same fixture under default JIT, --interpret, --release/AOT, and jet dev. Compare normalized event order, atomic mouse transitions, command completion, frames, exits, errors, and restoration.

decisions.title: What should authenticate a Nix reconstruction plan?
decisions.gist: What should authenticate a Nix reconstruction plan?
decisions.lesson: The signed narinfo already authenticates the final uncompressed NAR and its references. A reconstruction plan is a way to obtain those same bytes, not a new package identity. Choose bounded untrusted hints, index-committed plans, or co-published signed sidecars; none may admit a different output.
decisions.story: An updated tool changes its executable but keeps manuals and icons. Jet already holds verified old units. All options must obtain the same selected new output and closure while transferring only useful missing data when that route wins.
decisions.inWild: Debian apt-secure authenticates release/index metadata and committed package checksums. This is an authentication-chain comparison, not a claimed delta implementation. Primary source: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-secure.8.en.html.
decisions.detail:
This ballot chooses authority only; file-sized versus content-defined units is selected by matched measurements, not by taste. All options use one bounded assembler and the existing atomic closure admission.

Canonical output law: represent only lossless NAR semantics—raw path components and symlink-target bytes, directory/regular/symlink kind, the executable marker and file contents. Restore with the same mode normalization and sealing order as whole-NAR decoding. Do not add semantic hardlink edges, xattrs, ownership/timestamps or extra mode bits that NAR does not represent. Equal regular-file contents still need the same independent-inode semantics as baseline; reflinks may share storage, not change the tree identity. Never follow a created symlink while writing later entries.

Authentication law: configured-key narinfo binds StorePath, canonical uncompressed NarHash, NarSize and References. Unit digests check content integrity, not publisher identity. Before publication, recompute canonical NAR bytes/hash/size, then the normal sealed Hangar output/closure identity. Preserve direct/transitive references and existing producer/cache/transaction law. Original compression/URL/FileHash/FileSize are observed transport metadata, not signed narinfo identity. A delta path that does not read the original compressed stream must not claim to verify its FileHash or compressed size.

Resource and privacy law: cap manifest/node/part counts, declared lengths, total work, decompression, temporary disk and requests before/during work. Query only verified admitted units in the explicit authorized reuse scope; do not turn remote hints into probes of private/unrelated CAS membership or send a cache inventory. Use derived configured-endpoint paths and existing network pin/redirect rules. Invalid present metadata or corrupt units fail with no publication. No invalid-plan fallback or weakening of local/unofficial versus official trust rules.

Economic law: estimate manifest plus missing encoded-unit bytes, requests, assembly cost and resource use per selected output. Skip plan acquisition when the known reuse scope cannot make it useful. Choose whole NAR when a valid plan is uneconomic; that is planning, not an integrity-error fallback. Count already-paid plan overhead in the receipt. A fallback or bounded regression is never called a delta win. Preregister required rows/metrics and thresholds; every required strict win remains mandatory under Jet policy, and any failed/unavailable/inconclusive row keeps the card open.

Publishing law: #2200 owns endpoint/DNS/TLS/static hosting and trust-root setup. B/C co-publish complete immutable generations; no late sidecar mutation. A stays within the existing endpoint/immutability contract rather than quietly adding a dynamic host. Host-private cache-role HMAC is not a public signing option.

Sources: Nar.rs:232-259; NixCache.rs:1238-1298,707-850; NixIndex.rs OutputWire; Envelope.rs canonical entry identity; docs/spec/packaging/index-cache.md and trust-root.md. Primary comparison: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-secure.8.en.html.

options.name: Use signed NAR identity; treat plans as hints
options.detail: No new plan signature or signed-index schema is required. The plan is non-authoritative and cannot publish content or query unrelated private cache state.
options.code:
verify configured-key narinfo for the selected output
read a bounded reconstruction hint
reuse only authorized, verified local units
fetch and verify missing units
require canonical NarHash and NarSize to match
admit through the existing closure transaction
options.technical:
Reuse CacheEndpoint::narinfo/verified_signature: its authenticated fingerprint binds StorePath, canonical uncompressed NarHash, NarSize and References. Bind the selected index record/output to that StorePath before consuming a plan. A same-endpoint, bounded hint may carry or accompany those already verified facts but does not authenticate itself, the compressed stream, arbitrary URLs or local CAS membership. Node/unit limits, path rules, byte/decompression/time budgets and authorized-candidate scope apply before/during all work.

Only prior authenticated/admitted units in the explicitly authorized package/update reuse scope may be queried; do not probe unrelated or private CAS objects and do not send an inventory. Derived object paths stay under configured endpoints with existing pinned-address/redirect policy. Newly fetched units remain staged until complete canonical NAR/closure verification. A missing hint permits the normal whole-NAR path but is not authenticated proof of absent coverage; a present malformed or integrity-invalid hint fails.

Final signed output identity is authoritative.

options.name: Commit each output plan in the signed index
options.detail: Add an optional plan descriptor to each OutputWire, not one digest shared by a multi-output record. No separate plan signature is needed.
options.code:
verify the signed index target
read the selected OutputWire plan descriptor
require its digest to match the fetched plan
verify configured-key narinfo and missing units
require the same canonical NAR and closure identity
admit through the existing transaction
options.technical:
Each named OutputWire carries an explicit absent descriptor or a digest/length/format descriptor for its own canonical plan. The plan binds stable record/output identity and the signed narinfo fields, but not the enclosing index digest: otherwise index->plan->index would cycle. Publish descriptors and objects atomically in one complete immutable index generation. A descriptor that commits presence cannot fall back on a missing, altered or invalid plan; an authenticated absent descriptor selects whole NAR.

Reuse all common bounds, privacy, canonical NAR and closure laws. The existing pinned index key authenticates metadata; existing configured Nix keys still authenticate narinfo. No host-private HMAC becomes a public publisher credential.

options.name: Co-publish a separately signed output sidecar
options.detail: This keeps the current index record schema while adding a domain-separated sidecar signature and exact generation/output binding.
options.code:
verify the index generation and selected output
verify its co-published delta sidecar signature
verify configured-key narinfo and missing units
require the same canonical NAR and closure identity
admit through the existing transaction
options.technical:
Define a canonical domain-separated signature under the existing pinned index key for each generation/output sidecar. Bind the exact generation, stable selected record/output, signed NarHash/NarSize/References and node/part table. Co-publish it atomically with a complete immutable index root; never add or replace a sidecar inside a published generation. Its address includes generation/output identity. Drop the previous claim that it can appear later without new publication.

Present unsigned/wrong-key/invalid sidecars fail; absence can select whole NAR but is unauthenticated and susceptible to stripping unless a future separately approved coverage commitment exists. No such extra coverage mechanism is assumed here.

comparisons.note: Debian apt-secure authenticates release/index metadata and committed package checksums. This is an authentication-chain comparison, not a claimed delta implementation. Primary source: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/apt/apt-secure.8.en.html.
comparisons.code:
apt-get update
apt-get download ripgrep
# Authenticated repository metadata supplies
# the checksum for the acquired package.

recommendation.why: A is sufficient for output authenticity because the existing signed canonical NarHash remains the admission gate. Explicit resource and cache-privacy limits contain the untrusted hint. Start without another signing mechanism unless authenticated coverage or early plan authority is required.
gains: Reuses the existing output signature and closure authority.
Avoids an extra signing format and signed-index schema change.

losses.loss: A bad or stripped hint can waste bounded work or force full transfer.
losses.mitigation: The signature authenticates final output, not hint availability. Resource and privacy bounds cannot prove coverage.

whyNot.reason: Choose B when authenticated coverage is required. It changes each output record and binds coverage to index publication.
C adds signatures and publication work without authenticated absence. Keeping the record schema does not remove that cost.

recommendation.tradeoff: A minimizes authority machinery. B authenticates planning and coverage early. C preserves the record schema but adds signatures and still permits availability downgrade.

decisions.checkInstructions: Future proof only: exercise the ratified authority branch, bounded/privacy-scoped reconstruction, canonical NAR/Hangar/closure parity and all failure/atomicity paths. Compare file and chunk candidates with the same whole-NAR output across preregistered reuse/workload rows and all required metrics; report every paid metadata byte and do not count fallback as a win. No runtime or performance proof was run during preparation.

decisions.designAway: First test whether a new authority mechanism is needed: signed canonical NarHash already prevents wrong output admission. decisions.title: Make repeat audits leave checkable answer evidence
decisions.gist: Make expected answers and rerun evidence explicit in the existing conformance audit?
decisions.lesson: A contract audit checks Jet against approved rules. The existing skill already runs programs and examines their behavior. This change makes reports state the expected answer and explain whether a rerun tested the same cases. Two ways of running Jet can agree on a wrong answer.
decisions.explainer: The same map-extrema job anchors all options: values 2 and 10 require min=2 and max=10. The retained historical failure was min=10 and max=2 on one comptime library path. A strengthens the existing instruction file and performs a bounded method trial; B records the method and trial plan only; C changes nothing. The existing audit already checks approved rules. This addition standardizes what answer evidence and rerun changes must be visible, without a new runner or report format.
decisions.story: A retained comptime map case returned min=10 and max=2 for numeric values 2 and 10. That is historical evidence, not a new run or a claim about every execution mode. A synthetic multi-mode copy of that wrong answer tests whether an audit mistakes agreement for correctness.

options.technical:
Authorize edits only to .agents/skills/spec-compliance-audit/SKILL.md and one bounded trial of that method. No router change is needed for this already-routed skill.

Within scope, cite the approved rule and list its required behaviors. Distinguish source reading from program execution. Establish an independent expected observable. Consume and check returned values. For non-value behavior, check its diagnostic, exit, effect, state transition or artifact. Match records by behavior, input and execution mode, not prose wording. Keep added or removed coverage separate from fixed, recurring or regressed behavior. A mode not exercised is unmeasured, not passing. Reuse existing records and formats;

do not require a duplicate report table when those facts are already present.

Use the retained numeric-map case from docs/audits/mine-for-jet-2026-09-10.md F2. Numeric values 2 and 10 require min=2, max=10. The historical comptime result was min=10, max=2, not proof of every public execution path. Before execution, freeze this finite matrix at an exact revision: the retained production comptime-library path, public AOT, default jet run, interpreter and web. The pure numeric operation is relevant to each. Absent interfaces, unsupported hosts, failed builds and explicit gates remain recorded missing/unmeasured rows.

Do not remove or substitute their workload. Use the corresponding existing entry point, recording the exact command/API before any trial row runs. Each row receives a disposition. Add exactly one declared adjacent case, values [-1, 2, 10] with expected min=-1/max=10, to those same rows. Stop after the two cases and named matrix have dispositions; do not start another audit campaign.

Feed the method a clearly synthetic bundle in which two modes both report the wrong min/max; it must reject the shared wrong answer. A matching valid bundle must pass that narrow answer check. A changed-case rerun must be reported as changed coverage, not a fix. Preserve actual current run results, including a repaired result, failure or unavailability.

The existing skill already checks conformance and keeps its status vocabulary and live-probe duties. Add no product fix, syntax change, runner, schema, ledger or second report owner. This method's report cannot approve a release or replace verify.

The controller keeps the expected dispositions separate from the trial prompt and relabels synthetic records. The reviewer must derive correctness from the approved numeric rule, not repeat a record labelled wrong.

Missing or unmeasured evidence does not add a status: use the existing shipped/partial/gap/gated/declined/stale-doc vocabulary as justified, recording the missing evidence in the finding. An affected behavior cannot be marked shipped or support a broad clean verdict without its required observations. The report can still complete with non-shipped findings.

The source-edit restriction does not forbid required evidence outputs. A also authorizes one ordinary method-trial report at docs/audits/conformance-method-trial-<run-id>.md and its bounded disk-backed scratch artifacts under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch. Use the existing report form and Tower Docs registration, not a new format or work ledger. Do not overwrite historical reports.

decisions.title: Make routine work easy in Jet, in the library or compiler
decisions.gist: Should audits seek the best Jet-owned solution, including compiler improvements that earn their place?
decisions.lesson: This changes agent instructions, not Jet itself. Routine jobs should work through bundled CoreLib or Jet-owned libraries, without foreign-library setup. Library code is not automatically the best answer. Repeated boilerplate can justify better compiler support. The JSON example uses existing Jet features; this ballot does not invent another parser.
decisions.explainer:
A skill is an instruction file for an agent. This ballot improves an existing practical-use audit. It does not choose a new JSON API or authorize a compiler feature.

Start with Jet’s bundled CoreLib and first-party libraries. Needing foreign bindings for an ordinary application is an out-of-the-box shortcoming, not proof that Jet already handles the job well. A useful domain capability may belong in Jet’s own library offering even when the compiler mechanisms already exist.

Also look for repeated boilerplate, awkward patterns and work the compiler could safely remove. An implementation in a library does not settle that comparison. Library and compiler support may work together, as the existing typed-JSON example illustrates. Recommend a compiler improvement when the same-job evidence supports its performance, usability or clarity benefit. Preserve safety and explicit expert control.

The fixed example reads {"port":8080} into Settings and prints 8080. Replacing 8080 with the string "bad" must be rejected rather than silently accepted. Existing sources: examples/features/serde/json_typed.jet and examples/features/serde/json.jet. These sources establish the example pattern, not a fresh execution claim.
decisions.story: A developer reads application settings. Jet should handle the routine work directly. The audit asks whether its own libraries and compiler make the program easy to read, write and understand.
decisions.inWild:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html
import json
settings = json.loads('{"port":8080}')
if type(settings["port"]) is not int:
    raise ValueError("port must be an integer")
print(settings["port"])  # 8080
decisions.detail: Update the existing practical-use audit to seek a complete Jet-owned solution. Routine users should not have to assemble foreign libraries and bindings. Keep compiler changes eligible when repeated patterns or boilerplate reveal a better experience. Judge the actual program, not a library-versus-compiler slogan.

options.technical:
Authorize updates only to .agents/skills/pragmatism-audit/SKILL.md and one bounded method trial. No product feature, package, dependency or router change is approved. Preserve the existing report-only workflow and friction vocabulary.

Judge the complete Jet-owned path for each requested job. Prefer bundled CoreLib and first-party Jet libraries for routine capabilities. A foreign package, hand-written binding or FFI wrapper does not count as the desired out-of-the-box solution. Explicit external integration remains possible for users who actually need it; this instruction does not ban interoperability.

If a common capability is absent, consider a Jet-owned library or CoreLib addition. Do not confuse adequate compiler mechanisms with an adequate standard offering. Existing dependency and owner-approval rules remain binding; this ballot approves no new bootstrap dependency.

Repeated patterns, boilerplate and awkward code are signals to investigate compiler improvements. Do not require a library solution to be impossible first. Compare the best credible Jet-library solution with the compiler-supported alternative on the same complete job. Consider measured performance, setup, readability, writing effort, reasoning, error behavior, safety and expert control. A combined library/compiler solution is allowed; the categories are not exclusive.

Neither fewer characters nor repetition alone proves a feature worthwhile. Preserve required semantics and safety. Keep unmeasured benefits unknown. Performance-motivated proposals need the standing matched-program gate before ratification; other compiler proposals also require their normal owner approval. The audit recommends changes but does not implement them.

The bounded trial uses exactly the example and inputs in the explainer, through default jet run. It checks the revised method, not every execution mode or domain. Record which support exists and whether any further improvement is justified. No invented compiler gap is needed for the trial to finish. If setup fails, retain that non-result rather than substituting a foreign library.

Keep one ordinary report under docs/audits/jet-owned-workload-method-trial-<run-id>.md, with isolated proof files under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch. Use current report and Tower Docs registration conventions. Do not overwrite retained reports or add a runner, schema or work ledger.

decisions.title: Add a controlled first-attempt and repair trial
decisions.gist: Add an optional controlled trial to persona-audit, without slowing ordinary persona work?
decisions.lesson: Persona-audit gives representative user profiles real Jet projects and reports completion and friction. A participant here is a fresh coding agent, not a recruited person. The optional trial preserves its first submitted program, then measures one repair under fixed help rules. A correct duplicate-field error is success; recovery means fixing a program that mishandled that case.
decisions.explainer:
The retained fixture is docs/audits/raw/2393-r2/fixtures.json, T1. This is preregistered task data, not participant evidence. The program reads its first argument and resolves one-level inheritance while preserving section order and first field appearance. It must compute from input rather than hardcode these outputs.

records.cfg (including its final newline):
[base]
name = "Ada"
role = "admin"
[dev]
inherits = "base"
role = "reviewer"

records-failure.cfg (including its final newline):
[base]
name = "Ada"
name = "Grace"

Success argv after the executable: ["records.cfg"]. Required stdout, including the final newline:
base.name=Ada
base.role=admin
dev.name=Ada
dev.role=reviewer

Failure argv: ["records-failure.cfg"]. Require nonzero exit, empty stdout and a diagnostic identifying duplicate field name in section base. The retained checker searches duplicate and base; the stronger written task also requires the field name. Preserve that distinction rather than treating the weaker checker as the full task.
decisions.story: A first program may print a partial configuration instead of rejecting a duplicate name. The controller preserves that failure, supplies the allowed result feedback, then checks whether the agent repairs the program. A passing checker alone does not establish correct output.

C leaves the existing project, repairability and preference observations unchanged. No option recruits humans or resumes the full #2393 comparative campaign. The initial one-agent, one-language pilot cannot establish population success, cross-language preference or release readiness.

Without frozen help and retained first attempts, controlled-study results are unavailable.

options.technical:
Authorize edits only to .agents/skills/persona-audit/SKILL.md and one isolated coding-agent pilot. No router change is required. Use the controlled branch only when the request explicitly asks for a controlled cold-session, repair, assistance or preference study. Ordinary repairability or preference observations do not trigger it. Otherwise ordinary persona work remains the default and collects no controlled-trial paperwork.

Initial pilot: one fresh OMP @implementation agent on the existing Linux CLI host, using the currently configured profile without model substitution. Record its exact resolved provider/model/settings. Use the retained T1 bytes and argument vectors in the explainer. Freeze the fresh Jet binary identity, task/prompt, allowlisted current documentation, tools, limits and expected outputs before the agent starts. A explicitly delegates selection of that bounded documentation set to the implementer; B is the option for reviewing those details first.

Capture or content-address every resolved harness-delivered role, system, project, skill and injected context instruction before launch; those inputs are part of the help boundary. Record later injected messages and treat unapproved help changes as loss of controlled status. If that delivered context cannot be observed and frozen, the controlled-help result is unavailable. This promises control of observable harness inputs, not access to opaque provider internals or control of model training. No historical participant solutions, transcripts or audit answers may enter the first session.

Use a fresh disk-backed task workspace and program-artifact state under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch, while retaining the shared bounded compiler Cargo target. The agent may read the frozen task/input/help and write its task program. It submits the first complete program before receiving any compiler or run feedback; preserve its exact source. The controller then checks it against the frozen success and duplicate cases. Permit at most one repair submission, with only raw compiler/run results and expected-versus-actual differences as feedback, not suggested code.

Keep the input and expected results immutable. Each submission has a 15-minute limit. Missing profile, fresh session, required tool or verifiable help boundary makes the pilot unavailable rather than silently changing it. The transcript establishes adherence to the declared help policy; this is not a security sandbox claim.

Keep first-attempt success under that help policy, checker result, independent semantic output, refusal, first failure, repair and post-task comments separate. Hardcoded fixture output is not task success. Preserve the stronger duplicate-field requirement even if the existing checker misses it. A passing checker with wrong bytes or an unnamed duplicate is a failed semantic result. A program that already handles both cases needs no forced failure or repair. If it fails and the repaired program passes both, report repaired success without erasing the first failure.

A refusal, timeout or unavailable run is not a poor language score or a successful trial.

Record the actual supported command paths and outputs; do not infer unrun modes. Post-task comments from one Jet arm are usability observations, not earned cross-language preference. A does not waive any #2393 gate, authorize its full rerun, recruit humans, create a runner or ledger, edit product code, or issue a release verdict. Missing controlled setup blocks only this branch and claims requiring it; ordinary persona observations remain available.

The source-edit restriction does not forbid required evidence outputs. A also authorizes one ordinary method-trial report at docs/audits/persona-controlled-t1-method-trial-<run-id>.md and its bounded disk-backed scratch artifacts under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch. Use the existing report form and Tower Docs registration, not a new format or work ledger. Do not overwrite historical reports.

decisions.title: Check evidence with existing skills instead of adding another
decisions.gist: Should we strengthen existing evidence reviews instead of adding another skill?
decisions.lesson: An evidence review asks what saved observations actually prove. A correct result needs the matching program and tool versions, the unedited output, and an expected answer established independently. This proposal routes the question to an existing skill; it does not grant that skill authority to approve a release.
decisions.explainer:
Shared synthetic example, not observed Jet results: the claim is that current program P1, artifact B1 built with tool T1, returns numeric minimum 2 for input values [2, 10]. P1/B1/T1/I1 are readable labels for exact source/artifact/tool/input identities in this example; a real review must carry the actual recorded identities, not these labels. The expected answer follows independent numeric ordering, not the tested implementation. R1: matching P1/B1/T1/I1, retained raw stdout "2\n", independent expectation 2.

Supports this case only. R2: old P0/B0/T1/I1, raw "2\n". Stale for P1; supports P0 only if a separately identified P0 claim, artifact B0, tool T1, input I1, independent expectation and raw record match. Otherwise insufficient. R3: a copied representation of R1. Counts as the same observation once, not a second run. R4: the test tool crashed before completion. Supports only that failed attempt, not correctness. R5: the requested execution path was unavailable and never ran. Unmeasured, not passing.

R6: matching P1/B1/T1/I1, raw "10\n", checker says PASS because its expected-answer source incorrectly says 10. This is an intentionally wrong answer accepted by a broken checker. Reject the correctness claim and identify the faulty expectation; preserve the raw failure evidence.
decisions.story: A supplied bundle may contain a valid result, an old result, a duplicate copy, a crashed check, a check that never ran, or a wrong answer marked green. Their value differs; none should be averaged into one green verdict.
decisions.inWild:
# Same example claim: numeric minimum of [2, 10] is 2.
# stryker-mutator.io/docs/mutation-testing-elements/mutant-states-and-metrics/
A deliberately changed program returns the wrong answer.
Test rejects it -> the test noticed this bug.
Test accepts it -> the test missed this bug.
Tool crashes -> no result for this check.
decisions.detail: A installs a retrospective evidence-review procedure in existing research guidance and updates the existing router. B writes a standalone-skill design and a future comparison protocol, without running or installing it. C changes nothing. Each option concerns the same six-record example in the explainer. The preparation has not tested any skill on that bundle. Old and copied evidence is narrowed to what it supports, not deleted.

options.name: Strengthen existing reviews
options.detail: Route by the requested verdict: verify for closeout, spec-compliance-audit for ratified rules, existing specialists for their verdicts, research only for retrospective evidence adequacy. Install that guidance now. Keep the useful narrow meaning of old and copied records. Expose wrong answers accepted by a broken checker. Keep security and competitive checks with their existing owners. Research instructions and the existing routing entry must remain aligned.
options.code:
Ask: what does this unchanged-tree R1-R6 bundle prove?
Route to research; this is not code-closeout approval.
Keep R1 narrow, R2 stale for P1 and conditional for P0, R3 counted once.
Report R4 failed, R5 unmeasured, R6 wrong despite green.
Install the guidance and exercise this example.
options.technical:
Authorize edits only to .agents/skills/research/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/JetSkillsRouter.md, plus a bounded exercise of the method. The research change adds retrospective review of supplied records; the router maps the subject to its existing owner. It does not change approval authority.

Choose one primary owner by the requested verdict, not the fact that records were supplied. Current code/card/milestone/release closeout goes to verify, which retains its specialist prerequisites. Codebase-versus-ratified-law goes to spec-compliance-audit; a fixed-diff review goes to code-review. A security qualification or competitive qualification request stays with its existing security-closure workflow or gauntlet. Research receives only the standalone retrospective question of what supplied records prove, without issuing any of those verdicts.

If a request also asks for current approval, that outcome-specific owner takes precedence over research. A user makes one natural-language request; no new command, skill name or generic coordinator is added.

Use existing evidence records and test-economics normalization where applicable. For each claim, inspect exact program/build/tool/input identity; raw unedited output; an expected-answer source independent of the tested implementation; test-machinery failure; and whether the requested check ran at all. A wrong expected-answer source is a broken oracle. Do not count a copied representation as another observation. An old record is stale for the current claim; it supports an older claim only when that separate claim and all required evidence match.

A failed or unavailable check supports a non-result, not a correctness claim. Retain those narrow meanings and provenance instead of discarding the evidence.

Exercise the shared R1-R6 bundle. Keep R1's narrow observation and conditional P0 support for R2; R2 is stale for P1. R3 is one representation of R1. R4 is failed machinery; R5 is unmeasured. R6 is a wrong answer falsely accepted by a bad expectation. These are bounded installation checks using existing forms, not a new maintained fixture suite or runner. The instructions and router entry are the two durable maintenance surfaces.

No schema, ledger, product edit, second report owner, security bypass or release approval is authorized.

For the method exercise, the controller relabels the records and retains the expected dispositions separately. Keep the exact six records, identities and [2, 10] values from the explainer; hide only display labels and the answer table, never alter the selected job. The reviewer receives the claim and records, not an answer-labelled control table.

R2 supports a separately identified P0 claim only when that claim, identity, input, independent expectation and raw record match; without those facts it is insufficient for either claim. R1 supports the narrow observation that one matching run returned 2. R6 blocks a broad correctness claim; a passing observation cannot average away the wrong one.

The source-edit restriction does not forbid required evidence outputs. A also authorizes one ordinary method-trial report at docs/research/evidence-adequacy-method-trial-<run-id>.md and its bounded disk-backed scratch artifacts under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch. Use the existing report form and Tower Docs registration, not a new format or work ledger. Do not overwrite historical reports.

Require an additional detected weakness or improved repeatability without losing correct narrow conclusions before recommending installation.

This is a proposal criterion, not automatic permission: the comparison run, skill installation and router activation each remain outside B and require later explicit owner authorization. Current owners remain unchanged. The controller retains the expected-disposition table separately and gives both future reviewers the same unlabelled records and claim. Neither receives the ballot/design answer labels. Freeze all six identities and contents; only display labels may change.

decisions.title: Select values or safe borrowed records without raw positions
decisions.gist: Should top-k offer owned values and checked borrowed views, instead of raw positions?
decisions.lesson: Top-k selects the smallest or largest k items. Owned results are independent values. Borrowed views let you inspect original records without copying them. Jet prevents changes that would invalidate a live view. The stream path consumes input only when you explicitly pass an owning iterator. These are proposed methods, not shipped features.
decisions.explainer:
The ordinary job is unchanged: [9,1,5,3,7] produces [1,3,5], its third result is 5, and the source order stays unchanged. A adds a second explicit result choice. smallest_views returns a normal List of one-item View windows into the source. A view is a checked borrow, not an independent record or an integer position.

For records with those scores, smallest_views_by(3, r -> r.score) selects views of the same three records without copying them. The caller reads fields through those views. Existing provenance checks keep the source alive and reject changes that could invalidate a later view use. Permitted disjoint writes do not re-run selection; the result is not a live sorted query.

An independent value result still copies selected payloads. Borrowing avoids that copy by keeping the source available. Moving instead of copying is an explicit expert choice through an owning Iter, such as values.lazy(). Its terminal consumes that source. Bound an infinite stream before asking for an exact answer; do not silently choose a cutoff.

This replaces the raw-position recommendation, not Jet’s general indexes operation. Stable mutable identities such as Pool Id are separate existing contracts, not another top-k feature here. Current rank and extrema behavior remain unchanged.

Current lowering still copies a record during a direct indexed field read. A therefore includes compiler work so picked[2][0].score borrows the record and reads its score without copying the record. Existing fold/map callbacks already borrow, but requiring that workaround would not meet this proposal.
decisions.story: Nora wants the three smallest values while keeping the original List. For large or move-only records, she wants to inspect the same selected records without copying them or tracking fragile positions.
decisions.inWild:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/heapq.html#heapq.nsmallest
from heapq import nsmallest
values = [9, 1, 5, 3, 7]
print(nsmallest(3, values))  # [1, 3, 5]
print(values)                # unchanged
decisions.detail: A proposes owned values, checked borrowed List views and explicitly consuming Iter results from one algorithm. The borrowed result removes the top-k position bookkeeping and payload-copy requirement. It uses existing View lifetime and mutation checks. C retains current full-sort composition. Neither choice claims a speed win or approves public adoption. A also includes the compiler change required for direct borrowed record-field reads.

options.technical:
Status: proposed only. It is not shipped and reserves no public method name.

The value-first family has these proposed forms on List and existing owning `Iter<T>`:

- `[T].smallest(n: Int) [T]` and `[T].largest(n: Int) [T]`.
- `[T].smallest_by(n: Int, key: fn(item: T) K) [T]` and `[T].largest_by(n: Int, key: fn(item: T) K) [T]`.
- Fallible keyed forms return `[T] !E` with the same names and key shape.

On a List, `T` must be cloneable because the receiver remains owned and unchanged while the selected result becomes independent storage. Only selected payloads are materialized at that result boundary. The candidate state retains indexes and order keys, not a second copy of every losing payload. Positive calls inspect the List without mutation. `n == 0` returns `[]` before reads, key calls or candidate work. `n < 0` reports the existing `sequence count must be nonnegative` error before reads.

Counts at least the length return every selected value in the requested order.

On an existing owning `Iter<T>`, the same terminal names and key forms have no `Clone` bound. The terminal consumes its owner by the existing Iter terminal contract. It retains at most `min(n, m)` candidate entries for an input of length `m`, moves selected payloads into the independent result, and drops losing entries. A positive finite call reads through exhaustion because a later item can displace any candidate. An infinite source does not become a bounded-read operation;

the terminal does not promise to return unless the source ends. For `n == 0`, it pulls no items and calls no key, then consumes and drops the owner. A negative count fails before pulling, while the terminal still owns and consumes its receiver.

Add named List siblings: `[T].smallest_views(n: Int) [View<T>]` and `largest_views`, plus `smallest_views_by(n: Int, key: fn(item: T) K)` and `largest_views_by`. Their fallible keyed forms return `[View<T>] !E`. These methods preserve the List and require no Clone bound on payload T. Each selected View contains exactly one source item.

Values, views and owning Iter results share candidate selection, tie, count and error rules. List candidate descriptors retain source locations and comparison keys, not copied payloads. Owned results materialize selected payloads only. View results construct existing borrowed windows from selected source locations. Never expose those internal locations as a top-k position API.

Track receiver provenance through the returned `[View<T>]`, wrappers and aggregate returns. Reuse existing local-owner escape and overlapping mutation checks. Prevent source moves, storage changes and reorderings that could invalidate a later view use. Disjoint writes permitted by existing checks do not cause automatic re-ranking. Do not add a selection carrier, stable-identity promise, lifetime mechanism or runtime permission bypass.

List callbacks read stable receiver storage. Both List result families accept owned keys and the existing List-only borrowed-key shape `View<V> from _0`, including `View<str>`. Retain only candidate key descriptors; no forced text-key copies. Release temporary borrowed keys before publishing result windows or owned values. Returned item views are rooted in the receiver, not leaked callback key views.

Unary keys run exactly once per encountered item in source order. Owning Iter keys remain owned because candidate payloads move. No pinning, self-referential storage, borrowed key into moving payloads or raw reference escape is introduced.

A fallible key stops at the first exact error. On a List, prior callback effects remain, no later key runs, temporary keys and candidates are released, the List is unchanged and no partial result is published. On an owning Iter, the consumed prefix cannot be rewound; candidates and keys are released, prior effects remain and no partial result is published. A borrowed key view must be rooted in the item and cannot escape through a result, retained closure or later callback.

Its lifetime ends before the item is moved or the source alias is released.

The requested stable relation is ascending for `smallest` and descending for `largest`. NaNs follow non-NaNs for smallest and precede them for largest. All NaNs tie, and signed zeros tie. Equal keys keep source order, including the cutoff. At count one, both directions keep the first source item among equal extrema. The family must not delegate to current `min`, `max`, `min_by` or `max_by` when their equal-key rules differ.

Candidate storage, selected output storage and any key allocation are real costs. They are bounded and visible. The design does not claim a speed result. Existing owning Iter construction is separate from List `lazy`: there is no `List.iter` method. Where an already owning vector is wrapped with `jet_iter_from_vec`, the runtime uses `into_iter()` and the terminal moves items rather than cloning each payload. This does not authorize an undocumented List-to-Iter copy path.

List views use the same zero/negative-before-read rules as List values and return no partial result on error. Only the returned View headers and their normal List storage are allocated for borrowed output; payloads are not cloned. Retained candidate keys, output headers, selected copies and iterator construction remain measured costs.

All Iter top-k methods remain proposed; the owning Iter type and lazy/take operations already exist. The caller explicitly passes an owning source. For an unbounded stream, an explicit finite take defines the input prefix. Exact top-k of the original infinite stream still has no completion guarantee. No automatic cutoff or hidden collection is allowed.

Use matched owned-value, borrowed-view and owning-Iter full-sort baselines with the same keys, source and observable result. Private reference helpers may construct existing View windows; they introduce no public baseline API. A redundant full-list-copy baseline alone is insufficient. Do not add smallest_indexes or require callers to manage raw positions. Public adoption and performance claims need their separate gates.

Fix the general borrowed field-projection path needed by `picked[2][0].score`; do not special-case top-k or require a fold workaround. Current Field/Index lowering calls `jet_index_vec<T: Clone>` before field projection. Preserve a checked borrowed place through record field access instead. Copy only the requested field when its value contract requires copying. Keep bounds errors, evaluation order, effects, ownership checks and meaning across applicable tiers unchanged. Demonstrate direct scalar field reads from actual move-only records.

Existing View construction alone does not prove this behavior.

Apply the canonical strict gate to every required paired cell and metric: prototype/plain must be below 1.00. For peer comparisons, Jet/Rust may be at most 1.05; every non-Rust Jet/peer ratio must be below 1.00. Missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. Never average away losses. A performance card and public adoption remain open while any required cell fails.

Register receiver-rooted return_view_provenance for the [] result-element slot of every plain, keyed and fallible smallest_views* and largest_views* method. A [View<T>] return type alone is insufficient. Feed that provenance into the existing aggregate escape and owner-change checks, including wrappers and forwarded results.

options.technical:
Status: current operations only; no new helper or prototype.

Use the visible position-sort recipe: collect values.indexes(), sort those integers by the corresponding value/key, then take the requested positions and materialize only selected payloads. An owned value result still requires cloneable T. For move-only records, keep selected positions and construct existing one-item range views for borrowed callback reads while the source stays live and structurally unchanged. For example, records[i..i].fold(0, (a, r) -> a + r.score) reads a score without cloning the record.

Direct indexed field reads still need the compiler fix proposed by A. Existing public sort_by/sort_by_desc provide unary owned-key sorting or two-argument Ordering comparison; the same appropriate callback must be used on both sides of any performance pair.

This improves the old ~values; sort; take recipe, which copied all payloads twice. The new recipe never needs those full payload copies. It does build and sort every index. The existing order.lazy().take(n) path moves the temporary position list rather than cloning it. It checks n only after the preceding index collection and full sort; zero and negative counts therefore do not bypass that earlier work. Existing count errors, stable sorting, Float order and callback/error behavior remain unchanged.

No wrapper API or new preflight behavior is installed by C.

For largest use the corresponding descending stable key sort. Match key effects, owned results or checked position reads in candidate/plain evidence. Private borrowed-key baselines are separate from current public sort_by. C supplies current evidence only, not bounded-candidate or owning-iterator top-k guarantees.

For record keys, use existing borrowed-window callbacks where direct indexed field reads would clone the record. The visible Int recipe alone does not prove no-copy record handling.

decisions.checkInstructions:
Obtain fresh beginner and adversarial reviews before publication. After owner authorization, implement only the selected prototype scope.

For A, compare owned List values, borrowed List views and finite owning Iter results with matched independent full-sort references. Use [9,1,5,3,7] and records with the same scores: selected order [1,3,5], third result 5, preserved List order. Prove no payload cloning in the view path with an actual move-only record. Check direct borrowed field reads, returned aggregates, wrappers, local-owner escape, invalidating mutation before a later view use, and lawful mutation after the borrow ends.

Retain owned and List-only borrowed keys without forced key copies; Iter keys remain owned. Prove exact source-order key calls, first-error identity and prior effects, no later calls, release and no partial result. Cover empty, negative, zero, one, full, oversized and large counts; ties, NaNs, infinities, signed zeros and adversarial order. Count boundaries happen before reads/keys.

Owning Iter zero pulls nothing but consumes its owner; negative input also consumes that owner before returning the error. Finite success exhausts; a key error consumes through the failing item. Exercise an explicitly bounded stream, without claiming infinite-input termination.

Preserve same-build meaning across AOT, default run, interpreter and applicable web. Measure candidate/key/output/view-header/iterator costs only after semantic proof. C proves only current full-sort behavior, including sorting before count checks. No new top-k position API, altered extrema law or public-adoption claim is authorized.

Require direct picked[2][0].score reads on actual move-only records without copying the record. Exercise the general borrowed field-projection path outside top-k too.
