decisions.title: Publisher-required future-case fallback
decisions.gist: Should an enum publisher be able to require a fallback in downstream matches?
decisions.lesson: An enum lists named cases. A match chooses a response; else handles the remaining cases. Jet already lets callers use else. Should callers keep that choice, or may a library require it outside its own package? Both choices leave the fallback response with the caller.
decisions.story: Nora publishes a library. A later release adds a mode. She wants users to choose whether a new mode should break complete handling or flow to a fallback.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

A preserves current law. B adds one marker only on exported enum declarations, not fields, variants or arbitrary types. Empty groups remain illegal. Package identity follows existing visibility rules. B is a source-compatibility contract: downstream matching requires an explicit else; the defining package does not. Known cases can still be listed, but all-known coverage never removes the required else.

No implied wire catch-all, arbitrary integer validity, dynamic extension, stable discriminant or cross-version ABI guarantee exists. Removing the marker is a compatibility change. The marker choice is independent of D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1.

### Read the program before choosing

An enum names a fixed set of cases. A Mode value chooses one case. The function label receives that value and returns text. In fn label(m: Mode) String, m names the input and String names the text result. The construct if m == { ... } chooses a matching arm. An arm has a pattern, then ->, then its result. .Write names a case. else covers cases not selected by earlier arms.

A package is a group of files released together. The provider package declares Mode. The consumer package imports that declaration. Here mode_lib/package.jet declares the provider named modes. app/package.jet lists modes as a dependency at ../mode_lib. use modes imports it. pub enum exposes Mode outside its defining package. Two files in one package are not this boundary.

The A and B surface programs are four separate files, labelled by path. Do not paste their manifests into one Jet source file. Their package and visibility forms come from the captured pub_package_visibility example and public enum example. The marker in B alone is proposed. The same app label covers Read and Write without else. A accepts that source. B rejects that source, even before a third case exists. No new diagnostic number or observed compiler result is claimed.

### The exact repair under B

Replace app/run.jet with this complete consumer file. Keep the B manifests and provider declaration.

```jet
use modes
fn label(m: modes.Mode) String -> {
    return if m == { .Read -> "read", .Write -> "write", else -> "other" }
}
fn run() { print(label(modes.Mode.Write)) }
```

Its intended output is write. Every known case still has its own arm. The extra else is mandatory, not a ban on those arms. Inside mode_lib/modes.jet, the following same-package function needs no extra else under B:

```jet
pub fn local_label(m: Mode) String -> {
    return if m == { .Read -> "read", .Write -> "write" }
}
```

This function belongs beside the provider's Mode declaration. Its parameter uses the local Mode, not an imported type. Both snippets are source-composed and NOT RUN.

### Work through the next release

For provider version 0.2.0, replace its declaration with pub enum Mode { Read Write Append }. B keeps #NonExhaustive. If local_label is present, the provider adds .Append -> "append" to that function. Its own package still checks every case normally.

Now rebuild the original app against that release. Under A, its no-else label is incomplete and source checking refuses it. Adding .Append -> "append" repairs it. Choosing else instead is also legal under A. Under B, the repaired app above keeps compiling under the proposed rule because it already has else. Changing its run call to label(modes.Mode.Append) produces the intended other result. These are source predictions, not executions or binary-compatibility receipts.

The lost B guarantee is precise: downstream code cannot omit else to force a new explicit arm when a case is added. It can still write an explicit arm for every known case. A leaves that choice with each consumer. Neither policy forces a useful business response for a future case; the author of else still owns that response.

### Keep three kinds of compatibility separate

Source compatibility asks whether old source can be checked again against a changed library. This ballot addresses that question. Encoded-data compatibility asks whether stored or transmitted messages can be read. This marker adds no unknown-message decoder. Binary compatibility asks whether already-compiled machine code can safely exchange values across versions. This ballot gives no such layout or calling-convention promise.

A discriminant is an explicit integer code written on a declaration. The marker does not stabilize those numbers. Nor does it make arbitrary integers valid cases. Removing the marker relaxes the downstream source requirement; an existing caller that already has else need not remove it. But removal withdraws the publisher's future-addition policy. It must be recorded as a compatibility-policy change, not advertised as proof that every old binary remains safe.

### Read the Rust comparison

Rust calls its compiled package a crate. pub exposes the enum. #[non_exhaustive] marks a provider declaration. The use line imports it into a different crate. Rust's match selects an arm; => corresponds to Jet's -> here. Its _ arm is the catch-all. The example prints write; removing that arm exposes the same downstream restriction. The comparison is source-composed and NOT RUN. Source: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/type_system.html#the-non_exhaustive-attribute.


The Rust comparison needs two compilation units, not two sections pasted into one file. With its labelled lib.rs and main.rs files, this source-only recipe establishes the separate-crate boundary without Cargo:

```sh
rustc --edition=2021 --crate-name modes --crate-type=lib modes/src/lib.rs -o libmodes.rlib
rustc --edition=2021 app/src/main.rs --extern modes=libmodes.rlib -o app-example
```

This recipe is NOT RUN. It is not a Jet validation command or a runtime receipt.

### Relevant existing rules, not a new vote

D-ENUMDOT1 and D-ENUMDOT2 require the leading dot in case patterns, such as .Read. A qualified value such as modes.Mode.Write stays valid. The proposed marker does not change that syntax.

D-TAG1 permits nested variant groups. A value is always a leaf, never the group itself. A group pattern covers its subtree. Empty groups remain illegal. Under B, covering every current group still does not remove the downstream else requirement.

D-UNIONTYPE1=A keeps A | B a closed structural sum. Nested sums flatten, repeated member types disappear, and member order does not change identity. Members enter only at the existing checked boundaries. Ambiguous encoded member shapes are rejected. A named enum remains a separate declared type; crossing between these forms uses explicit matching and construction. Nothing here adds an open or arbitrary-value type.

The CoreLib metadata remains null because this choice lists no library addition. B would still require language and checker work. Null is not a zero-work or zero-cost claim. Exact governing excerpts and package manifests are in prior-decision-receipts.json and reader-package-phase-primitives.md.


## ratified constraints

D-UNIONTYPE1=A

D-TAG1

D-ENUMDOT1

D-ENUMDOT2

## Review provenance and author disposition

No material adversarial finding was returned for Evolution. The policy choices and workload code remain unchanged. The later ELI5 pass states concrete upgrade consequences instead of scoring the absence of a marker as a drawback.

The actual beginner summary in reviewPasses is copied verbatim from target-mine-playlist-20260911/coordination/enum-beginner-a-review.json (SHA-256 8822ac97a9c721788086c777a9e975d4474063cf8560b825d6687a1a414578c6). The actual adversarial summary is copied verbatim from target-mine-playlist-20260911/coordination/enum-adversarial-a-review.json (SHA-256 8a72e5f8e5df857a2bef6fc8b8b6ada6aff76b452b2f35fed395d98efd82702c). These are separate fresh agents and ordered passes over their stated frozen inputs. They are not owner approval.

The adversarial input is bound to enum-reader-repaired-ballots.json, SHA-256 838bdc7cbdd1d6329585c329a2fa9727cdfc4acfb1920406a6f0220af8a6b475. Later author changes in this document were not read by those frozen passes. The original source_metadata and reader_repair records remain historical provenance. Their earlier hashes and pending-review wording are not assertions about this final payload.

All current, peer, and proposed workload bodies remain source-composed and NOT RUN. No source edit, Tower write, build, test, formatter, or lint result is implied. Main owns final publication, exact-law reconciliation, and any focused runtime proof.

decisions.title: Generate checked decoders for explicitly numbered enums
decisions.gist: Should numbered enums decode declared codes automatically and reject holes?
decisions.lesson: An explicit code is a number assigned to a named enum case. A checked decoder accepts only declared codes and returns a failure for a hole. A generates that lookup from the enum; B keeps an application parser. Both preserve destination-owned conversion and the existing fallible error result.
decisions.story: Inez reads device codes 4 and 2. Mode declares Read=1 and Write=4, so both options should produce write for 4 and unknown for 2. A keeps one mapping in the enum. B keeps Inez’s separate parser, which she must update when codes change.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

D-SHAPE-CONVERT1=A already fixes Target.from_source and ordinary fallible checked narrowing, including enum conversions. This ballot does not reopen that law. It chooses only automatic lookup generated from the enum declaration versus an explicit application mapping. A generates T.from_int(Int) with the ordinary fallible result and existing checked-conversion error domain.

In the captured conversion table that domain is String, so the concrete source-level result is T !String. Integration must preserve the canonical conversion error contract on its selected snapshot, not invent an optional or enum-only error family. Eligibility requires every leaf to be payload-free, explicitly numbered and uniquely coded.

Duplicate codes make reverse lookup ambiguous and are rejected for this generated API without silently changing general declaration legality. Negative declared codes work; nonmembers return the ordinary recoverable conversion error. Wider inputs use checked Int conversion first. Payload-bearing, partially numbered and non-enum receivers do not gain this generated member.

Conflicting user members follow existing method coherence and duplicate diagnostics; they are never silently replaced. No enum-to-int API or stable default ordinal is introduced. This is a stock compiler/Core functionality addition, not an optional enum library. An existing equivalent generated decoder would replace this draft with a proof card. The present bounded source search found numeric/distinct routes, not that generator.

## ratified constraints

D-SHAPE-CONVERT1=A

D-UNIONTYPE1=A

## corelib change

### kind

stock existing conversion-family extension

### library

Compiler/Core destination-owned numeric conversion members

### addition

Generated declared-member T.from_int(Int) with the existing fallible checked-conversion result

### distribution

Stock; no optional enum package

### external dependency

None

### owner gate

D-ENUM-INGRESS1

## Recommendation reasoning

For Inez’s device stream, A maps 4 to Write and rejects 2 from the declaration itself. B stays useful for aliases or mappings that are not enum codes.

Option B: B keeps a second mapping that can drift from the enum declaration. A still leaves unrelated protocol aliases to explicit parsers.

No payload, implicit cast or source-order ordinal is invented. Other numeric inputs first use their existing checked Int conversion.

decisions.title: Adjacent tag and content in Codable
decisions.gist: Should Codable directly produce protocols with a separate tag and payload field?
decisions.lesson: A service may send a case name in kind and its payload—the attached value—in body. Codable converts between Jet values and encoded data. A adds this two-field form directly; B builds it explicitly. A unit case has no payload: absent or null body is accepted, then omitted on output. Non-null body fails. Other unit rules need B or a custom codec.
decisions.story: Ravi integrates a service whose messages use kind and body. He wants ordinary enum values in application code without maintaining a second conversion table.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

Extend #Discriminant(field:String) with optional content:String. Existing no-content internal tagging remains unchanged. A content argument selects adjacent tagging: unit -> {tag:wireName}; single -> {tag:wireName,content:encodedValue}; named -> {tag:wireName,content:encodedFieldsObject}. Tag and content names must be distinct, nonempty strings checked by the existing marker signature machinery.

Decode ignores key order, requires payload content for non-unit cases, and treats non-null content on a unit as an error. Existing unknown-field policy controls other keys. An unknown tag remains a typed error unless D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1 is separately selected. Missing/wrong payloads retain FieldError paths under the content key. Rename/RenameAll still determine the canonical wire case name.

Custom codecs remain the same Encode/Decode protocol. Stock core.encoding derives/adapters own this; no enum module, optional codec package, Glaze or Serde product dependency is added. Formats that cannot encode the chosen data shape must fail honestly through their existing adapter contract, not silently switch wire forms.

Existing D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A preserves unknown fields for PublishedSchema values; plain Codable drops them and DenyUnknownFields refuses them. Unknown enum tags remain a different question. This proposal does not reopen that field policy. Existing D-SERDE2=A requires derives to contribute checked Jet items through the same Encode/Decode protocol; no compiler-synthesized foreign-language codec or R11 exception is authorized.

### Read the success and failure from end to end

JSON is a text format. An object uses braces and named fields. A field has a quoted name, a colon, and a value. A quoted JSON value is text; an unquoted 7 is a number. The wire is the text sent to another program. Here is the intended first output, without requiring this key order or spacing:

```json
{"kind":"Write","body":"hello"}
```

kind is the tag: it names the selected case. body is the content: it carries that case's payload. Command.Write("hello") constructs Write with one String payload. json.to_string encodes the value as JSON text. json.decode<Command> checks JSON before constructing Command. In A, Discriminant names the two fields. In B, the Envelope record names them and the application converts between that record and Command.

A record groups named fields. Envelope.body is a record field and therefore participates in the wire form. A local variable such as e is only a temporary name inside the program. Renaming e does not rename the wire field. #Codable requests the existing checked encoding and decoding operations. Grouped #[Codable, Discriminant(...)] applies both markers; only content is new in A.

Both complete programs print the encoded object, then hello, then invalid message. The third call reads this same malformed input:

```json
{"kind":"Write","body":7}
```

The tag is known, but the payload is a number where String is required. In A, decoding Command fails under the proposed content path body. In B, decoding Envelope fails because its body field requires String. Neither constructs a usable Command from that input. Unknown tags also fail: B's explicit else refuses them; A keeps checked tag lookup. This ballot supplies no catch-all.

A result written T ![FieldError] contains either a T or a list of errors. Each FieldError has a path and a reason. The code uses ?? return "invalid message" to handle a failed result locally. That expression immediately returns from report, so its later case selection does not run. run prints the returned label. The label is written by this example; it is not a promised compiler diagnostic or a rendering of the error list. All these results are source-composed expectations, NOT RUN.

### Show what no content keeps unchanged

These are representations of the same selected Write(String) payload. They describe shape, not a new choice among four modes in this ballot.

**Case 1.**

**Form:** Existing external tag

**Marker:** default

**Encoded selected value:** {"Write":"hello"}

**Case 2.**

**Form:** Existing internal tag

**Marker:** #Discriminant("kind")

**Encoded selected value:** {"kind":"Write","value":"hello"}

**Case 3.**

**Form:** Proposed adjacent tag

**Marker:** #Discriminant("kind", content: "body")

**Encoded selected value:** {"kind":"Write","body":"hello"}

**Case 4.**

**Form:** Existing untagged payload

**Marker:** #Untagged

**Encoded selected value:** "hello"

External puts the selected name outside its payload. Internal places the tag inside the payload object; a single unnamed payload uses value. Adjacent gives the payload its own named field beside the tag. Untagged omits the case name. A tag-free String cannot itself tell Write from Remove; this proposal adds no guessing rule. Leaving content out must retain the existing internal form, including its value key. It must not silently switch to body.

The existing representation rows are captured at docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3647-3665 and docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:2871-2877 through the enum evidence packets. They establish the source-level baseline, not runtime execution of these composed examples.

### Ground the payload-shape contract

The following declaration extends only the worked shape illustration:

```jet
#[Codable, Discriminant("kind", content: "body")]
enum Command { Quit Write(String) Move(x: Int, y: Int) }
```

**Case 1.**

**Source value:** Command.Quit

**Payload kind:** Unit: no attached value

**Proposed encoded object:** {"kind":"Quit"}

**Case 2.**

**Source value:** Command.Write("hello")

**Payload kind:** Single: one unnamed value

**Proposed encoded object:** {"kind":"Write","body":"hello"}

**Case 3.**

**Source value:** Command.Move{x: 2, y: 3}

**Payload kind:** Named: two named fields

**Proposed encoded object:** {"kind":"Move","body":{"x":2,"y":3}}

null is JSON's explicit no-value token. For Quit, absent body and body:null both decode as Quit. A non-null body on Quit is an error. body is the recognized content slot even for a unit case, not an unknown field. Therefore DenyUnknownFields does not turn body:null into an extra-field error. Other keys still use the existing unknown-field policy. Encoding Quit emits no body key, even if input supplied null.

For Write and Move, body is required. Null is not a valid String or the required named-field object in these declarations, so body:null fails. Missing body fails at body. Both options commit to the external service's two names. This is a shared protocol cost, not a new A-only cost. The actual choice is who owns mapping and tag validation: existing Codable under A, application conversion under B. Neither option promises a performance win. ### Read the Rust comparison

Serde's derive generates the Rust codec methods. tag and content name the same two fields. Command::Write constructs the selected payload. from_str checks the incoming JSON; is_err detects refusal. The ? operator returns an error to main's caller rather than continuing. D-SERDE2=A requires generated codecs to enter the normal Jet checking path. They are not unchecked foreign-language code. D-SERDE7 keeps external tagging as the default and permits Discriminant and Untagged. D-SERDE8 keeps unknown-field refusal opt-in. decisions.title: Typed forwarding of unknown enum variants
decisions.gist: Should an enum explicitly retain unknown wire variants without weakening known-case decoding?
decisions.lesson: A tag names a message kind. A stores an unfamiliar kind in a protected enum case. B keeps DataTree—the parsed message—and routes known kinds separately. Neither preserves original bytes; unsupported values fail. A cannot use Untagged, which has no tag, or aliases on its fallback. Core currently keeps the last duplicate tag; that policy decision remains open.
decisions.story: Sam runs an event relay. A newer client sends a case this relay does not understand. Sam must forward its fields without treating a broken known message as an unknown one.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

Core placement: core.encoding.UnknownVariant<T>, a compiler-owned opaque value plus one #Unknown variant marker in existing Codable. T must be the owning enum and have exactly one marked fallback. Its payload must be UnknownVariant<T>; no unit, arbitrary DataTree, or differently owned fallback is accepted. The value has no public fields, unchecked constructor or Default.

Existing checked Decode creates it only from a tagged frame that passes the selected parser and tag Decode rules, whose surviving tag is not a canonical or accepted alias of T. This enum proposal does not independently choose duplicate-key input policy. It implements existing Encode, returning the retained DataTree, and checked Decode for the same unknown-only rule; no second codec or new conversion verb is needed. Cross-enum copying is rejected by its T parameter.

A marked case is not itself a wire tag. Known tags always use the known payload decoder; malformed known data remains FieldError. External, internal and separately ratified adjacent forms retain their entire parsed frame; untagged mode rejects the marker because it has no unambiguous unknown tag. JSON lexical whitespace, original bytes and data outside DataTree representability are not preserved.

Original names/payload values are retained within the parsed tree. Input schema rules still apply before the opaque value exists. Runtime type/schema changes cannot invalidate live values; any reload path must preserve the owning enum identity and existing compatibility rules. The infallible Encode contract is unchanged: every constructible opaque value is already valid for its owner’s unknown branch.

No Glaze/Serde product dependency is adopted.

Existing D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A preserves unknown fields for PublishedSchema values; plain Codable drops them and DenyUnknownFields refuses them. Unknown enum tags remain a different question. This proposal does not reopen that field policy. Existing D-SERDE2=A requires derives to contribute checked Jet items through the same Encode/Decode protocol; no compiler-synthesized foreign-language codec or R11 exception is authorized.

The worked contrast forwards the same Future/hello frame through current DataTree, proposed typed retention and Glaze catch-all decoding. The Glaze fallback has declared fields and is not evidence of arbitrary-tree retention. Preservation is the existing DataTree semantic/numeric contract, not raw wire-byte identity. No silent rounding or other lossy fallback is authorized; unsupported values must fail explicitly before a lossless claim.

### Follow the same three inputs

A tag is the part that selects a case. A payload is the data carried by that case. In this existing internal representation, Discriminant("kind") selects the tag field. A single unnamed String payload uses the value field. These exact frames connect the declaration to its wire shape:

**Case 1.**

**Input JSON text:** {"kind":"Future","value":"hello"}

**Current/B intended result:** Keep an untyped tree and forward those values

**A proposed intended result:** Retained holds the checked unknown frame and forwards those values

**Case 2.**

**Input JSON text:** {"kind":"Write","value":"hello"}

**Current/B intended result:** Decode a valid Command.Write, then encode it

**A proposed intended result:** Decode the same known Command.Write, then encode it

**Case 3.**

**Input JSON text:** {"kind":"Write","value":7}

**Current/B intended result:** Refuse the known String payload; print invalid message

**A proposed intended result:** The same refusal; never select Retained

The first two outputs are JSON objects with the same names and values shown above. Key order, spacing, and whole-message bytes are not promised. The third output is the example's own invalid message label, not a fixed FieldError rendering. All outputs are intended, NOT RUN.

B now contains both paths in one complete program. It parses once with json.decode<DataTree>, then uses the existing tree.decode<Header>() to require a String kind. For Write, tree.decode<Command>() checks the known payload. A failure returns immediately, before forwarding. Only other tags forward the retained tree without constructing Command. Header is an application record, not a new Core API. A obtains that routing from its marked case.

Retained is the source case name chosen for this example. It is deliberately different from the incoming Future tag. The marker selects the fallback, not that name. Changing only Future to Later still selects Retained under A and preserves Later in the output. Adding a source case named Later is neither needed nor authorized by that input.

### Explain the local notation and error handling

An enum names alternatives. Write(String) gives one alternative a text payload. Command.Write("hello") constructs that known value. UnknownVariant<Command> is the proposed protected carrier belonging to Command. The T in the type's definition means its owner type; Self in the technical description means that same owning enum. A carrier for another enum is not interchangeable.

JSON uses braces for objects, quoted field names, and colons before their values. "hello" is JSON text; 7 is a JSON number. Jet backticks delimit the source string literally. They are not sent. The double quotes inside that string belong to the JSON message. :: binds a local name. fn defines a function; String after its parameter list is its returned text type. return ends that function.

json.decode<T> checks input and returns T or [FieldError]. The notation T ![FieldError] describes those two outcomes. ?? return "invalid message" handles failure here by ending report with the example's error label. It does not turn the bad input into Command. The earlier ?? panic fixed-input style would stop the demonstration instead of returning this label. The new program deliberately handles failure without panic.

### Use the existing lossless typed-tree path

A DataTree stores parsed data as named nodes, not a complete original JSON byte stream. The relevant current JSON entry is json.decode<DataTree>(wire), not dynamic json.parse(wire). The typed entry preserves number tokens before a destination chooses a numeric type. DataTree's decoder retains that tree. Its Number node stores a validated numeric token, and JSON rendering writes it as a number, not a quoted string.

This distinction matters. Dynamic json.parse may choose a binary Float for fractional or exponent tokens. A retained unknown frame must not use that lossy route and then call the result lossless. B uses the existing typed-tree entry explicitly. A must retain the typed decoder's checked tree on the unknown branch, before any known numeric destination conversion. It does not need another parser, arbitrary-precision package, or conversion verb.

The current captured number-token validator permits at most 1,000,000 digit characters per number token. An explicit exponent must have magnitude at most 1,000,000. This is a resource bound, not a binary Float range. The operative source chain and hashes are in reader-reflection-primitives.md, sections DataTree numeric variants and Typed retained-DataTree JSON linkage.

**Case 1.**

**Unknown payload token:** 9007199254740993

**Current typed-tree path; proposed A requirement:** Preserve that exact integer value; do not round through Float

**Case 2.**

**Unknown payload token:** 1e400

**Current typed-tree path; proposed A requirement:** Retain the exact number token; no Float conversion is requested

**Case 3.**

**Unknown payload token:** 1e1000001

**Current typed-tree path; proposed A requirement:** Reject because the exponent exceeds the current resource bound

A known field declared Float is different: converting 1e400 to that destination fails. An unknown retained number is not such a Float. These are source-derived distinctions and proposed obligations, not runtime receipts. The full A/B examples include numeric_examples(), which prints the first two frames and then the example's invalid message label for the third. Whole-message whitespace and byte identity still are not promised.

### Keep unfamiliar fields separate from unfamiliar cases

With {"kind":"Write","value":"hello","extra":1}, Write is still known. The ordinary String decoder applies, and the existing field policy controls extra. Plain Codable drops that field. PublishedSchema preserves it. DenyUnknownFields refuses it. None of these field policies turns Write into Retained. Conversely, a genuinely unknown tag retains its whole checked frame under A, including fields this version cannot interpret.

External tagging puts the case name outside its payload, such as {"Write":"hello"}. Internal tagging uses a named field inside an object, as in the examples. Adjacent tagging would place a separately named payload beside that tag, but requires its own ratification. Untagged data omits a case selector. The Unknown marker is forbidden there because no unambiguous unfamiliar tag exists.

The carrier has no unchecked public constructor, mutable public fields, or Default. Only a checked unknown-tag decode creates it. One owning enum has exactly one marked carrier case. The marker's own source name is not accepted as a normal tag. A schema or runtime reload cannot reinterpret an already-retained value under a different owner identity. This ballot provides no reload API or binary compatibility guarantee.

### Explain the Glaze mechanism

C++ std::variant holds one declared alternative. Here the alternatives are Write and Unknown. Glaze's ids list supplies only Write, so it is shorter than that alternative list. The first unlabeled final alternative, Unknown, is the default for unfamiliar tags. Its kind field receives the actual tag value. A recognized Write still selects Write's declared String payload check.

read_json reports failure when it cannot decode the selected structure. The program prints its own invalid message label on that path and never encodes the failed value. write_json re-encodes a successfully decoded value. Unknown declares only kind and value; it is not evidence that arbitrary extra fields or numeric payloads survive. Jet A's retained-tree contract is intentionally broader than that declared-field example. Source: https://stephenberry.github.io/glaze/variant-handling/. The comparison is composed and NOT RUN.

### Relevant existing rules, not a new vote

D-ENC1 keeps JSON, CSV, TOML, and YAML inside core.encoding. They share one data model and codec protocol. A codec converts a checked value to data, or checks data before constructing a value. This ballot adds no serializer package.

D-SERDE1–12 names the existing serialization rules. The relevant captured rules follow. A type must qualify for generated codecs or provide its own codec. Codable requests both Encode and Decode; separate markers request one direction. Decode returns either the requested value or a list of FieldError values. Each error has a path and a reason. Encode remains infallible for a valid value.

D-SERDE2=A requires generated codecs to enter the normal Jet checking path. They are not unchecked foreign-language code. Hand-written codecs use encode(self) DataTree and decode(tree: DataTree) T ![FieldError]. These expert interfaces are unchanged; the worked programs only need json.decode and json.to_string.

D-SERDE3/5 keep canonical naming explicit. A per-case Rename wins over RenameAll. RenameAll selects a checked casing style. D-SERDE7 keeps external tagging as the default and permits Discriminant and Untagged. D-SERDE8 keeps unknown-field refusal opt-in. D-SERDE9/10/12 attach codec requirements only to generic parameters that reach encoded data. Unsupported arguments fail at use, not merely because the definition is generic.

D-SERDE6 retains decode<T>'s destination-type selection. No general conversion direction is changed here. D-SERDE1–12 is an umbrella source reference, not evidence of twelve ratifications.

Main's exact D-SERDE11 lookup returned E_NOT_FOUND with exit 1: no decision D-SERDE11. The bounded spec capture also found no separate D-SERDE11 wording. A current fixture labels its generic use-site refusal D-SERDE11/12. That is source evidence only, not a run or a ratification record. This ballot asserts no D-SERDE11 choice, ratified status, or standalone rule. Every separately evidenced existing codec constraint remains unchanged.

D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A concerns extra object fields, not unfamiliar enum cases. Plain Codable drops extra fields. PublishedSchema preserves them. DenyUnknownFields refuses them. The new enum rule must keep those choices distinct.

D-LIT-DOT1=B removes the dot before literal braces: Record{field: value}, not Record.{field: value}. The leading dot in a case pattern, such as .Write(s), remains. A marker begins with #. Grouped #[Encode, Decode] applies both markers; it does not declare a new case.

These consequences are captured in prior-decision-receipts.json, codec-gate-supplement.md, and reader-package-phase-primitives.md. Their locators and file hashes identify the evidence. Historical constraints do not ratify the proposed owner gate.

D-UNIONTYPE1=A keeps A | B a closed structural sum. Nested sums flatten, repeated member types disappear, and member order does not change identity. Members enter only at the existing checked boundaries. Ambiguous encoded member shapes are rejected. A named enum remains a separate declared type; crossing between these forms uses explicit matching and construction. Nothing here adds an open or arbitrary-value type.

### Compose fallback retention with decode aliases

This is an explicit proposed interaction if both D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1 and D-ENUM-WIREALIAS1 select A. It is not existing ratified behavior. A case marked #Unknown cannot also carry #DecodeAliases. Source checking rejects that marker combination; it does not silently ignore aliases or attempt to populate the opaque carrier as an ordinary known payload.

For example, #[Unknown, DecodeAliases("future")] Retained(UnknownVariant<Command>) is rejected at the declaration, before any input is decoded. Without that alias, a well-formed unfamiliar kind:"future" reaches the protected fallback. An alias on an ordinary known case selects that case before the fallback, and a malformed payload for that alias is a normal known-case error. These are owner-visible composition terms of the two proposed A choices, not a new ratification or runtime result.

### Ground duplicate-selector routing without selecting a new parser policy

The exact source capture is peer-evidence/adversarial-selector-routing.md, SHA-256 c34479ce3cd6a758caa855a2c1da17b529fb6bcec10f60fc0d4be791b70c247e. These are source-derived predictions, NOT RUN. They are not a claim of runtime safety or a ratified last-wins policy.

Core typed json.decode<T> currently calls the typed parser with reject_duplicate_keys=false. A later duplicate replaces the earlier value at the original key position. Header and Command then read the same surviving kind through DataTree.field. tree.decode<Command>() dispatches Command's ordinary Decode; it does not parse or independently choose another duplicate. The draft declares Header.kind:String and Command.Write(String), with internal tag kind and payload key value. Those exact source-composed declarations determine this matrix:

**Case 1.**

**Exact JSON input:** {"kind":"Future","kind":"Write","value":7}

**Parsed selector:** Write

**Current/B prediction:** Known Write decode rejects the typed Number payload as String; report returns invalid message.

**Proposed A requirement if this parser behavior remains:** Use the known decoder and reject; do not retain on its error.

**Case 2.**

**Exact JSON input:** {"kind":"Write","kind":"Future","value":7}

**Parsed selector:** Future

**Current/B prediction:** Route as unfamiliar and emit the normalized tree with kind Future and value 7.

**Proposed A requirement if this parser behavior remains:** Retain that same unknown parsed frame, not the discarded Write selector.

Thus known-malformed refusal concerns the surviving selector. Neither path promises to reject every byte sequence that once contained a known name. Both already lost the earlier duplicate before enum routing. Reversing duplicate order changes the current parsed value; it is not evidence of disagreement between Header and Command.

The canonical core input duplicate-key choice remains open in the captured core-f005 card. This ballot neither ratifies last-wins nor silently substitutes duplicate rejection. A must follow the eventual selected core policy. Main must reconcile that existing owner gate and run the two exact inputs on the supported routes before a runtime safety claim. Strict LSP/DAP parsing and canonicalization rejection are different boundaries, not proof of core input behavior.

For a manually constructed DataTree.Object containing duplicate pairs, field reads the first matching pair. That is a different input carrier from the JSON parser's normalized output. The carrier still uses one lookup rule for Header and the tagged decoder. Do not transfer the JSON last-wins prediction to arbitrary manually constructed trees.

Missing, null, numeric JSON, object, and array selectors fail the captured String decoding path. Typed numeric JSON becomes Number, which String Decode rejects. Boolean selectors currently become the strings true/false through that shared decoder; this proposal does not silently tighten that existing behavior. Direct typed Command decoding then compares canonical known names, while B forwards an unfamiliar surviving tag. A must compose with the selected existing tag-decoding rule. No additional selector strictness or new duplicate-key vote is hidden here.


## Existing constraints and source references

The frozen source_metadata.ratified_constraints list is retained verbatim as provenance, not as a new status assertion. Its D-SERDE1–12 entry is an umbrella source label. decisions.title: Canonical enum output with old input names
decisions.gist: Should Codable accept explicit old case names while writing only the current name?
decisions.lesson: A wire name is text that identifies a case in stored or sent data. A accepts listed old names whenever this enum is decoded, but writes one current name. B can translate names only at selected calls. Removing an alias later rejects old input. Aliases need a tag and unique names; they cannot mark the Unknown fallback.
decisions.story: Asha renames a protocol case for clarity. Years of stored messages still use the old spelling. She wants to read them without writing more old data.
decisions.inWild:
import json
from enum import Enum
class Mode(Enum):
    read = 1
    legacy_read = 1
    reader = 1
wire_members = {"read": "read", "legacy-read": "legacy_read", "reader": "reader"}
for wire in ['"legacy-read"', '"reader"']:
    mode = Mode[wire_members[json.loads(wire)]]
    print(json.dumps(mode.name))
# Intended output: "read", then "read". NOT RUN.
# Source aliases need this explicit JSON/name mapping; they are not wire aliases.
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

Stock core.encoding/Codable addition: #DecodeAliases(name:String, ...) on enum variants only, with at least one argument. Existing marker argument checking resolves constant strings. Canonical wire names still come from per-case Rename over container RenameAll. Decode aliases are exact strings, unaffected by RenameAll.

The combined canonical/alias name set must be unique across cases; duplicate aliases and an alias equal to its own canonical name are rejected as redundant. Aliases never create source constructors, extra case identities, discriminants or T.cases items. The marker is valid for external/internal and separately ratified adjacent tags, not Untagged.

Unknown-tag fallback, if separately ratified, runs only after canonical/alias lookup; malformed payloads under an alias remain known-case errors. Encode never emits an alias. Removing an alias is an explicit wire compatibility change. Custom Decode retains application control through the same DataTree protocol. No external serializer or separate compatibility library is adopted.

Existing D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A preserves unknown fields for PublishedSchema values; plain Codable drops them and DenyUnknownFields refuses them. Unknown enum tags remain a different question. This proposal does not reopen that field policy. Existing D-SERDE2=A requires derives to contribute checked Jet items through the same Encode/Decode protocol; no compiler-synthesized foreign-language codec or R11 exception is authorized.

### Explain why a bare string is a tag

Mode.Read has no payload. In the existing default external representation, a no-payload case is encoded as its case name alone. Rename("read") chooses that canonical wire name. Thus the whole JSON string "read" is the case selector. It is tagged even though it has no separate kind field. An accepted old tag such as "reader" selects the same Read case under A.

For an external payload-bearing case, the name instead appears as the object key: {"write":"hello"}. Internal tagging puts the selector in a named object field. Adjacent tagging would put a separate content field beside it, but requires its own ratification. These are locations of a selector, not different alias identities.

Untagged omits the selector. For example, an untagged Write(String) payload could be the JSON text "hello" itself. That text is the payload, not an accepted case name. DecodeAliases is forbidden on an Untagged enum. It must not search and replace arbitrary strings inside a payload. The current representation contract is captured in codec-gate-supplement.md and prior-decision-receipts.json under D-SERDE7.

### Follow the text and value states

The first block is Jet source. The second is the JSON message it contains.

```jet
wire :: `"reader"`
```

```json
"reader"
```

The backticks delimit the Jet source string and are not sent. The double quotes belong to JSON. The message has eight characters: an opening quote, reader, and a closing quote. No backslashes are sent. The older escaped source form represents the same bytes:

```jet
wire :: "\"reader\""
```

Here is B's exact path for one input:

**Case 1.**

**Step:** Incoming wire

**State:** JSON text "reader", including its double quotes

**Case 2.**

**Step:** json.decode<String>

**State:** A Jet String whose contents are reader, without JSON delimiter quotes

**Case 3.**

**Step:** canonical_name

**State:** A Jet String whose contents are read

**Case 4.**

**Step:** json.to_string of that String

**State:** JSON text "read", including its double quotes

**Case 5.**

**Step:** json.decode<Mode>

**State:** The checked enum value Mode.Read

**Case 6.**

**Step:** json.to_string of Mode.Read

**State:** Canonical JSON text "read"

The middle encode is not another alias policy. The ordinary typed decoder expects JSON text, not the bare String contents read. A skips the application conversion because its proposed marker makes the decoder recognize the old tag directly. Both complete examples print "read" twice, including the JSON quotes. These are intended results, NOT RUN.

fn defines a function. :: binds a local name. String names the returned text type. if s == { ... } chooses an arm; -> gives its result, and else returns unchanged names here. loop repeats the same operation for each listed input. ?? return "invalid name" handles a failed decode and leaves report immediately. It does not make an invalid Mode. The printed error label is application text, not a promised diagnostic rendering.

### Make the small extension yourself

To accept archive-read under A, add "archive-read" to DecodeAliases. Leave Rename("read") and the single Read case unchanged. Under B, add "archive-read" -> "read" to canonical_name. Test input `"archive-read"` still produces canonical output "read" under the intended policy. The new alias must be distinct from every accepted name in the enum.

If reader is removed from A's alias list or B's converter, the shown program's old input is no longer accepted. The report function returns invalid name. A does not infer historical spellings from renames. Changing Rename("read") to Rename("scan") changes canonical output. To keep accepting the former canonical read, an author must now list it explicitly. B must likewise update its conversion targets.

### Instantiate the malformed-known boundary

This complete additional A example uses a payload, rather than asking a no-payload case to demonstrate a payload error:

```jet
use core.encoding.json as json
#Codable enum Command {
    #[Rename("write"), DecodeAliases("legacy-write")]
    Write(String)
}
fn report(wire: String) String -> {
    c :: json.decode<Command>(wire) ?? return "invalid payload"
    return json.to_string(c)
}
fn run() {
    loop wire in [`{"legacy-write":"hello"}`, `{"legacy-write":7}`] -> print(report(wire))
}
```

The intended first output is {"write":"hello"}. The second is invalid payload. The alias selects known Write before the String payload is checked. A number is not that String. Even if another ballot separately adds unknown-tag fallback, that recognized alias cannot escape into it. This program does not add such a fallback. It is proposed and NOT RUN.

B can perform the same narrow old-version conversion with ordinary records. This complete example intentionally reads the legacy-write version; the primary Mode converter above shows canonical and multiple-old-name acceptance.

```jet
use core.encoding.json as json
#Codable enum Command { #Rename("write") Write(String) }
#Codable struct LegacyWrite { #Rename("legacy-write") value: String }
fn report(wire: String) String -> {
    old :: json.decode<LegacyWrite>(wire) ?? return "invalid payload"
    return json.to_string(Command.Write(old.value))
}
fn run() {
    loop wire in [`{"legacy-write":"hello"}`, `{"legacy-write":7}`] -> print(report(wire))
}
```

Its intended outputs are the same canonical object and invalid payload label. The record's String field performs the concrete refusal before construction. This is source-composed current syntax, NOT RUN. A Data Transfer Object, or DTO, is simply such a record used to match another system's format. No extra codec protocol is implied by that term.

### Keep identity and collisions precise

Canonical means the one name written on output. An alias is an additional name accepted only on input. A collision occurs when one accepted string identifies two cases. The combined canonical-and-alias name set must be unique. Two copies of one alias, or an alias equal to its own canonical name, are rejected as redundant. There is no first-case-wins rule.

Rename overrides the enclosing RenameAll for the canonical name. Alias strings remain exact; RenameAll does not transform them. Removing an alias changes compatibility with data already stored under that spelling. Authors must keep the accepted historical names deliberately; neither the compiler nor a migration tool can infer their intent.

No alias creates another source case, constructor, declaration code, or finite-case-list item. T.cases is an expert reference to the separately governed finite-value list; this ballot does not require that API to exist or change. Custom Decode is another unchanged expert escape path. A beginner need not implement it to understand this choice; the complete B records and conversion functions already demonstrate application ownership.

### Explain the Python comparison

Python Enum makes the first declaration with value 1 the canonical member, here read. Later declarations with the same value are source aliases of that same member. Selecting Mode.legacy_read therefore obtains the member whose name is read. This explains why mode.name returns read rather than legacy_read.

The dictionary wire_members is still necessary. It maps the JSON spelling legacy-read to the Python identifier legacy_read; the hyphenated wire name is not that source identifier. json.loads removes JSON delimiters to obtain the name String. Mode[...] selects the member, and json.dumps writes its canonical source name as JSON. Python source aliases do not automatically accept wire aliases. Source: https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/enum.html. The program is composed and NOT RUN.

### Relevant existing rules, not a new vote

D-ENC1 keeps JSON, CSV, TOML, and YAML inside core.encoding. They share one data model and codec protocol. A codec converts a checked value to data, or checks data before constructing a value. This ballot adds no serializer package.

D-SERDE1–12 names the existing serialization rules. The relevant captured rules follow. A type must qualify for generated codecs or provide its own codec. Codable requests both Encode and Decode; separate markers request one direction. Decode returns either the requested value or a list of FieldError values. Each error has a path and a reason. Encode remains infallible for a valid value.

D-SERDE2=A requires generated codecs to enter the normal Jet checking path. They are not unchecked foreign-language code. Hand-written codecs use encode(self) DataTree and decode(tree: DataTree) T ![FieldError]. These expert interfaces are unchanged; the worked programs only need json.decode and json.to_string.

D-SERDE3/5 keep canonical naming explicit. A per-case Rename wins over RenameAll. RenameAll selects a checked casing style. D-SERDE7 keeps external tagging as the default and permits Discriminant and Untagged. D-SERDE8 keeps unknown-field refusal opt-in. D-SERDE9/10/12 attach codec requirements only to generic parameters that reach encoded data. Unsupported arguments fail at use, not merely because the definition is generic.

D-SERDE6 retains decode<T>'s destination-type selection. No general conversion direction is changed here. D-SERDE1–12 is an umbrella source reference, not evidence of twelve ratifications.

Main's exact D-SERDE11 lookup returned E_NOT_FOUND with exit 1: no decision D-SERDE11. The bounded spec capture also found no separate D-SERDE11 wording. A current fixture labels its generic use-site refusal D-SERDE11/12. That is source evidence only, not a run or a ratification record. This ballot asserts no D-SERDE11 choice, ratified status, or standalone rule. Every separately evidenced existing codec constraint remains unchanged.

D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A concerns extra object fields, not unfamiliar enum cases. Plain Codable drops extra fields. PublishedSchema preserves them. DenyUnknownFields refuses them. The new enum rule must keep those choices distinct.

D-LIT-DOT1=B removes the dot before literal braces: Record{field: value}, not Record.{field: value}. The leading dot in a case pattern, such as .Write(s), remains. A marker begins with #. Grouped #[Encode, Decode] applies both markers; it does not declare a new case.

These consequences are captured in prior-decision-receipts.json, codec-gate-supplement.md, and reader-package-phase-primitives.md. Their locators and file hashes identify the evidence. Historical constraints do not ratify the proposed owner gate.

D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1=A keeps marker names distinct from unrelated language or library meanings. It replaced the old serialization marker #Tag with #Discriminant. This is about the marker's source name. It is not the rule for collisions between strings written inside JSON. Proposed marker names still need the same registry check before ratification.

### Compose fallback retention with decode aliases

This is an explicit proposed interaction if both D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1 and D-ENUM-WIREALIAS1 select A. It is not existing ratified behavior. A case marked #Unknown cannot also carry #DecodeAliases. Source checking rejects that marker combination; it does not silently ignore aliases or attempt to populate the opaque carrier as an ordinary known payload.

For example, #[Unknown, DecodeAliases("future")] Retained(UnknownVariant<Command>) is rejected at the declaration, before any input is decoded. Without that alias, a well-formed unfamiliar kind:"future" reaches the protected fallback. An alias on an ordinary known case selects that case before the fallback, and a malformed payload for that alias is a normal known-case error. These are owner-visible composition terms of the two proposed A choices, not a new ratification or runtime result.


## Existing constraints and source references

The frozen source_metadata.ratified_constraints list is retained verbatim as provenance, not as a new status assertion. Its D-SERDE1–12 entry is an umbrella source label. The exact D-SERDE11 lookup returned E_NOT_FOUND; no D-SERDE11 ratification or standalone rule is claimed. The other captured existing constraints are preserved.

D-SERDE1–12 — umbrella source reference, with the explicit D-SERDE11 absence above

D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1

D-BOUND-EVOLVE1=A

D-LIT-DOT1=B

options.name: Add decode-only aliases
options.detail: Add #DecodeAliases with one or more string arguments on a case. Decode accepts those names plus the canonical name; Encode only writes Rename/RenameAll’s canonical name. Collisions are rejected before code generation. The existing case identity, value iterator and metadata model remain authoritative. This changes the accepted-input set of every ordinary decode of the enum. No per-call strict opt-out is proposed. Removing an alias is an input-compatibility change; choose B or a custom decoder for boundary-local acceptance.

options.name: Keep version conversion explicit
options.detail: Keep Rename and explicit application conversion. The complete program decodes the JSON string, converts its old name, writes canonical JSON text, and invokes the ordinary typed Mode decoder. It handles invalid inputs with an application error label. No new Core name or dependency is added. canonical_name is already a reusable central mapping. B does not require policy copies; it requires application ownership of that mapping and agreement between its canonical target and Rename. Only callers that use this boundary conversion accept the old names.

decisions.title: One declaration model for shape consumers
decisions.gist: Should codecs, enum facts, and schema projections read one checked declaration model?
decisions.lesson: A declaration names a record and its fields. Here who is the source name and customer is the JSON name. Current law requires one checked shape authority. A completes that consolidation. B explicitly relaxes that rule for the named consumer models, with agreement checks. Neither choice changes the successful user output.
decisions.story: Leah renames a field on the wire. Encoding, decoding, command arguments, and generated request descriptions must not independently guess which name applies.
decisions.detail:
This ballot concerns ownership of checked declaration facts, not a new universal schema type. D-SHAPE-ONE1=A, D-META-REG1=A and D-VALIDATE-DECODE1=B remain the baseline. Runtime materialization of compile-time facts and historical-schema type identity receive separate explicit analysis. Diagrams are implementation maps, not proposed language grammar.

Captured work:
Prior finding 3 and tactical mirrored shape mapping/builtin enum metadata.
Planned enum values, reflection, constructors, wire variants and shape consumers share declaration ownership.
Keep every format-specific validation, migration, and HTTP behavior criterion.

Required evidence before implementation closure:
Rename, skip, computed, default, ordering, duplicate and unknown field behavior.
AOT/evaluator agreement and builtin enum declaration-order evidence.
HTTP/OpenAPI body examples proving selected names describe actual serialization.

Example status: current snippets are explicitly source-composed or captured source/test expectations. This preparation ran no Jet compiler, provider or UI scenario. Proposed alternatives are design contracts, not implemented behavior. No peer example proves Jet semantics.

Contribution or failure trial (proposed acceptance, not an observed run):

A: Contributor trial: change #Rename("customer") to #Rename("buyer"). Regenerated JSON and the matching JSON-schema view both use buyer from the checked fact. A computed field remains distinct from a skipped stored field.

B: Same trial: independent consumer models must be updated to agree on buyer. Leaving a schema model at customer must fail a correspondence check. This is a proposed limited amendment, not current law.

Authority: A follows D-SHAPE-ONE1=A and D-META-REG1=A. B explicitly amends the single-consumer-fact-authority requirement only for the named AOT, evaluator and schema consumer models. It does not replace the Registry substrate or change declaration syntax.

The current ShapeFact skip flag loses computed-versus-skipped identity. Before redirecting consumers, extend the existing checked facts with stored/computed kind and checked getter identity/type where required. Metadata extraction must not execute getters.

Keep the key space explicit. Current decode_name uses the JSON slot in the shared carrier path. Prove each format’s wire-to-carrier normalization before replacing it; never substitute a requested wire name blindly.

decisions.title: Pass eligible constructors as ordinary callables
decisions.gist: Should eligible payload constructors pass directly to ordinary function parameters?
decisions.lesson: A payload constructor combines a case name with supplied data. Today a helper receives a lambda around that constructor. A removes that wrapper when the checked signature fits an ordinary function type. B keeps it. Unit cases stay values. Ownership, public argument labels and effects remain ordinary callable rules; reflection does not perform construction.
decisions.story: Lee passes a text constructor into a helper that supplies hello. The helper must receive an ordinary function value, and the resulting payload must remain hello. A removes a forwarding-only lambda. Lee still writes a lambda when adding defaults, reordering arguments or doing extra work. Unit cases and unrepresentable callable signatures keep their current boundaries.
decisions.detail:
## Improved unanswered ballot

The example now passes a constructor through an actual function parameter and inspects the payload. Both options print hello. This avoids relying on unspecified enum display text or presenting a stored function as the whole user job.

## Exact ordinary-callable contract

A qualified eligible payload constructor without call arguments denotes an ordinary capture-free function value. Its checked payload parameter list and enum result supply the signature. Reuse the same Fn representation, binder, S30 public labels, parameter zones, effects and call-site obligations as ordinary functions. Do not create Constructor<T>, a constructor protocol, an enum factory object, a runtime case registry or a reflection-based invocation path.

Eligibility is deliberately ordinary. The signature must be representable under the current function-type law. Single payloads remain positional. Named payloads retain their existing public labels and parameter zones; they do not become a new anonymous record argument. Declaration-local names do not acquire function-type identity. Never erase a public label, view provenance, write requirement or move requirement to make a constructor fit an expected type.

S47 currently leaves write/move-parameter named functions direct-call-only where their requirements cannot be represented by a function type. A gives constructors no exception. Reject an unrepresentable first-class use with the ordinary source diagnostic. The user can keep direct construction or a lawful explicitly typed wrapper; this ballot does not claim that any wrapper can defeat ownership checking.

Only qualified payload constructors gain this meaning. Leading-dot shorthand does not start inferring an enum result from an expected function type. Unit cases remain enum values; Message.Quit does not turn into fn() Message. A caller needing that factory writes an ordinary zero-argument lambda.

Direct constructor calls remain unchanged. Generic arguments and expected-type inference use the existing callable rules. Unresolved type arguments, incompatible payload types and wrong arity remain source errors. Do not add return-type-only overload selection or a special generic inference engine. Preserve current namespace and duplicate-member rules.

Use D-CALLVALUE1=B unchanged: a stored plain-name function can be called normally; a callable call result uses .call(...). Do not add a constructor-specific call spelling. Derive the function signature and direct construction lowering from the same checked case declaration used by matching and metadata. Reflection describes that declaration; it does not instantiate payloads, authorize private construction or manufacture values by name.

A has no captured environment, but this is not a measured allocation or dispatch claim. The existing ordinary function-value representation determines lowering. Do not require a constructor object or heap box solely because the value originated at a case.

## Alternative B

B keeps current constructor lookup and explicit lambda adapters. A lambda can also select defaults, reorder arguments or add behavior. That useful capability remains available under A. B adds no new first-class constructor meaning.

## Proof after ratification

Reproduce the captured no-call payload-constructor failure and the equivalent lambda. Run the same helper program under A, checking hello from both paths. Cover unit cases, generic resolution, named/public-label obligations, incompatible callable signatures and refusal to erase move/write/view requirements. Preserve direct construction and ordinary .call routing. Prove the applicable I9 execution paths; no current-tree runtime result is claimed here.

## Evidence

examples/features/functions/named_function_value.jet:1-12 establishes the existing fn(Int) Int helper shape. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:323-345 records S47 and D-CALLVALUE1=B. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:6918-6920 routes the current no-call enum field path through check_enum_lit. The frozen constructor witness and original references remain in docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f36-constructor-callable-values.

D-CALLVALUE1=B, D-APILABEL1, D-MEMPROVENANCE3, S30, S47 and I1-I9 remain law. No Core module, optional package, dependency, token or parser production is added. This revision changes an unanswered proposal only.

decisions.title: Local callable reading view
decisions.gist: Should one selected function show its checked consequences before detailed records?
decisions.lesson: A checked consequence is a fact the checker derived, such as a possible failure or an effect. A runtime observation is what actually happened. Jet records these facts, but separate views make Mina join them. A adds an optional summary; B keeps separate views. Neither changes source syntax or checking.
decisions.story: Mina edits question_path, which calls with_guards(false). Before reading details, she wants the likely failure and the next reachable statement. A summarizes Int !Fail, the call, and checked effects, then labels cleanup execution as unknown. B leaves her to open the effect and signature views and combine them herself.
decisions.detail:
## design away record

Removed mandatory display cost: the view is opt-in and collapsible.

Removed new source ceremony: no syntax or per-function annotation is added.

Removed duplicate analysis risk: all fields project existing checked facts and identities.

Reduced false authority: distinguish checked from observed, and unavailable from empty; keep source/build identity and truncation visible.

Retained honest residual losses: an open view still needs space, and summaries still omit detail.

## Recommendation reasoning

A answers Mina’s local question first, then links to proof details. It marks cleanup as unobserved rather than claiming that the summary ran the program.

Option B: B preserves the facts but makes Mina assemble the failure and effect story across views. A leaves those detailed views available.

Any necessary transport shape is part of this product decision and must remain a projection of existing facts.

decisions.title: Program source sites in core.log records
decisions.gist: Should each core.log record identify the Jet source site that emitted it?
decisions.lesson: A source site is the exact program location that made a log call. A message is its text, and an event field is an author-chosen label. Jet records structured fields, but current evidence points to the library emitter rather than the Jet call. A adds compiler-bound site data; B keeps event fields only. Redaction and source policy stay in force.
decisions.story: Mina searches a translated or redacted “Saved” record. The event key row.saved helps, but several callers may use it. A lets her match the record to the exact run function and source digest. B leaves that match to a manual lookup. Both keep the same message and hide token values.
decisions.inWild:
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(pathname)s:%(lineno)d %(message)s [%(event)s]")
item = "row"
logging.info("Saved %s", item, extra={"event": "row.saved"})
decisions.detail:
## Complete technical contract

### record shape

An optional site object in the existing log record/envelope: availability is known, redacted or unavailable. Known requires compiler source_id, real relative file/line/column and source_sha256. Include a Jet function name only when available, reusing existing optional source-identity encoding. Other states do not invent a zero line, empty success, generated-Rust site or current-source substitution. Downstream consumers compare source hash before navigation and show stale mismatch.

### identity

Preserve the current low-level emitter identity separately. The new site identifies the immediate Jet call. This is not a stable business-event ID, logical caller inference, full stack trace or proof that a runtime result is correct.

### ordinary surface

Existing log.info/info_fields/warn/error/debug calls and LogField builders stay unchanged. Source metadata comes through existing compiler/source-map machinery, not a new source keyword or annotation.

### privacy and cost

Do not add source text, argument/local values, absolute paths or full stacks by default. Respect current redaction/export policy. Do not format/allocate per-record site metadata for disabled/filtered-out records; measure emitted-record and compilation/runtime cost.

### versioning

One versioned addition to the current record protocol; no second telemetry envelope, artifact kind or sink family.

### distribution

This is an in-place stock core.log functionality addition under D-LOGTRACE1 and D-OBS3’s std-only logging placement. External exporters remain optional FFI-wrapped packages and never compiler dependencies. No new CoreLib or dependency is proposed.

### proof

READ-F11 is the existing-capability comparator. READ-F17 verifies identical messages at different sites, wrappers, composition/translation, redaction, unavailable mappings, source edits and applicable execution paths on one source-matched build. Source-only capture is not proof that current output or the proposal works.

### authority

D-FOUND-COREAPI1=A accepts exactly its eleven listed additions. This unlisted record addition requires D-READ-LOGSITE1.

### worked record

ballot-example-data.json binds complete read-logsite.jet bytes and source hash to the proposed JSON site. The record is only the proposed additive payload, not a new envelope or observed log output. read-logsite.jet is a concrete fixture source identity; production uses the existing compiler source identity. No placeholder values or fabricated runtime IDs are shown.

## corelib change

### library

core.log

### addition

compiler-bound immediate emitting-site metadata in existing records

### placement

stock/std-only current core.log; optional exporters retain existing package placement

### dependency

none

### gate

D-READ-LOGSITE1

## design away record

Reuse existing compiler-owned facts, identities, APIs and protocols; no second index, analyzer or dependency.

Keep ordinary source calls unchanged; request or expand detail only when needed.

Represent stale, redacted, unsupported and unavailable facts explicitly rather than invent values.

Retain source/build and captured-versus-executed limits; comparative usefulness and cost still require scoped proof.

## Recommendation reasoning

A links Mina’s record to the exact call without treating message text as an ID. It keeps redaction, manual event keys and unavailable sites explicit.

Option B: B keeps useful event keys but cannot certify which source call produced a record. A adds that relation without changing the call.

decisions.title: Preview a signature change with explicit caller values
decisions.gist: Should Jet preview a signature change after the user chooses each new caller value?
decisions.lesson: A signature is a function’s name, parameters and result. Adding a parameter changes the function and every caller. Jet already knows checked symbol identities and typed edits. A previews those edits after Mira chooses each value; B leaves the multi-file migration manual. Both require correct identities, source locations and document versions.
decisions.story: Mira adds offset: Int to scoring.letter. Her old call letter(91) now needs a value; she chooses 0, so the job remains A. A previews the declaration and exact caller edit before applying it. B asks Mira to find, edit and check each caller herself. Unknown callers stay visible instead of being guessed.
decisions.detail:
Use one checked declaration identity from jet-semindex and the existing dependency/query service.

Hold a consistent set of source snapshots.

Build the preview as ordinary typed edits and stage them in overlays, not on disk.

Every caller expression must be supplied or explicitly selected by the user.

Include resolved direct calls, aliases and overload/implementation identity where the checked graph supports them.

Higher-order uses, generated declarations and external consumers must be resolved or listed as blocking a claim of complete automatic migration.

Serialize standard versioned LSP workspace edits; reject changed versions.

Recheck with the existing front end.

Compilation establishes only language validity, not the business correctness of the chosen values.

No new command, JSON schema, effect analysis, syntax, dependency or invariant exemption is part of this choice.

Identity, snapshot and diagnostic-origin correctness are prerequisites, not alternate ballot options.

Distribution choice is explicit: option A places this action in the existing stock Jet LSP; option B adds no action.

A separate optional adapter or dependency is not adopted by this ballot.

Neither adds another checker or guesses from error codes alone.

decisions.title: Keep a review attached to its exact checked inputs
decisions.gist: Should a saved semantic review identify both checked snapshots and its proof inputs?
decisions.lesson: A semantic review is a saved conclusion about two source versions. Provenance means the identities of the inputs and proof records used. Jet already records hashes and authenticated claims, but the captured review object does not state both complete input sets. A stores paired provenance with the review; B keeps it in a sidecar. Neither uploads source or calls an unknown closure complete.
decisions.story: Mira changes scoring.jet while run.jet and util.jet stay identical. She saves a review, then opens it later. A keeps both snapshot input lists beside the conclusion, with closure unknown when no proof receipt exists. B leaves those hashes in a separate sidecar that Mira must keep paired with the review.
decisions.detail:
Propose schema jet.review/v2 on the existing semantic-review object.

The new snapshots.base/head records have entry:String, inputs:[{path:String,digest:String}], claim_key:?String, closure:complete|entry_only|unknown, and proof_receipt:?{path:String,digest:String}.

Reuse ReceiptStores existing canonical input rows and claim key; no second hash authority, cache or provenance store.

The entry hash is its inputs row, not duplicated as another independently maintained field.

Capture rows from the checked source buffers and proof bytes, never a later filesystem reread.

The claim_key may be absent even when some file hashes are known.

Completeness is relative to the declared checker scope; known rows alone do not prove complete closure or authenticated currentness.

Preserve existing semantic-operation, authority and receipt-comparison fields; the surface shows only the relevant projection, not a whole response.

No provider adapter, upload or new export command.

Existing jet report stays its private source-free support bundle.

decisions.title: Preserve the locations of diagnostic causes
decisions.gist: Should a canonical diagnostic report keep each cause’s location, not only its code?
decisions.lesson: A diagnostic cause explains why a reported error exists. A location identifies the source occurrence that supplies that cause. Jet keeps cause spans internally, but the current canonical report serializes only code strings. A keeps each code with its location; B keeps strings. Both retain registered codes and existing editor-related locations.
decisions.story: A formatter receives E0107 at line 9 with two E0107 causes at lines 8 and 6. The codes match, but the locations do not. A preserves both source occurrences so an editor can navigate to each one. B emits ["E0107", "E0107"], so a reader cannot tell which cause came from which line. The chain is authored serialization input, not an observed compiler causal trace.

decisions.title: How should kernels share a temporary array?
decisions.gist: Should checked kernels expose workgroup arrays and barriers?
decisions.lesson: `grid:[256]` starts 256 runs; `workgroup:[256]` puts them in one cooperating group. `local_linear` numbers members; `workgroup_linear` numbers groups. A needs indexed-resource A's writable output. Its barrier waits for every member before shared reads. Moving `buffer` consumes it even on a returned error; retry needs new output storage. B sums axis zero into shape `[1]`, intending `[5559680]`.
decisions.story: Maya squares a workgroup of samples and reduces them. She needs an explicit shared temporary without turning the custom algorithm into unchecked foreign code.
decisions.detail:
## Practical limits of the chosen group admission

A needs a shared-array bound known at compile time and complete cooperating groups. With 257 inputs and a group size of 256, the caller cannot request 257 cooperating runs unchanged. It can explicitly pad the logical domain with guarded reads or handle leftovers through a separate route. If padding produces two group totals, combine them before comparing with B's single whole-input sum. No automatic padding, unmatched output or hidden CPU fallback is permitted.

Moving the preallocated output consumes it even if launch returns a validation or device-capability error. Retrying requires new output storage. These practical consequences are distinct from the non-negotiable rule that every member reaches the barrier. The barrier rule stays in the contract; it is not presented as a cost unique to safe programming.

## Pre-ratification performance gate: option A is blocked

The canonical matched candidate/plain programs and a strict measured win are both missing. This is a pre-ratification blocker for option A, not an optional implementation benchmark. The author recommendation remains unchanged and conditional; it is not readiness or owner approval.

A workgroup_array/barrier sum-of-squares versus the complete B scalar square launch plus sum_axis, with the redundant reshape removed from the measured plain program. Preserve ascending F32 accumulation and shape[1]; measure larger matched workload, setup, shared/global storage, transfers and strict numeric controls.

For each required matched metric and cell, divide the candidate surface cost by the plain cost. The result must be strictly below 1. Equality, missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. The Rust peer parity band is not a candidate/plain win. Target identity and measurement boundaries must be explicit.

Source counts, NOT RUN programs, frozen e841 snapshot receipts and reader approval cannot satisfy this gate. No canonical pair ID or evidence record exists for this choice. The other option remains a real choice, but cannot approve this gated API or bypass its independently named prerequisites.

Explicit source-work, memory or hardware-reuse advantage in the complete source alternatives.

Keep the original authored B fixture as provenance. The measured plain baseline must remove its redundant reshape([1]) and consume sum_axis output directly. Shape remains[1], and the option and meaning do not change. This source clarification is not a measured win.

## Beginner repair: group positions and the reduction axis

`grid:[256]` requests256 logical runs, not 256 groups. `workgroup:[256]` puts those runs in one complete group. Its `workgroup_linear` is0; its `local_linear` values are 0 through 255. Every member writes its own shared square, then reaches the barrier. Member zero later reads the 256 published squares in ascending order and writes output0. Only this last store is restricted to member zero; the barrier is not.

A requires D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1=A for its writable output parameter. Choosing indexed-resource B does not secretly enable this program. The separate constructor and helper decisions also remain independent. The short surface names its fixture values; both complete option programs below retain the imports, list construction and allocation needed to see where those values come from.

An axis is one dimension, numbered from zero. `products` has shape `[256]`: one axis with 256 entries. `sum_axis(products,0)` adds that whole dimension. The captured Core source removes the selected axis, then uses `[1]` if no axes remain. Its declared output shape is `[1]`; this paper job’s intended value is 5559680. Axis 1 is invalid for this rank-one input and returns an out-of-bounds error; zero is not a starting element or a mode.

The authored B fixture's `reshape(reduced,[1])` changes `[1]` into `[1]`. It is redundant, not a conversion from a rank-zero scalar.
