Equality, missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. The Rust peer parity band is not a candidate/plain win. Target identity and measurement boundaries must be explicit.

Source counts, NOT RUN programs, frozen e841 snapshot receipts and reader approval cannot satisfy this gate. No canonical pair ID or evidence record exists for this choice. The other option remains a real choice, but cannot approve this gated API or bypass its independently named prerequisites.

Explicit source-work, memory or hardware-reuse advantage in the complete source alternatives.

## Beginner repair: the required lane-to-input relation

The draft's logical numbering rule is explicit: for requested subgroup size S, `at.subgroup_lane` equals `at.linear % S`. Each complete subgroup contains S consecutive logical positions in increasing input order. Workgroup boundaries must preserve these complete groups. This rule is part of proposed B's contract, not an assumption about whatever physical lane numbering a GPU happens to expose. A provider that cannot preserve it must reject the requested variant before work.

For the shown S=32 job, linear positions and subgroup lanes are both 0 through 31. Lane k supplies the square of input k. Reading source lane `(k+1)%32` therefore obtains the next input's square; lane 31 reads lane 0. Changing the source lane to 0 makes every member in this single subgroup read input 0's square. For a later subgroup beginning at position 32, lane 0 instead carries input 32. It is not global input 0.

All members must call the same shuffle with compatible types and the declared complete group. A call reached only by lane zero rejects. Different source-lane arguments are permitted within that one collective call, but each requested source lane must be in range and participating. These definitions repair the missing mapping; they do not prove a backend implements it. The fixed32-member teaching case is NOT RUN.

A positive power of two is reached by starting at 1 and repeatedly doubling:1,2,4,8,16,32,64. For example,24 fails this arithmetic rule. Passing it does not establish device support. The requested size must also be supported by the actual backend, and the grid and workgroup must form complete groups of that size.

A register is a run's private working-value storage. A shuffle obtains another member's supplied value without borrowing that member's storage. It does not publish arbitrary array writes. For example, writing a shared array and shuffling an unrelated number does not make later shared reads safe. That storage-sharing job still needs its own checked synchronization and ownership rules. F32 is a limited-precision fractional-number type; the shuffle must preserve the supplied value's bits, not recompute it.

For the shown S=32 job, linear positions and subgroup lanes are both 0 through 31. Lane k supplies the square of input k. decisions.title: How should checked kernels count shared buckets?
decisions.gist: Should kernels use existing atomic cells or avoid contended writes?
decisions.lesson: A counts each input into a shared cell. B scans inputs once for each bucket. Both intend `[1,3]`. `^` moves owned cells: construction takes `cells`, launch takes `counts`, and readback takes `out`. `output:^counts` supplies the kernel's final parameter. A returned error still consumes the moved owner. A's required candidate/plain performance proof is missing.
decisions.story: Inez counts parity buckets from integer IDs. She wants shared updates without raw pointers or a second atomic model.
decisions.detail:
## What differs from the non-atomic alternative

A may reject a provider on which B's non-atomic counting can run, because A needs the complete existing atomic contract. This is conditional: no particular provider is established usable by this draft, and B still needs its own admitted operations. Neither route gains permission to weaken ordering or reinterpret numeric storage.

A also consumes actual cell owners through transfer and on a returned error; retry requires newly allocated cells. B's numeric readback is not that consuming overload. Generic GPU readback and compliance with safety rules are not independent disadvantages unique to A. The device restriction and cell-recovery consequence are the choice-relevant differences. No timing cost or automatic fallback is inferred.

## Pre-ratification performance gate: option A is blocked

The canonical matched candidate/plain programs and a strict measured win are both missing. This is a pre-ratification blocker for option A, not an optional implementation benchmark. The author recommendation remains unchanged and conditional; it is not readiness or owner approval.

A owned Atomic<U32> histogram versus complete B noncontending per-bucket scan. Include moving actual cells, device encoding, initialized output, launch, owning readback, and larger matched bucket/input distributions. Preserve existing ordering, wrap, nonblocking progress and ownership.

For each required matched metric and cell, divide the candidate surface cost by the plain cost. The result must be strictly below 1. Equality, missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. The Rust peer parity band is not a candidate/plain win. Target identity and measurement boundaries must be explicit.

Source counts, NOT RUN programs, frozen e841 snapshot receipts and reader approval cannot satisfy this gate. No canonical pair ID or evidence record exists for this choice. The other option remains a real choice, but cannot approve this gated API or bypass its independently named prerequisites.

Explicit source-work, memory or hardware-reuse advantage in the complete source alternatives.

## Beginner repair: following the actual cells

Read the owner chain literally: `cells` is the initialized list of Atomic<U32> cells. `from_list(^cells)` consumes that list and returns the owning Tensor named `counts`. `output:^counts` consumes that owner and binds the kernel's final atomic-output parameter. A successful launch returns the completed owner named `out`. `to_list(^out)` consumes it and returns owned host cells named `cells_out`. Ordinary readback of numeric data is not a substitute for moving these cells.

After each move, the old name cannot be reused. No surviving host loan or host reference may expose the moved device cells. A returned failure still consumes the owner and returns neither restored cells nor partial output. Allocate new cells to retry. A compile-time rejected program never starts; do not confuse that with the returned runtime-error case. These remain proposed admission and transfer rules, not exercised GPU behavior.

U32 stores whole numbers from 0 through 4294967295. Adding 1 to 4294967295 reaches 4294967296, so wrapping removes one complete group of 4294967296 and stores 0. The existing add operation returns the old value. Thus an add at that boundary returns 4294967295 while the cell becomes 0. The tiny `[1,3]` histogram does not reach this boundary and cannot establish it experimentally.

Linearizability means each add appears to take effect at one indivisible instant between its call and return. If two runs each add1 to a zero cell, their returned old values must be0 and 1 in some assignment, never both 0. The final count is2. Jet's stronger ordinary ordering must also provide one order respecting each participant's program order. Merely avoiding a lost increment does not establish that whole ordering contract.

CUDA's shown relaxed device-scope add covers participating threads on that device. By itself it does not publish earlier unrelated writes to another observer. For existing Jet publish/observe, an observer that sees a publication must see writes that preceded it, where ordinary sharing rules permit access. This explanation does not admit GPU Bool cells or concurrent host/device access. Those are not additions hidden inside this U32 ballot.

Where ordinary sharing rules permit access, a writer stores 7, then publishes a ready signal. An observer that sees that publication must see 7 if no later write changed the data. Seeing the older 0 would violate the rule. This is a conceptual example of the existing promise, not a new shared-host/device API or GPU Bool admission.

A lock holder is a participant whose permission must be released before another proceeds. The required nonblocking progress rule cannot depend on a paused holder releasing a hidden lock. Layout, target size and alignment, transfer encoding, sequential consistency, linearizability, progress and device loss all still require proof. CUDA atomicAdd alone supplies none of that combined proof.

Integrity limit: the earlier Core capture's Atomic.rs digest has 65 hex digits and cannot attest its seven historical snippets. Its retained source readings are not verified historical-byte or device-layout proof. Do not repair that provenance by substituting today's digest. The proposal's conditional admission requirements remain unchanged, and no host AtomicU64 representation authorizes a device reinterpretation.

## CUDA notation used by the comparison

These CUDA adaptations are source illustrations, not executed programs or Jet approval. `__global__` marks a launch entry; `__device__` marks a device-callable helper. `const float*` is a pointer to input floating-point values that this function may not modify. A writable output pointer exposes storage without Jet's checked view proof. `threadIdx.x` is a worker's local position; `blockIdx.x` numbers its group and `blockDim.x` is that group's size.

The expression blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x gives a global position for these one-dimensional launches. `<<<blocks,threads>>>` supplies the group count and group size. A guard excludes positions outside the logical input. The surface's comparison note explains the operation specific to this ballot. These meanings let the small examples be traced; they do not turn CUDA's contracts into evidence for Jet's proposed guarantees.

## Unchanged evidence and prerequisite boundary

Every independently named prerequisite remains a separate owner choice. A snippet showing a prerequisite's A spelling does not ratify that spelling. No reader observation, source calculation or source excerpt is execution proof. Existing frozen receipts keep their snapshot-only scope; the frozen executable is not source-equated to the current tree. This repair changes documentation only. The complete programs, exact API alternatives and inherited failure and ownership rules below remain author drafts.

Sequential consistency gives ordinary operations one order that respects each participant’s source order. Publish/observe instead establish the selected release/acquire visibility link. Nonblocking progress is a property of the complete operation: it cannot wait for a lock holder. It does not promise every participant a fixed completion time.

A admits the existing Atomic<U32> family inside checked kernels, without reinterpreting ordinary numeric storage. It adds the exact owning constructor overload `compute.from_list(values:^[Atomic<U32>]) Tensor<Atomic<U32>> !ComputeError`. Moving the list transfers its initialized atomic cells into the existing Tensor owner. It does not clone their identities or manufacture atoms from Tensor<U32> bytes. This owning overload is distinct from numeric borrowed construction by its actual element and ownership types, not a second owner family.

The kernel's final `View<Atomic<U32>>` parameter identifies the supplied atomic output. The caller must provide `output:^counts` of type Tensor<Atomic<U32>>. There is no inferred fresh atomic output: the explicit initialized cells determine its extent and starting values. Launch returns the same completed Tensor<Atomic<U32>>. Ordinary input/output alias checks and exclusive transfer rules remain. Concurrent invocations may call the existing atomic methods on the same cell; plain reads or writes to its representation are forbidden.

A also adds the owning readback overload `compute.to_list(tensor:^Tensor<Atomic<U32>>) [Atomic<U32>] !ComputeError`. It transfers the completed cell states back to an owned host list before ordinary host load calls. The example then loads the two returned cells. Numeric to_list retains its existing contract; it does not silently become this consuming operation. An error consumes the moved owner and returns no partial list.

A caller must allocate fresh cells and retry explicitly if recovery is required.

Atomic cells are non-copy storage. No live host cell reference may survive a move into the tensor or device launch. Device-owned atomic storage cannot yield a host Atomic reference to device bytes. Host references become available only after the owning readback succeeds. Reshape, view projection and transfer may preserve the one owner only when their ordinary ownership and address-space rules permit it.

Numeric algebra, raw serialization or a cloning conversion cannot treat an atomic tensor as ordinary U32 data. This admission supplies no concurrent CPU/GPU access to one cell.

The captured current host implementation carries U32 in AtomicU64. That is an implementation fact, not a ratified promise that every device uses an eight-byte cell. The device target must have an explicit compatible cell encoding, width, alignment and transfer contract. Exclusive transfer moves logical cell state through that checked encoding; it never casts a four-byte numeric buffer to a host Atomic layout. Each target's real representation must be recorded and proved.

The device encoding must preserve the selected one-word cell law and every target-visible size, alignment and layout fact. This design adds no layout exception to D-PLACE1 or D-ATOMIC-WIDTH1.

Existing ordinary load, store, add and compare_exchange remain sequentially consistent. Publish and observe retain release/acquire intent. No order argument, relaxed user operation, hidden lock or extra atomic family is added. Add returns the old value and fixed U32 addition wraps as already ratified. The complete operation must preserve its nonblocking progress promise, not merely use one atomic instruction at the end. Fixed-width operations must not enter an exact-number allocator.

All concurrent observers of these moved cells are within the selected device operation. Its atomic ordering must cover those observers and the completed ownership transfer. A provider that only supplies relaxed atomicAdd is not sufficient evidence. Unsupported target semantics reject during declaration or variant admission. A dynamically selected unsupported provider fails before submission. CPU reference uses the same atomic meaning; it cannot masquerade as the requested GPU. No compatible GPU is currently proved by this draft.

B keeps GPU work noncontending. It launches one run per bucket, scans the same four input IDs and writes one unique result. A launches one run per input ID and atomically increments its parity bucket. Both produce [1,3]. A makes four source input visits; B makes eight. Those counts are algorithm facts, not timing or physical memory measurements. A has stronger storage and ordering requirements; B is a real checked alternative that may suit small histograms.

Parity means remainder after division by two. Thus0 contributes to bucket0, while each1 contributes to bucket1. Modulo2 proves the bucket is either zero or one. Starting cells are both zero. The sum is independent of update order because the final U32 counts use the existing modular addition law. Floating atomic addition is not admitted as a strict reproducible reduction.

Negative examples. Supplying Tensor<U32> as the atomic output is a type error, not a reinterpretation request. Keeping a host reference to a cell while moving its owner is an ownership error. A provider without the required ordering or progress proof rejects the kernel variant. Proposed explanations must identify the incompatible type, live loan or missing atomic capability. Repair by using owned Atomic cells, ending the loan, or choosing a supported device or B.

Weakening the order is not a repair.

Required proof remains substantial: layout encoding, move/readback identity, cell lifetime, global ordering, cross-invocation linearizability, progress and device loss. The packet supplies an exact public proposal, not evidence that those obligations are solved by current source. The stronger-contract prerequisite must stay on the implementation card and block any unsupported provider claim.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-PLACE1=A and D-ATOMIC-WIDTH1=A are preserved. D-GPU-U32-SCOPE1=A supplies numeric U32 resources. D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 supplies the checked resource/owner binding. D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1 supplies bounded loop proof for B. Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

decisions.title: Should matrix tiles become public kernel values?
decisions.gist: Should tile optimization stay internal or become an explicit checked kernel value?
decisions.lesson: A uses existing matrix operations. B's tile is one table value shared by a complete workgroup, not four independent stores. `grid:[4]` and `workgroup:[4]` make one four-member group. Four members need not mean four tile cells. The matrix product is `[[-9,-10],[-13,-14]]`; adding ten and replacing negatives with zero gives `[1,0,0,0]`.
decisions.story: Mira combines matrix multiplication, a bias and a zero floor. She wants useful GPU execution without learning a tile protocol unnecessarily.
decisions.detail:
## Arithmetic check that the clamp cannot hide

The second row is 3*5−4*7=−13 and 3*6−4*8=−14. With bias 14, all four intermediate results are [5,4,1,0], so the final result is also[5,4,1,0]. Bias 10 and 11 hide a mistaken negative second row by turning it into zero. This bias 14 change exposes that mistake. These are paper calculations from the unchanged inputs, not executed results.

## Pre-ratification performance gate: option B is blocked

The canonical matched candidate/plain programs and a strict measured win are both missing. This is a pre-ratification blocker for option B, not an optional implementation benchmark. The author recommendation remains unchanged and conditional; it is not readiness or owner approval.

B Tile pipeline versus complete A existing-operation sequence. The 2x2 teaching case is not sufficient speed evidence. Use larger identical matrices, strict stage errors, rounding-sensitive controls, compilation/cache costs, allocations, transfers and collective failure behavior.

For each required matched metric and cell, divide the candidate surface cost by the plain cost. The result must be strictly below 1. Equality, missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. The Rust peer parity band is not a candidate/plain win. Target identity and measurement boundaries must be explicit.

Source counts, NOT RUN programs, frozen e841 snapshot receipts and reader approval cannot satisfy this gate. No canonical pair ID or evidence record exists for this choice. The other option remains a real choice, but cannot approve this gated API or bypass its independently named prerequisites.

Explicit source-work, memory or hardware-reuse advantage in the complete source alternatives.

## Beginner repair: arithmetic and one collective store

The tables contain two rows and two columns. For each product cell, multiply the matching left-row and right-column entries, then add in the specified order. The worked product is `[[-9,-10],[-13,-14]]`. Adding the bias ten gives `[[1,0],[-3,-4]]`. Replacing negatives with zero gives `[[1,0],[0,0]]`. Bias eleven instead gives `[2,1,0,0]` in row order. These calculations explain the intended answers; neither Jet alternative was executed.

The size controls count runs, not cells. `grid:[4]` starts four runs; `workgroup:[4]` puts all four in one group. Every member participates in each collective tile operation. The group owns one logical tile result and performs one cooperative store, not four independent overlapping stores. Choosing four members for four cells is a teaching fixture, not a rule that group size must equal tile element count. Internal cell distribution is not an author-visible second ownership scheme.

With otherwise unchanged `grid:[8]` and `workgroup:[4]`, there are two groups. Both would use the same origins and destination tile; the checked store-ownership proof must reject that overlap. Changing both sizes to 8 makes one eight-member group, but is only legal if the backend supports that complete collective variant. It does not create an eight-cell tile. No silently partial group, padding or duplicate output owner is permitted.

B also requires the separately chosen indexed output, ranked resource and workgroup contracts. This ballot does not ratify those prerequisite APIs. `[Int#2]` means a fixed two-entry collection of Int coordinates or dimensions; `{0,0}` gives its two values. The load's origin pair names row and column; its shape pair gives two lengths. Changing the collection's count is not admission of a higher-rank Tile API.

Every arithmetic stage must preserve its specified rounding and failures. A later zero clamp cannot hide an earlier numeric failure. Collective failure transport must return no partial output. The 2x2 example teaches those semantics; it is not performance evidence or proof of a hardware matrix instruction. B remains blocked until its larger, complete, strict candidate/plain comparison and all capability proofs exist.

## CUDA notation used by this comparison

A CUDA block is one cooperating worker group. `fused<<<1,dim3(2,2)>>>` requests one block with two columns and two rows. `threadIdx.x` selects column 0 or 1; `threadIdx.y` selects row 0 or 1. The four coordinate pairs are (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1). The `__global__` function is the launch entry. This is a two-dimensional block, not four different x positions.

Each worker copies one left operand into `a[row][col]` and one right operand into `b[row][col]`. These arrays are shared inputs, not shared products. Every worker reaches `__syncthreads()` before reading the needed row and column. Its `value` accumulator is private. Each then writes its distinct `out[row*2+col]` place. The four workers initialize both complete input tables before use. This adaptation is NOT RUN and does not prove Jet’s proposed Tile behavior.

## Unchanged evidence and prerequisite boundary

Every independently named prerequisite remains a separate owner choice. A snippet showing a prerequisite's A spelling does not ratify that spelling. No reader observation, source calculation or source excerpt is execution proof. Existing frozen receipts keep their snapshot-only scope; the frozen executable is not source-equated to the current tree. This repair changes documentation only. The complete programs, exact API alternatives and inherited failure and ownership rules below remain author drafts.

A keeps tile optimization behind existing Core tensor operations. It adds no Tile type or tile intrinsic. The ordinary program uses matmul, add and maximum on explicitly placed F32 tensors. Source reading also found the existing two-argument matmul_f32_tile operation. It owns a fixed F32 matmul/profile path, not an authored tile value or arbitrary fused epilogue. A neither deletes nor silently redefines that existing operation. Its implementation and any canonicalization stay under the already selected Core laws.

A may fuse or tile operations only when aliasing, effects, errors and numeric order remain identical. Otherwise it must retain the ordinary operation boundaries. No single-dispatch, no-intermediate-allocation or Tensor Core instruction promise follows from the public source. Those are measured implementation facts. The Vulkan request in the fixture is explicit; unsupported operations fail, never switch to CPU.

B adds a kernel-only `compute.Tile<F32>` value and five exact operations. `load_tile(at:Invocation, source:View<F32>, origin:[Int#2], shape:[Int#2]) Tile<F32>` loads an in-bounds rectangle. `tile_matmul(at:Invocation, left:Tile<F32>, right:Tile<F32>) Tile<F32>` multiplies two compatible tiles. `tile_add(at:Invocation, tile:Tile<F32>, scalar:F32) Tile<F32>` adds a uniform scalar. `tile_maximum(at:Invocation, tile:Tile<F32>, floor:F32) Tile<F32>` applies the existing maximum meaning.

`store_tile(at:Invocation, output:ViewMut<F32>, origin:[Int#2], tile:Tile<F32>)` stores that rectangle.

Tile is a bounded collective calculation value, not another owner for external tensor storage. Its shape must resolve to positive compile-time dimensions. Its fragments belong to one complete workgroup and cannot escape the kernel. There is no public constructor, host tile pointer, mutable shape field, or cross-workgroup tile exchange. The underlying fixed values reuse Core representation. Every operation carries the sealed Invocation context and must be called uniformly by its workgroup.

Scalar operands and shape/origin choices are uniform within that group.

The five operations are checked kernel operations. Shape, ownership and access preconditions must be proved or checked before the authored dispatch. Each arithmetic stage retains the declared Core F32 error policy. A non-finite arithmetic stage that ordinary Core rejects must fail the enclosing launch with the existing ComputeError.Arithmetic, even if a later clamp could hide it. No intermediate result or partially written Tensor is exposed.

This is part of the proposed kernel operation contract, not an assertion that the current compiler transports such failures. The shared checked program must carry those failure facts; a provider cannot invent a second exception policy.

The implementation must make a collective failure uniform and preserve required participation while completing or safely ending the operation. It cannot let one lane return early and strand others at a tile synchronization point. This failure-path requirement is an explicit prerequisite for B, including the CPU reference and device-loss paths. If the common kernel error transport cannot satisfy it, B is not implementation-ready; that is not permission to weaken the error rule.

B uses the existing ranked views and the write-view output contract. Each collective store must produce one owner of each written destination, despite all members calling the collective operation. Overlapping writes from separate workgroups reject. Input/output byte overlap rejects. Full in-bounds tiles need no hidden padding. An edge needs an explicit smaller specialization, explicit padding, or a separately proved ordinary edge program. Padding/copies must appear in the measurement.

No out-of-bounds zero-fill is implied by load_tile.

F32Strict uses the same multiply, add and reduction order as the ordinary operation. No implicit TF32/FP16 conversion, FMA contraction or reassociation is authorized. A matrix instruction is permitted only when it preserves that exact policy. Otherwise the selected GPU may use ordinary F32 instructions. That remains a GPU execution strategy, not a CPU fallback. A receipt must not label ordinary instructions as Tensor Core acceleration.

The example multiplies [1,-2;3,-4] by [5,6;7,8], giving [-9,-10;-13,-14]. Adding10 gives [1,0;-3,-4]. Replacing negatives with zero gives [1,0;0,0]. Thus the clamp is exercised, not a dead decoration. Both alternatives and CUDA have the same values and intended output. None of these complete new programs was run here.

Negative cases include mismatched inner dimensions, an out-of-bounds rectangle, a divergent collective, incompatible group origins and a numeric error hidden by a later maximum. Proposed errors must name the failed shape, participation or numeric obligation. Repair the dimensions, move the collective outside divergent control, or use an explicit legal edge program. Do not alter precision or fabricate a successful zero tile.

A is recommended because the full job already fits existing operations. B gives authors exact collective boundaries and tile value reuse, but adds a new concept and several kernel operations. Before performance-based ratification, the canonical candidate/plain cell must compare full setup, compilation, launches, temporary storage, transfers, edge handling and strict numeric errors. The2x2 teaching fixture is not a meaningful speed benchmark. Larger matched matrices and a rounding-sensitive control remain required.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1 supplies physical typed construction. B requires D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1=A, ranked views and workgroup admission. B cannot proceed without the stated common numeric-error and uniform-failure proof. Where shown, typed F32 from_list uses the recommended but unratified A of D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1. If that independent decision selects B, those same calls use from_list_f32; numeric and ownership meaning stay identical. No constructor spelling is ratified by this draft.

Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

// Same Vulkan fixture: a=[1,-2;3,-4], b=[5,6;7,8], buffer=zeros[2,2].
#Kernel(.parallel)
fn fused(at: compute.Invocation, a: View<F32>, b: View<F32>, out: ViewMut<F32>) {
    left :: compute.load_tile(at, a, [Int#2]{0,0}, [Int#2]{2,2})
    right :: compute.load_tile(at, b, [Int#2]{0,0}, [Int#2]{2,2})
    product :: compute.tile_matmul(at, left, right)
    biased :: compute.tile_add(at, product, F32{10})
    result :: compute.tile_maximum(at, biased, F32{0})
    compute.store_tile(at, out, [Int#2]{0,0}, result)
}

## Beginner repair: deriving the wrapping boundary

U32 stores whole numbers from 0 through 4294967295; negative numbers do not fit. There are 4294967296 possible values. The expression `2^32` here means multiplying 2 by itself 32 times, which equals4294967296. It does not mean multiplying 2 by 32. In this explanatory arithmetic, the caret means exponentiation; in Jet's shown call arguments, `^owner` instead means moving ownership.

Wrapping keeps the remainder after removing complete groups of 4294967296. Start with 4294967295. Multiplying by 3 gives 12884901885. Remove two groups, totaling 8589934592, to leave 4294967293. Adding 1 then gives 4294967294, already inside the range. This derives the stated boundary result after the two explicit wrapping operations. In the simpler boundary,4294967295 plus1 wraps to 0.

Checked arithmetic is different: a result outside the range must fail rather than wrap. The boundary multiplication already exceeds the range, so replacing the wrapping multiplication with checked multiplication must not produce the wrapped answer. A admits checked arithmetic only with a proved range or the same visible failure. If the backend cannot preserve that failure, it rejects this kernel variant. It cannot quietly change checked arithmetic into wrapping or floating arithmetic.

`.push(value)` appends one entry to the list; `.len()` counts entries. `[U32]{}` is an empty U32 list. With a valid compatible variant, empty input means zero invocations and an empty output list, not one zero value. Empty work is not a claimed GPU submission. To observe it, print the list itself. The shown first/last display must be changed: indexing its places 0 and 256 on an empty result would itself fail.

Omitting a device requests a compatible real GPU under the launch rule. An unavailable device or unsupported U32 variant returns an error, not hidden CPU work. Option B is the explicit CPU algorithm. Its frozen receipt cannot establish A's constructor, physical storage, device execution or speed. Four-byte physical U32 storage is a required admission fact, not an inference from an F32-labelled profile.

[INFERENCE] Offloading this exact integer job rather than running its explicit CPU alternative is conservatively treated as performance-motivated. No acceleration was observed. Do not reclassify that motivation to evade the pre-ratification strict-win gate. Construction, actual target, transfers, readback and wrapping boundaries must remain in the complete comparison.

## CUDA notation used by the comparison

These CUDA adaptations are source illustrations, not executed programs or Jet approval. `__global__` marks a launch entry; `__device__` marks a device-callable helper. `const float*` is a pointer to input floating-point values that this function may not modify. A writable output pointer exposes storage without Jet's checked view proof. `threadIdx.x` is a worker's local position; `blockIdx.x` numbers its group and `blockDim.x` is that group's size.

The expression blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x gives a global position for these one-dimensional launches. `<<<blocks,threads>>>` supplies the group count and group size. A guard excludes positions outside the logical input. The surface's comparison note explains the operation specific to this ballot. These meanings let the small examples be traced; they do not turn CUDA's contracts into evidence for Jet's proposed guarantees.

## Unchanged evidence and prerequisite boundary

Every independently named prerequisite remains a separate owner choice. A snippet showing a prerequisite's A spelling does not ratify that spelling. No reader observation, source calculation or source excerpt is execution proof. Existing frozen receipts keep their snapshot-only scope; the frozen executable is not source-equated to the current tree. This repair changes documentation only. The complete programs, exact API alternatives and inherited failure and ownership rules below remain author drafts.

A extends the existing Tensor/View and authored launch family to U32. The exact added constructor admission is `compute.from_list(values:[U32]) Tensor<U32> !ComputeError`; to_list of a U32 tensor returns [U32]. It preserves all32 bits and four-byte numeric elements, not a Float/F32/F64 representation or a retagged buffer. This U32 overload is part of this decision. The independent F32 constructor spelling decision remains independent; it does not change this explicitly shown U32 call.

A maps Tensor<U32> scalar inputs to U32 kernel parameters at the same logical position. Return-form kernels return one U32 per position. The indexed-resource amendment applies to View<U32> and ViewMut<U32> with the same ownership and proof rules. No mixed F32/U32 input coercion, integer widening, new buffer owner, profile that silently changes arithmetic, or alternate launch function is added. Other integer widths remain separate inventory cells.

Ordinary U32 arithmetic keeps its existing checked meaning. Explicit wrapping expressions keep modulo2^32 meaning. This first admission accepts wrapping operations and checked operations whose required range or failure contract is proved. An unproved checked-overflow path cannot silently wrap. Its admission remains blocked until the existing checked failure meaning is preserved across the reference and selected provider. This is a kernel proof restriction, not a new meaning for ordinary CPU U32 arithmetic.

The displayed affine function uses existing explicit wrapping at both multiplication and addition. For input i from zero through256, the intended output is3i+1:257 values from1 to769. The frozen CPU receipt exercised the full ordinary-array fixture, including every value check. It did not execute the proposed tensor constructor or GPU launch. The shorter B display is the same explicit CPU algorithm, not an additional runtime receipt.

A must record actual U32 dtype, layout, submitted program and selected device. A provider that lacks the required integer instructions, index width or checked meaning rejects before submission. CPU reference execution requires an explicit CPU choice. An omitted device cannot turn a GPU-required U32 launch into B's CPU loop.

B keeps authored GPU launch F32-only. The complete ordinary CPU code still computes exactly the requested integers. That is a real scope alternative, not a GPU-equivalent performance result. It deliberately gives up authored U32 execution on a GPU; no cast to F32 is offered as an equivalent substitute.

Boundary mutation. Keep257 inputs but replace the final value with U32{4294967295}. The wrapping function must return4294967294 at that position. This boundary has not been run in Jet here. It distinguishes32-bit modular arithmetic from floating conversion and wider arithmetic. Test empty input, the257-item tail, mismatched types/layouts and a nonwrapping overflow separately. A matched benchmark must include construction, transfer and physical U32 storage, not compare a CPU list with a claimed GPU label.

The example uses explicit wrapping; other checked arithmetic must preserve its existing failure meaning.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1 keeps the same call and completion contract. Indexed U32 resources follow the separately chosen indexed-resource rule. Every new spelling is a proposal. Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

Complete fixture context. This is explanatory evidence/proposal metadata, not an added public schema.

```json
{
  "status": "GPU_NOT_RUN",
  "input": {
    "U32_values": "all integers0 through256"
  },
  "expected": {
    "length": 257,
    "first": 1,
    "last": 769,
    "all": "3*i+1"
  },
  "overflow_mutation": {
    "last_input": 4294967295,
    "last_expected": 4294967294,
    "status": "NOT_RUN"
  },
  "observed_current": "coordination/probe-receipts/GPU-affine-cpu-default.json"
}
```

Complete proposed A program. Not executed or ratified.

```jet
use core.compute as compute
#Kernel(.parallel)
fn affine(value: U32) U32 -> wrapping(wrapping(value * 3) + 1)
fn run() {
    values := [U32]{}
    value := U32{0}
    loop _i in 0..<257 {
        values.push(value)
        value += U32{1}
    }
    xs :: compute.from_list(values) ?? panic("{err}")
    out :: compute.launch(affine, inputs: (xs,)) ?? panic("{err}")
    print(compute.to_list(out)) // Intended257 values: first1, last769.
}
```

## Pre-ratification performance gate: option A is blocked

The canonical matched candidate/plain programs and a strict measured win are both missing. This is a pre-ratification blocker for option A, not an optional implementation benchmark. The author recommendation remains unchanged and conditional; it is not readiness or owner approval.

A ranked coord/view program versus complete B flatten/return/reshape program. Both contiguous and non-contiguous windows are required; count all actual materialization and transfers while preserving identical values, shape and errors.

For each required matched metric and cell, divide the candidate surface cost by the plain cost. The result must be strictly below 1. Equality, missing, wrong, mismatched or inconclusive evidence fails. The Rust peer parity band is not a candidate/plain win. Target identity and measurement boundaries must be explicit.

Source counts, NOT RUN programs, frozen e841 snapshot receipts and reader approval cannot satisfy this gate. No canonical pair ID or evidence record exists for this choice. The other option remains a real choice, but cannot approve this gated API or bypass its independently named prerequisites.

Explicit source-work, memory or hardware-reuse advantage in the complete source alternatives.

## Beginner repair: coordinates and a layout that really copies

The current job keeps shape `[2,3]`: two rows with three columns each. `coord(0)` selects the zero-based row and `coord(1)` the column. Brackets `[row,column]` use that pair together. `at.linear` instead counts positions 0 through 5 in row order. The remainder `%3` gives a column. Exchanging the two rows changes `[1,2,3,4,5,6]` into `[4,5,6,1,2,3]`; it is not a transpose.

A stride is how many stored elements to step when one coordinate increases by one. For a concrete different layout, begin with backing values `[1,4,2,5,3,6]` in a table of shape `[3,2]`. Its strides are `[2,1]`. Transpose swaps the dimensions and strides, yielding shape `[2,3]` and strides `[1,2]` over the same backing. Reading its rows gives `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]`, the same logical input as the teaching job.

That transposed view reads stored positions 0,2,4,1,3,5 in logical row order. These steps are 2,2,−3,2,2, not one constant forward stride. It is non-contiguous in that logical order. A retains the shape and strides: reading source row1 gives stored positions 1,3,5 and values 4,5,6. It does not need a preliminary copy merely to express that view.

The captured `reshape(transposed,[6])` branch instead materializes logical order: it creates new storage containing `[1,2,3,4,5,6]`. Materialize means copy those logical values into that new order, not relabel the existing six positions. The shown B row-exchange then produces `[4,5,6,1,2,3]` and restores shape `[2,3]`. A representable projection keeps one mapping from coordinates to existing storage; pretending this irregular logical sequence is one flat constant-stride view is not such a mapping.

This is a source-derived example, not an executed workload. Compute.rs:6941–6971 swaps dimensions and strides while sharing backing;6496–6540 copies when reshape sees non-contiguous source strides. The captured source hash is acd0a789f7ba159d3d360d506d739a619860512696980ec065b0d1703d7686ed. Its materializer uses `Vec<f64>`; it is not physical-F32 GPU proof. Strides in this explanation count elements, not bytes.

The copying loss is conditional, not a claim that every plain program must copy. If the caller retains the original contiguous backing and knows this mapping, a different plain indexed kernel can read stored positions 1,3,5,0,2,4 directly. That avoids this preliminary reshape. A fair comparison must consider such a viable plain route when its inputs and ownership contract match; it must not make B artificially worse. The proposal itself still has no measured win.

The required performance comparison includes both contiguous and non-contiguous windows, all materialization and transfers, and identical values, shape and errors. A contiguous-only demonstration cannot satisfy this gate. Do not count a view descriptor as a data copy, or omit a real materialization from measured costs.

## CUDA notation used by the comparison

These CUDA adaptations are source illustrations, not executed programs or Jet approval. `__global__` marks a launch entry; `__device__` marks a device-callable helper. `const float*` is a pointer to input floating-point values that this function may not modify. A writable output pointer exposes storage without Jet's checked view proof. `threadIdx.x` is a worker's local position; `blockIdx.x` numbers its group and `blockDim.x` is that group's size.

The expression blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x gives a global position for these one-dimensional launches. `<<<blocks,threads>>>` supplies the group count and group size. A guard excludes positions outside the logical input. The surface's comparison note explains the operation specific to this ballot. These meanings let the small examples be traced; they do not turn CUDA's contracts into evidence for Jet's proposed guarantees.

## Unchanged evidence and prerequisite boundary

Every independently named prerequisite remains a separate owner choice. A snippet showing a prerequisite's A spelling does not ratify that spelling. No reader observation, source calculation or source excerpt is execution proof. Existing frozen receipts keep their snapshot-only scope; the frozen executable is not source-equated to the current tree. This repair changes documentation only. The complete programs, exact API alternatives and inherited failure and ownership rules below remain author drafts.

A extends the existing Invocation with `coord(axis:Int) Int`. The method returns the zero-based coordinate on that logical grid axis. Its axis must be in range, proved from source or a validated grid-rank precondition. It does not allocate a coordinate list. Logical dimensions use existing row-major ordering: the final axis changes fastest. The provider may use different physical blocks only while preserving these facts.

A admits existing View<F32> indexing for any positive rank represented by the source access. `xs[row,col]` is the existing one-bracket, one-index-per-axis rule. A scalar index drops an axis and a range keeps it. Existing whole-axis and range rules remain unchanged. There is no chained-bracket replacement, new kernel matrix type or alternate copy marker.

Scalar tensor resources use the existing scalar-input domain or an explicit one-place projection; this choice adds no zero-index bracket grammar.

A return-form launch uses the full logical grid shape for its output. A write-view kernel may use the separately approved indexed output contract with the existing ranked output places. Resource ranks and dimensions need not match the output; the compiler proves the actual access relationships. Launch validates shape, offset, stride, byte bounds and representable indices before submission. A non-contiguous resource remains a genuine strided view.

It is never relabeled contiguous or copied merely to pass a kernel admission check.

B leaves authored resources one-dimensional. The caller uses existing reshape to make the chosen flat representation explicit and restores the output shape afterward. The row-major six-value fixture can share its existing backing. Captured reshape source materializes a non-contiguous input, so B does not promise that every flattening is free. That source observation is not runtime proof of copy behavior. Applications requiring no-copy must retain a representable projection or refuse the conversion.

The worked job exchanges two rows, not a transpose. A reads row one when output row is zero, and vice versa. B rotates the six flat positions by three. Both return rows [4,5,6] and [1,2,3]. A's resource keeps its two-dimensional shape; B spells the width and flattened extent directly. Neither is intrinsically faster. The performance cell must compare both the contiguous case and a non-contiguous window, with all explicit materialization counted.

An out-of-range coord axis fails source proof or the grid-rank precondition. An invalid resource row similarly fails bounds proof or its shape precondition. Repair the coordinate or supply the required dimensions; do not clamp the address. Empty dimensions produce no invocations and no claimed GPU work. Shape-product overflow fails before allocating or dispatching.

D-MATRIX-INDEX1=E and D-MATRIX-HOME1=D remain ratified. Fixed-size Matrix/Vec arithmetic stays where it is. This only admits existing ranked Tensor/View meaning in a checked kernel. Core source owns coordinate and view rules; device adapters consume the checked metadata.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

F32Strict preserves 32-bit source operations and their required rounding. Reproducible preserves the declared operation order and result policy. No hidden F64 staging, TF32/FP16 conversion, reassociation, contraction, or floating atomic sum may change that meaning. A specifically declared alternative numeric mode is a separate existing control; these examples do not select one. An unsupported provider rejects instead of changing the result policy.

A successful launch returns a completed Tensor, never a pending token. Inputs remain borrowed until completion. A moved preallocated output returns with the same semantic storage on success; permitted physical transfers remain disclosed. Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

Prerequisites. D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 provides Invocation and resource binding. D-MATRIX-INDEX1=E and D-MATRIX-HOME1=D are preserved. Typed construction follows D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1. Where shown, typed F32 from_list uses the recommended but unratified A of D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1. If that independent decision selects B, those same calls use from_list_f32; numeric and ownership meaning stay identical. No constructor spelling is ratified by this draft. Every new spelling is a proposal.

Required independent choices are not silently approved by appearing in another example.

Complete fixture context. This is explanatory evidence/proposal metadata, not an added public schema.

```json
  "status": "NOT_RUN",
  "input_shape": [
    2,
    3
  ],
  "input": [
    1,
    2,
    3,
    4,
```

```jet
    xs :: [F32]{1,2,3,4,5,6}
    out := [F32]{}
    loop i in 0..<6 -> out.push(xs[(i + 3) % 6])
    print(out) // Intended rows: [4,5,6] then [1,2,3].
}
```

Complete proposed A program. Not executed or ratified.

```jet

#Kernel(.parallel)
fn swap_rows(at: compute.Invocation, xs: View<F32>) F32 ->
    xs[1 - at.coord(0), at.coord(1)]
fn run() {
    values :: compute.from_list([F32]{1,2,3,4,5,6}) ?? panic("{err}")
    xs :: compute.reshape(values, [2,3]) ?? panic("{err}")
    out :: compute.launch(swap_rows, resources: (xs,), grid: [2,3]) ?? panic("{err}")
    print(compute.to_list(out)) // Intended: [4,5,6,1,2,3].
}
```

```jet
use core.compute as compute
#Kernel(.parallel)
fn swap_rows(at: compute.Invocation, xs: View<F32>) F32 ->
    xs[(at.linear + 3) % 6]
fn run() {
    values :: compute.from_list([F32]{1,2,3,4,5,6}) ?? panic("{err}")
    xs :: compute.reshape(values, [2,3]) ?? panic("{err}")
    flat :: compute.reshape(xs, [6]) ?? panic("{err}")
    values_out :: compute.launch(swap_rows, resources: (flat,), grid: [6]) ?? panic("{err}")
    out :: compute.reshape(values_out, [2,3]) ?? panic("{err}")
    print(compute.to_list(out)) // Intended: [4,5,6,1,2,3].
}
```

decisions.title: How should a kernel reuse an ordinary helper?
decisions.gist: Should device eligibility follow the kernel call or require a helper marker?
decisions.lesson: A helper is reusable calculation. A’s compiler checks it while checking a kernel that may call it. B checks marked declarations even without a GPU caller. Both perform four rounds of double-plus-one. `inputs:(xs,)` supplies one scalar input per list position; results keep that order. These authored GPU programs are NOT RUN; both still owe the same safe behavior.
decisions.story: Lea uses one four-round gain function in CPU tools and image kernels. She wants the same calculation without copied helper bodies.
decisions.detail:
## The library-author difference is checking time

Both alternatives reject forbidden device printing, allocation and other effects. That common rule is not A's disadvantage. Under A, a library author cannot obtain an independently checked device promise until a kernel needs the helper. Under B, the marked declaration can fail earlier, even with no GPU caller. A therefore avoids repeated markers while B offers earlier eligibility feedback. This is a diagnostic-timing choice, not a speed claim.

## Beginner repair: scalar inputs and declaration checking

A helper is an ordinary function called by another function. Under A, checking a kernel also checks every helper body that the kernel may reach. Under B, `#Kernel(.helper)` checks the marked declaration even when no GPU caller exists. It is a promise about allowed device behavior, not a launch entry. A printing helper used only by CPU code can remain ordinary under A; leaving B's marker on it produces a declaration error.

`inputs:(xs,)` is a one-item input group; the trailing comma does not add an empty second input. For this scalar-return kernel, launch infers one invocation per element of xs. The invocation for position i receives xs[i] as scalar x, calls `transform(x)`, and puts its return value at output position i. The fresh output therefore has the same shape and order as this input. This explains the omitted grid; it is not one call receiving the whole list.

With `[1,2]`, two runs return 31 and 47. Adding input 3 creates a third run:3 becomes 7, then15, then31, then63. The intended output is `[31,47,63]`, not a reordered list or a single aggregate. Multiple scalar input tensors, when used, must satisfy the inherited exact matching-shape rule. There is no hidden broadcasting in this explanation.

`0..<4` visits 0,1,2,3 and excludes4. The compiler, not the author, proves this loop's finite bound for device admission. Changing the bound to 3 performs one fewer double-plus-one step and gives 15 and 23 for the original two inputs. Both markers still reject forbidden device behavior; a final host print after completed launch is not a print inside the helper. All these GPU examples remain NOT RUN.

decisions.gist: Should approved GPU compilers ship as optional components or in the stock toolchain?

decisions.detail:
This is one distribution policy choice, not an adoption of a named external dependency. The illustrative input is an offline machine, a checked F32 gather program and a provider whose already-approved compiler component is needed. The component identity would come from that provider's real approved manifest. The schema is explanatory data only. It introduces no command, package name, manifest field, hash or API. No component approval or installation is claimed to exist from this example.

A keeps ordinary Core source, semantic checking and the device-independent interface in stock Jet. A physical provider compiler that is actually required is acquired explicitly through the existing Jetpack-governed path. A fresh offline installation lacking that approved component returns an actionable missing-component error. It does not download files, accept terms, grant permissions or fall back to CPU. Once the component is present, the same checked program may compile; successful compilation still needs its own receipt.

B includes the selected, separately approved compiler closure in the pinned stock toolchain. The same offline machine therefore has that component. Drivers and browser hardware access remain platform responsibilities. An unsupported driver, device or kernel is still an error. Bundling is not evidence of successful execution. Only approved identities may enter the bundle; this decision does not authorize a license or version by implication.

Both preserve D-CORE-SOURCE-AUTHORITY1. Core source defines meaning, the pinned toolchain carries the required semantic source and metadata, and caches include source/toolchain/target identity. Optional physical compilers cannot become the semantic authority. Reachable-only emission and existing fetch/lock/audit rules remain. A provider that needs no extra compiler component incurs no installation step under A.

Current evidence establishes peer toolchain separation and the frozen frontend failure, not the installed Jet compiler-component set. Rust-CUDA separates its pinned Rust compiler and CUDA Toolkit requirements. Rust-gpu, CubeCL and NVIDIA's recent projects have their own captured version and feature requirements. Their popularity or dependency structure is not proof that Jet needs to adopt any of them.

The policy example assumes the independent F32 construction/indexed-kernel work is implemented and approved. Otherwise the existing source-proof failure occurs before this distribution question matters. The policy is complete without inventing a future package name. A future external compiler adoption remains a distinct dependency decision with exact version, artifact identity, license, target closure and offline behavior.

Before publication, reconcile this scope with existing Jetpack and provider cards. Before any component adoption, inventory which selected provider actually requires it. Measure fresh/offline install size, cache behavior, missing-component diagnostics and a real compile. A complete install does not count as a GPU workload result.

Reading key. `use core.compute as compute` gives the compute library a short name. `fn` defines a function. A colon introduces a parameter type. The type after the parameter list is the result type. `->` introduces a one-expression body; braces group statements. `return` gives the caller a result. `::` binds a name that is not reassigned; `:=` binds a variable. `=` stores a new value. `+=` adds and stores. `loop i in 0..<n` repeats for positions zero through n minus one.

`xs[i]` reads position i, so a list of length two has positions zero and one. A comma-separated bracket selects one coordinate per dimension. `if condition -> statement` executes that statement only when the condition holds. `%` gives the remainder. `wrapping(expression)` explicitly permits fixed-width integer wraparound. `F32` is a 32-bit floating-point number; `U32` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Int` is Jet's ordinary exact integer. `[F32]{3,5}` is a list containing two F32 values.

A Tensor owns an array and its dimensions. A View borrows existing values; ViewMut is a writable loan. `#Kernel(.parallel)` marks an authored function whose runs may execute together. The launch supplies Invocation, the read-only facts for one run. Safe code cannot construct or edit those facts. `at.linear` is this run's zero-based position. `at.extent` is the number of logical runs. `resources: (xs,)` supplies one borrowed tensor resource. The trailing comma makes a one-item tuple.

`grid: [2]` requests two logical runs, not two hardware blocks. `output: ^buffer` moves an output owner into the call. `?? panic("{err}")` takes the successful result, or stops and shows the actual error. It is an example stop policy, not an automatic retry. `print` displays the value. All proposed programs and their intended results remain unexecuted.

Inherited launch constraints. The following applies to compute.launch, not to the ordinary default placement of tensor construction.

Preserved safety and execution contract. The compiler checks seven named matters: sendability, bounds, aliasing, captures, races, barriers, and control flow. Sendability means values can cross the worker boundary. Bounds mean every access names existing storage. Aliasing checks which names reach the same bytes. Captures must not bring unproved host state into device work. Race checks prevent conflicting simultaneous access. Barrier checks require every participant to reach the same meeting point. Control checks reject paths whose required execution cannot be proved.

These are required checks, not a claim that the current implementation proves the new examples. Naming seven matters does not require seven new fields or another checker.

The compiler proves relationships from source. The launch checks the actual shapes, lengths, offsets, strides, device capabilities and stream ownership required by those relationships. A failed source proof rejects before lowering. A failed runtime precondition returns the existing compute error before submission. Proposed diagnostic text below is illustrative wording, not a newly registered error code.

Omitting device, or choosing compute.device_auto(), requests a compatible real GPU. compute.device_cpu() explicitly chooses the reference path. compute.device_vulkan() explicitly requests Vulkan. No compatible device or capability returns an error. Neither a CPU substitute nor a requested-device label counts as GPU execution. Existing placement() and device() reports must describe actual work.

Moving output consumes the caller's owner even when validation or execution fails. The error does not return a partly written Tensor or restore that old name. The runtime retains submitted resource lifetimes until completion or safe device teardown. Retrying needs a new output allocation.

Device loss can also invalidate other storage on that device; recreate required inputs from retained host data or another valid owner. This is not transactional rollback of GPU bytes.

Only audited provider adapters may use the existing typed raw #Unsafe boundary. Unsafe foreign code is outside the compiler's safety theorem. A safe caller cannot obtain raw access by choosing a different launch option. Core source defines the operation meaning; provider adapters consume the shared checked program and its facts. No second GPU language checker, owner family, or launch engine is authorized.

decisions.title: Load rooted configuration layers explicitly
decisions.gist: Should stock Core load an explicitly requested rooted configuration graph?
decisions.lesson: File-backed configuration can remove repeated loading, merging and provenance code. Its IO must be visible in the loader call, never activated by ordinary decode. A hostname is a caller-selected input, not hidden ambient policy.
