decisions.title: How CI and Nix obtain the native Jet seed compiler
decisions.situation: After the cutover, only an existing jet program can build or check Jet, so automated checks and the Nix package need a trusted starting copy, called a seed. None is published yet, and the full compiler check uses about 15 GB of memory on a 16 GB runner. You choose where the seed comes from and where the check runs. We recommend publishing the compiler that has already proven it rebuilds itself as the seed, then checking every pull request on the free runner with extra swap.
decisions.gist: Where do CI and Nix get the native seed, and where does the compiler check run?
decisions.lesson: A seed is a previous jet program used to check or build the next one, pinned by its hash. A publishes it at the cutover and checks on the free runner with swap. B uses a larger paid runner. C runs no hosted compiler check yet.
decisions.explainer: The cutover lands only after the native compiler builds itself twice and both copies match. That proven copy is the natural seed, so the seed exists the moment the cutover can land. The free GitHub runner for public repositories has 16 GB of memory. Adding swap space on its spare disk turns a near miss into, at worst, a slightly slower run.
decisions.story: Ana opens a pull request after the cutover. She needs the hosted check to tell her, before review, whether her change breaks the compiler.
decisions.inWild:
# Go bootstraps from a pinned previous Go release downloaded by hash.
# https://go.dev/doc/install/source#bootstrapFromBinaryRelease
GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP=$HOME/go1.22.6 ./make.bash
# Zig builds from a pinned zig1.wasm seed committed to the repository.
# https://github.com/ziglang/zig/tree/master/stage1
decisions.detail:
Revised 2026-10-10 because the owner did not ratify the posted A. The posted A deferred the hosted check because no seed existed, which left pull requests with no hosted compiler check. That premise was avoidable. Card #4956 lands the cutover only after the native stage1 == stage2 fixed point. The stage2 binary from that proof is a proven seed and exists at landing time. The new A publishes it as soon as that proof exists, so nothing waits, even while the remaining native ports finish.

Current state on cutover-prep. ci.yml runs the coverage ratchet, then requires vars.JET_SEED_URL and vars.JET_SEED_SHA256. It downloads the seed, checks its SHA-256, and runs Tools/agent/lane-check.sh in nix develop with JET_CHECK_MEM=off. Neither variable is set and the repository has no releases (gh variable list and gh release list, 2026-10-10). The repository is public. flake.nix no longer has packages.jet.

Memory. lane-check.sh records the whole-compiler check at a measured 15.4 GB peak; local runs cap it at 20 GB. GitHub's standard Linux runner for public repositories has 4 CPUs and 16 GB of memory, free and unmetered. The operating system needs some of that memory, so the peak can exceed free memory by roughly a gigabyte. A swap file on the runner's temporary disk absorbs that overflow instead of killing the job. Projects that build LLVM or rustc on hosted runners use the same step.

Cost shared by A and B. A seed must understand the compiler source it checks. When the compiler starts using a language feature the pinned seed lacks, the same change publishes a new seed from a locally proven fixed point and bumps the pinned hash. Zig refreshes zig1.wasm on the same rule, and Go requires a minimum bootstrap release.

Trust in the seed rests on the fixed point and the pinned hash. The rust branch at the pre-cutover head keeps a source-only path to rebuild a seed, as Go 1.4's C compiler did.

Option C keeps the hosted check off until someone publishes a seed, so pull requests rely on local lane-check and verify-full only.

options.name: Publish the proven compiler as the seed at cutover; check on the free runner with swap
options.detail: When the cutover lands, publish its fixed-point jet binary as a GitHub release asset and pin its URL and SHA-256 in repository variables. Hosted CI downloads it by hash and runs the whole-compiler check on the free standard runner. A swap step gives the check memory headroom. Nix fetches the same pinned asset.
options.technical: Cutover runbook: gh release create seed-<rev> with the stage2 jet, then set JET_SEED_URL and JET_SEED_SHA256. ci.yml adds a swap-file step before lane-check and logs peak memory. flake.nix adds the seed via fetchurl with the same hash.
options.code:
fallocate -l 16G /mnt/swapfile && mkswap /mnt/swapfile && swapon /mnt/swapfile
curl -fsSL "$JET_SEED_URL" -o jet && sha256sum -c seed.sha256
Tools/agent/lane-check.sh

options.name: Same seed on a larger paid runner
options.detail: Publish the same pinned seed, but run the check on a larger hosted runner with 32 GB or more.
options.technical: runs-on a larger-runner label; billed per minute even for public repositories.
options.code: runs-on: ubuntu-latest-8-cores

options.name: Defer the hosted compiler check
options.detail: CI runs only the coverage ratchet until someone publishes a seed. The full check runs locally through lane-check and verify-full.
options.technical: ci.yml keeps the ratchet step; seed and lane-check steps are removed until a seed is published.
options.code: node Tools/agent/core-coverage-census.mjs --check

comparisons.note: Go builds from a pinned previous release and documents the minimum bootstrap version.
comparisons.code: GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP=$HOME/go1.22.6 ./make.bash

comparisons.note: Zig keeps a pinned seed and refreshes it when the compiler needs newer features.

recommendation.why: A gives every pull request a hosted compiler check from the first day after the cutover, at no cost. Its seed is the binary the cutover already proves.
gains: Every pull request gets a hosted compiler check from day one.
No runner bill.
CI and Nix use one seed, pinned by hash.

losses.loss: If the check needs more memory than the runner has, part of it runs from swap and takes longer.
losses.mitigation: Swap holds only the overflow above memory, about a gigabyte today, and CI logs peak memory so growth shows early.

whyNot.reason: B pays for a larger runner to avoid a small swap overflow that costs only minutes.
C leaves pull requests without a hosted compiler check, although the seed exists the moment the cutover lands.

recommendation.tradeoff: At worst a few minutes of swap on a free runner, instead of a paid runner or no hosted check.

decisions.checkInstructions: Check a seed release asset exists and that JET_SEED_URL and JET_SEED_SHA256 match it. Check ci.yml enables swap, verifies the seed by SHA-256, runs lane-check on the standard runner, and logs peak memory. Check flake.nix fetches the same hash, and that no CI step builds Jet with cargo.
